units.la: Ἐνθφαγῆ. בית פאגי: In Lexico iuris בית פאגי מקום תץ ירושלים id est Bethphage locus eius nominis extra Ierusalem. Græca pleraque exemplaria Ἐνθ-σφαγῆ, quomodo etiam scriptum legimus apud Iustinum Βηθςτρύφωνα, sed mendose. In eodem Lexico: חומת בית פאגי
units.tr: Ἐνθφαγῆ [Bethphage]. [בית פאגי]. In the Lexicon of the law, [בית פאגי] is a place in the district of Jerusalem, that is, Bethphage, a place of that name outside Jerusalem. Most Greek copies have Ἐνθ-σφαγῆ [Enth-sphagē], as we also read written in Justin's Βηθςτρύφωνα [Dialogue with Trypho], but erroneously. In the same Lexicon: [חומת בית פאגי]

units.la: exponitur, murus Ierusalem. Apud Syrum בית פאגא.
units.tr: is explained as "the wall of Jerusalem." In the Syriac, [בית פאגא].

units.la: CAP. XIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII.

units.la: Eli Eli Lama sabacthani. A. Vtrum Christus pendens in cruce Eli Eli dixerit, an Eloi, eloi? B. mos Græcus scribendi chirec manus
units.tr: Eli Eli lama sabacthani. A. Did Christ, hanging on the cross, say Eli Eli or Eloi, eloi? B. The Greek way of writing the chirek sign.

units.la: C. Decamets, eiusque sono antiquo. D. Sabacthani scribendum non Sabachthani. E. Hieronymus notatus, & alia pauca.
units.tr: C. The qamets and its ancient sound. D. That it should be written Sabacthani, not Sabachthani. E. Jerome is criticised, and a few other points.

units.la: M ATTH. 27, 46. Πεϱὶ δὲ τὴν ἐνάτην ὥϱαν ἀνεβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, λέγων· Ηλὶ ἠλὶ λαμὰ σαβαχθανί. τοῦτ' ἐστὶ· Θεέ μου θεέ μου ἱνατί με ἐγκατέλιπες; id est Deus mi, Deus mi, propter quid me deseruisti?
units.tr: Matt. 27:46. "About the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying: Ēli, ēli, lama sabachthani. That is: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" [Πεϱὶ δὲ τὴν ἐνάτην ὥϱαν ἀνεβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, λέγων· Ηλὶ ἠλὶ λαμὰ σαβαχθανί. τοῦτ' ἐστὶ· Θεέ μου θεέ μου ἱνατί με ἐγκατέλιπες;] That is: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

units.la: Marci 15, 34.
units.tr: Mark 15:34.

units.la: Ελωὶ Ελωὶ λαμμᾶ σαβαχθανὶ, ὅ ἐστι μεθερμηνευόμενον· Ο Θεός μου ὁ Θεός μου εἰς τί με ἐγκατέλιπες;
units.tr: "Eloi, eloi, lamma sabachthani, which being interpreted is: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" [Ελωὶ Ελωὶ λαμμᾶ σαβαχθανὶ, ὅ ἐστι μεθερμηνευόμενον· Ο Θεός μου ὁ Θεός μου εἰς τί με ἐγκατέλιπες;]

units.la: In verbis ecce Hebraicis varietas est. Nam pro Eli Eli, quod est apud Matthæum, Marcus habet Ελωὶ Ελωὶ. Si quæres vtro modo pronuntiarit Christus, respondeo ἐλωὶ magis Syriacum esse: tamen ἠλὶ ἠλὶ servat Ierosolymitana psal. 22, vbi Syriaca quam laudat in Introductione eius linguæ Theleus Ambrosius ex Albonensibus Comes אלהי אלהי id est Elohi Elohi. Non sum diuinus, tamen conjicio Christum dixisse potius Eli Eli, quod ad Eliæ nomen propius accedit: eo magis quia Eusebius citans Marci verba non Eloi legit, sed vtin Matthæo quædam exemplaria ηλεὶ ηλεὶ, ἀπoδιἰξ. lib. 10.
units.tr: There is variation in the Hebrew words themselves. For where Matthew has Eli Eli, Mark has Eloi Eloi. If you ask which form Christ pronounced, I answer that elōi is more Syriac; yet the Jerusalem version of Psalm 22 keeps ēli ēli, where the Syriac that Theleus Ambrosius, Count of Albano, cites in the introduction to his grammar of that language has אלהי אלהי, that is, Elohi Elohi. I am no oracle, but I conjecture that Christ said Eli Eli rather than Eloi, since this is closer to the name Elijah. The more so, because Eusebius, quoting Mark's words, read not Eloi but, as some copies of Matthew have, ēlei ēlei. Book 10 of the Demonstratio.

units.la: Eli Eli id est אלי אלי Hebraicum pariter & Syrum. Syri etiam אילי dicunt. vide supra capite 8, & psal. 22, 1.
units.tr: Eli Eli, that is אלי אלי, is equally Hebrew and Syriac. The Syrians also say אילי. See above, chapter 8, and Psalm 22:1.

units.la: ἠλὶ scriptura alia ἠλεὶ. vtraque rationem habet ex antiquitate. Nam antiqui Chirec maius, quale est in אלי exprimebant modò per ει modò per ιῶτα. De ιῶτα exempla habes apud Epiphanium in καναν quod Hebraicè scribitur, & apud Euangelistas ραββωνὶ: σα-βαχθανὶ, μελχισεδὲκ. De ει sunt, εἰμει apud Theodoritum, ωλιμελμ in Exaplis Isa 26: ελαλειμ, & quæ alia à nobis obseruata sunt in libro De pronuntiatione veterum. Igitur ἠλὶ & ἠλεὶ eadem sunt. Sic ραββὶ & ραββεὶ. sic χεουβεὶμ & χεουβὶμ, quæ Moschopul° differre ait, eo quòd χεουβεὶμ sit numeri singularis, χεουβὶμ verò numeri pluralis: imperitè, cùm vtrumque sit numeri multitudinis.
units.tr: Another reading is ēlei for ēli. Both have a basis in antiquity. For the ancients rendered the Hebrew chirek, as in אלי, sometimes by ει and sometimes by ιῶτα. For the ιῶτα you have examples in Epiphanius at Κανάν, which is written in Hebrew, and in the Evangelists, ραββωνί, σαβαχθανί, Μελχισεδέκ. For ει there are εἰμει in Theodoret, ωλιμελμ in the Hexapla at Isaiah 26, ελαλειμ, and other cases that I have noted in my book On the Pronunciation of the Ancients. Therefore ἠλὶ and ἠλεὶ are the same. So too ραββὶ and ραββεὶ, and χεουβεὶμ and χεουβὶμ, which Moschopulus says differ, because χεουβεὶμ is singular and χεουβὶμ plural. This is careless, since both are plural.

units.la: ἐλωὶ.id est אלהי pronuntiatione vetere vt ωδωμ אדם apud Iosephum: Atto אתה, & Lecho לך apud Hieronymum. habet enim mixtum sonum hæc vocalis inter a & o; sonatque proprie a obscurum.hodie Iacobitæ (Syrorum ea gens est) perpetuò efferunt per o, vocalem quam O dom vocant, quæ respondet Hebræorum camets.
units.tr: ἐλωὶ, that is אלהי, in the old pronunciation, as ωδωμ for אדם in Josephus, Atto for אתה, and Lecho for לך in Jerome. For this vowel has a mixed sound between a and o, and properly sounds like an obscure a. Today the Jacobites (a Syrian people) always pronounce it as o, the vowel they call O dom, which corresponds to the Hebrew qamets.

units.la: λαμα. Hic libri mirè variât. Quidâ λιμα. alij λεμα,id est לַמָא: pleriq̈s λαμμᾶ. Apud Dauidem est למה id est λαμᾶ aut λαμμα. In Ierosolymitana למנא id est λεμανᾶ. Chaldæorum לָמָּא ex sono antiquo scribi potest λαμα, Lat. vulg. Lamma.
units.tr: Lama. Here the books vary wildly. Some have lima, others lema, that is לַמָא; most have lamma. In David the word is למה, that is lama or lamma. In the Jerusalem version it is למנא, that is lemana. The Chaldean לָמָּא can, from its ancient sound, be written lama; the Latin Vulgate has Lamma.

units.la: Σαβαχθανι error à librarijs. scribendum σαβαχθανι שבקתני. Nam σαβαχθανι. id est שבכתני. sic antiqui distinguebant has literas. In Latina vetere Lamma Azabthani. lectio à patre Hieronymo. In lib. De nom. Hebraicis.
units.tr: Sabachthani is a copyists' error. It should be written sabachthani, שבקתני. For sabachthani, that is שבכתני, is how the ancients divided these letters. In the old Latin version it is Lamma Azabthani, a reading from the Father Jerome, in his book On Hebrew Names.

units.la: Eli Eli Lamma azabthani:
units.tr: Eli Eli Lamma azabthani:

units.la: Deus meus, Deus meus, quare derelinquisti me?
units.tr: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

units.la: Stenthachum [illegible, ~8 letters] Hieronymus [illegible, ~20 letters] Græcas. Ade [illegible, ~30 letters] cutlocutum Syriacè? Ex eius officina est Beelzebub & Belial in libris Latinis. Hebraica haud dubiè vox Azabthani, reponenda Syriaca σα- βαχθανι ex libris Græcis.
units.tr: [Passage largely illegible in the scan.] ... Jerome ... the Greek books ... Did he speak Syriac? From his workshop come Beelzebub and Belial in the Latin books. The Hebrew form is undoubtedly Azabthani; the Syriac σαβαχθανι should be restored from the Greek books.

units.la: Ἡ μου. alibi scriptum ὁ Θεός μου, vt in Euangelio secundū Marcum. In quibusdam exemplaribus ἠλὶ ἠλὶ absque pronomine; sed pronomen addendum ex libris melioribus, eo magis quam in Hebraicis est, nec caret emphasi. Apud Syrum pro אל אל videtur quoque reponendum אלי אלי ex interpretatione. alioqui אֵל Syriæ haud insolitum verbum.
units.tr: Ho mou: elsewhere it is written ho Theos mou, as in Mark's Gospel. In some copies it is ēli ēli without the pronoun; but the pronoun should be added from the better books, all the more because it is in the Hebrew and does not lack emphasis. In the Syriac, for אל אל it also seems that אלי אלי should be restored from the translation; otherwise אֵל is not an unusual verb in Syriac.

units.la: CAP. XIIII. De Mamona.
units.tr: Chapter 14. On Mammon.

units.la: A. Vnde nomen sortitû sit. E. Vera scriptura inuestigata. C. Quid Chaldeis. D. quid Pœnus significet? E. Mamona iniquitatis?
units.tr: A. Whence the name is derived. E. The true Scripture reading investigated. C. What it means for the Chaldeans. D. What the Punic word signifies. E. "Mammon of unrighteousness"?

units.la: IN hoc capite dicam de Mamona, eiúsque apud Chaldæos scriptura ac sensu. est enim vocabulum Chaldaicum siue Syriacum. Primum quæro μαμμωρᾶ scribendum an μαμμωρα? vtraque enim scriptura reperitur in libris Græcis. In Latinis ferè est Mammona, aut me animus fallit, aut rectè diuino ממון ab יסן argumento firmitudinis iuxta prouerbium, [?] quemadmodum Hebraicè opes vocantur חָזָק robore. Si hoc rectè, scribi quidem potest μαμμωνᾶ videlicet מממונא,ac defendi exemplo מליף quod est ab אלף, de quo non contenderim: tamen malo μαμωνᾶ duabus de causis. primum quia reperio מָמוֹנָא sub Mem camets in omnibus libris Chaldaeorum: deinde quia me docuit Grammatica, fi prima radicis Aleph, magis esse vt quiescat, quàm vt indicetur per daghes. Igitur מָמוֹנָא more contrahendi in eo ordine vsitato pro מאמונא simile vt מְקָרָא pro מֵאמְרָא sermo ab אמר. Tantum de scriptura. venio ad sensum.
units.tr: In this chapter I will speak of Mammon, and of how it is written and understood among the Chaldeans. It is a Chaldean or Syriac word. First I ask whether it should be written μαμμωρᾶ or μαμμωρα, for both spellings are found in Greek books. In Latin books it is mostly "Mammona." Unless I am mistaken, it is rightly derived from the Hebrew ממון, from יסן, by the argument of firmness, following the proverb, just as the Hebrews call riches חָזָק, strength. If so, it can indeed be written μαμμωνᾶ, that is מממונא, and it can be defended by the example of מליף, which comes from אלף. I will not argue the point, but I prefer μαμωνᾶ, for two reasons. First, because I find מָמוֹנָא with a mem under qamets in all the books of the Chaldeans. Second, because grammar has taught me that when the first radical is aleph, it is more likely to be quiescent than to be marked by a dagesh. So מָמוֹנָא, by the usual manner of contraction in that class, stands for מאמונא, just as מְקָרָא stands for מֵאמְרָא, "word," from אמר. So much for the spelling. I come to the meaning.

units.la: Hieronymus Matth. 6 ,, Mammona sermone Syriaco diuitiæ nuncupantur.
units.tr: Jerome on Matthew 6: "Mammon, in the Syriac language, is called riches."

units.la: Suidas:
units.tr: Suidas:

units.la: μαμωνᾶς, χρυσός, ϑ̓ήσος πλούτος. diuitiæ id est עָשְׁרָא. χρυσὸς id est דָּהָב. In Chaldaeorum Targumin declaratio est τῶν ... quorum vnum lucrum significat, alterum opes, tertium exponit Dauid Grammaticus dicens eo nomine non solùm aurum & argentum, sed res omnes mobiles & pecora contineri. In lucro uenit vox Punica. Nam Pœni lucrum Mamon vocant. Augustinus sermone 35 De verbis Domini, & lib. 2 super sermone Domini in monte. Apud Iurisconsultos iudicia pecuniaria. multa pecuniaria. Lexicon Eliæ:
units.tr: μαμωνᾶς [mamōnas], gold, treasure, wealth [χρυσός, θησαυρός, πλοῦτος]. "Wealth," that is עָשְׁרָא ["osra"]. "Gold," that is דָּהָב ["dahav"]. In the Targum of the Chaldeans there is an explanation of ... of which one means gain, another riches; a third is explained by David the Grammarian, who says that the word contains not only gold and silver but all movable goods and livestock. The word is Punic in the sense of gain, for the Carthaginians call gain "mamon." Augustine, in Sermon 35 On the Words of the Lord, and in Book 2 on the Lord's Sermon on the Mount. Among the jurists, pecuniary judgments, fines. The Lexicon of Elias:

units.la: ממון בלא האבא בלעז רובא
units.tr: ממון [mamon] without the aleph [בלא האבא], in the vernacular [בלעז], roba [רובא].

units.la: Mamon Germanicè haue: Italicè Robba
units.tr: Mamon in German is "Habe"; in Italian, "Robba."

units.la: Mamona iniquitatis Luc. 16, 9. μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας, id est ita Syrus transtulit: aut Ionathan Hab. 2, 9: aut. idem Hos. 5, 11. sed hoc postremum proprie significat opes vanas ac fallaces. Porrò apud Euangelistam variè exponitur. mea sententia Mamona iniquitatis capiendum ex similitudine qua ibi vsus Seruator, qua de re dicam plenè alias.
units.tr: "Mammon of unrighteousness," Luke 16:9 [μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας]. That is how the Syriac translated it, or Jonathan on Habakkuk 2:9, or the same on Hosea 5:11. But the last of these properly signifies empty and deceitful riches. Moreover, in the Evangelist it is variously explained. In my opinion "mammon of unrighteousness" is to be taken from the comparison the Saviour uses there, about which I will speak fully elsewhere.

units.la: CAP. XV.
units.tr: CAP. XV.

units.la: DE MARIA.
units.tr: DE MARIA.

units.la: A. Scriptura vetus. B. mos Gracorum depravandi nomina barbara. C. Hieronymus notatus. D. Idem correctus. E. Mariam quid?
units.tr: A. Scripture old. B. The Greeks' custom of corrupting barbarian names. C. Jerome criticised. D. The same corrected. E. What is Mary?

units.la: HOc caput Mariæ sacratum erit: in cuius nomine explicando frustra fuit antiquitas, etiam Hieronymus doctissimus alioqui ac sanctissimus vir.
units.tr: This chapter will be devoted to Mary. Antiquity laboured in vain to explain her name, including Jerome, otherwise a most learned and most holy man.

units.la: Scriptura vetus μαεια aut μαειαμ. hæc terminatio Hebraica, illa Græca est. Vtraque reperitur in nouo Testamento. Apud Iosephum etiam μαειαμὴ de sorore Mosis. Ezechiel poëta tragicus: Μαειὰμ δὲ ἀδελφή μου χατὼ πτευτ πέλας. &, Μαειὰμ ἀδελφὴ ᾱεοτδ εαμοῦσα ζαοιλδ.
units.tr: In Scripture the old forms are μαεια [Maeia] or μαειαμ [Maeiam]. The latter ending is Hebrew, the former Greek. Both are found in the New Testament. In Josephus also we find μαειαμὴ [Maeiamē] for the sister of Moses. The tragic poet Ezekiel writes: "And Maeiam, my sister, χατὼ πτευτ πέλας [...]," and "Maeiam, sister of ... εαμοῦσα ζαοιλδ [...]."

units.la: In libris antiquis Hebræorum μειαμ, quod sine punctis scriptum מרים,media ætas μαειὰμ sonabat ex proprietate idiomatis Syriaci, quod mutat i in a: ex quo postea factum μαεία,an à Græcis, quibus in more deprauare barbara nomina? Sic ἀννιβας, ἀσδρυβας, Annibal, Asdrubal. nam apud eos nullum nomen definit in λ aut μ. an ex more breuiter scribendi מרי pro מרים? Nihil decerno. hoc tantum, quod non dubito affirmare. Nam cum Maria [illegible, ~12 letters] vox מר, nisi apud Græcos reperta, [illegible, ~10 letters]onymus in libro De nominibus Hebraicis ita scribens:
units.tr: In the old Hebrew books the name is written מירם or מרים without points, and in the Middle Ages it was pronounced Μαειὰμ, owing to the peculiarity of the Syriac idiom, which changes i into a. From this later came μαεία. Did the Greeks make this change, since they were accustomed to corrupt barbarian names? So ἀννιβας and ἀσδρυβας become Annibal and Asdrubal, for among the Greeks no name ends in λ or μ. Or did it come from the habit of briefly writing מרי for מרים? I decide nothing. This only I do not hesitate to affirm: since Maria [illegible] the word מר, unless it was found among the Greeks, [illegible] Jerome writes thus in his book On Hebrew Names:

units.la: „ Mariam plærique æstimant interpretari illuminant me isti, vel
units.tr: "Many suppose that Mary means 'illuminating me', or 'illuminator', or 'myrrh of the sea', but to me this does not seem so at all.

units.la: „ illuminatrix, vel smyrna maris, sed mihi nequaquam videtur.
units.tr: "It is better, however, to say that it means 'star of the sea', or

units.la: „ Melius autem est, vt dicamus eam sonare stellam maris, siue
units.tr: "'bitter sea'; and it must be known that in the Syriac language Mary is called 'Do-

units.la: „ amarum mare: sciendumque quòd Maria sermone Syro Do-
units.tr: amarum mare: and it must be known that Mary is called "Lady" (Domina) in the Syriac tongue.

units.la: „ mina nuncupatur.
units.tr: This is the Syriac word for "lady."

units.la: Quæ hîc dicit, refelli possunt ex scriptura Syriaca. Non enim <bl>מריא</bl> scribunt Syri, sed <bl>מרים</bl>. clarè liquet ex illius idiomatis testamento. Quod autem ait, Melius est vt dicamus eam sonare Stellam maris: recténe scriptum,an legendum, fel maris? nam <bl>מרא</bl> fel & amarum; stellam nunquam significat. Scripturam dixi, [illegible, ~8 letters] [illegible, ~2 letters]. vellem possem veram interpretationem dare, quæ non in vetere, non in nouo Testamento vsquam expressa. Si diuinandum sit, crediderim dictam quasi exaltatam à verbo <bl>רום</bl>,quod exaltare significat. Quid ni credam? Caninius ante me prolixè fidem fecit. Non sim homo, si verbum addam in re non maioris momenti.
units.tr: What he says here can be refuted from the Syriac Scriptures. The Syrians do not write מריא [Maria], but מרים [Mariam]. This is clear from the New Testament in that language. As for his statement, "It is better to say that it means star of the sea," is it written correctly, or should it be read "gall of the sea"? For מרא [mara] means gall and bitter; it never means star. I have said "Scripture..." [illegible, about 8 letters] [illegible, about 2 letters]. I wish I could give the true interpretation, which is not expressed anywhere in the Old or New Testament. If one must guess, I would believe the name was given as if from the verb רום [rum], which means to exalt. Why should I not believe it? Caninius before me made the case at length. I would not be a man if I added a word on a matter of no great importance.

units.la: CAP. XVI.
units.tr: CHAP. XVI.

units.la: A. Gehenna. B. Eusebius correctus. C. item Origenes. D. quid Hennom. E. Vocales non semper adscriptas fuisse. F. Gehenna, infernus, & cur? G. Gehennaignis quid sit, explicatum.
units.tr: A. Gehenna. B. Eusebius corrected. C. Origen likewise. D. What Hennom is. E. That vowels were not always written in. F. Gehenna, hell, and why. G. What the fire of Gehenna is, explained.

units.la: Γέεννα. Veritas scripturæ γεννα μ. ex Hebraeo γενομ, quod sonat Vallis Hennom. Nam veteres scilicet Hennom dixisse pro Hin-
units.tr: Γέεννα [Gehenna]. The truth of Scripture: γεννα, from the Hebrew γενομ [Gennom], which means the Valley of Hennom. For the ancients evidently said Hennom for Hin-

units.la: D nom. & nom. & est sane alterna migratio inter has vocales, ut id mirum videri nemini debeat. Eusebius an Hieronymus? de locis Hebraicis:
units.tr: nom, and there is indeed a free alternation between these vowels, so no one should find this strange. Eusebius or Jerome? On Hebrew places:

units.la: „ Geennom quod interpretatur, vallis Ennom, & ab hac quidam „ putant appellatam Geennam.
units.tr: "Geennom, which is interpreted 'the valley of Ennom', and from this some think Gehenna was so named."

units.la: Vulgo, Ennon & Geennon cum n, in fine, & literis Hebraicis à corrPectore Canonico ינם, sed perperam. Geennom id est γεεννομ. Nam Graeci aspiratione media praeterquam in ρ non utuntur, mansit postea spiritus lenis in Ennom ex hac causa. Origenes in 23 Matth.
units.tr: "Commonly Ennon and Geennon, with n at the end, and in Hebrew letters from the Canonical corrector ינם, but wrongly. Geennom, that is γεεννομ. For the Greeks do not use the middle aspirate except before ρ; afterwards the smooth breathing remained in Ennom for this reason. Origen on Matthew 23:"

units.la: „ Quae sit haec Gehenna, & in quo loco scripturarum prius est „ nominata, qui potest requirat, maxime in divisione haereditatis Iesu filij Naue; vbi interdum quidem appellatur Vallis filiae Non, interdum autem Vallis Ennom, quae est Gehenna. Gehenna enim est vallis.
units.tr: "Who can inquire what this Gehenna is, and in what place of the Scriptures it was first named, especially in the division of the inheritance of Joshua the son of Nun, where it is sometimes called the Valley of the son of Non, and sometimes the Valley of Ennom, which is Gehenna. For Gehenna is a valley."

units.la: C Verba haec adduxi Origenis bono. corrupta enim sunt, & legenda ad hunc modum:
units.tr: C. I have cited these words of Origen for their good. For they are corrupt, and should be read in this way:

units.la: „ - - - vbi interdum quidem appellatur vallis filij Ennom, interdum autem vallis Ennom, quae est Gehenna. Ge „ enim est vallis.
units.tr: "...where it is sometimes called the valley of the son of Ennom, and sometimes the valley of Ennom, which is Gehenna. For Gehenna is a valley."

units.la: Vallis filij Hennom appellatur Iof. 15, 18. Hebraice בן הנם ... Vallis Hennom, & interpretatione Graeca vetere φαράγξ ... ἴννομ, Hebraice בני הנם aut בן הנם Iof. 18, 16. Hic noto, quod habeo à Massoritis & ab Elia. Elias Tisbite בשלשה מקומות נמצא ... בן: Haec verba in eam partem valent non reperiri Gehennom, nisi ter ceteris in locis esse Ge ben Hennó. Notatu hoc in Masforeth magno. Loca sunt Iof. 15, 18, & 18, 16, & Nehem. 11, 30. Addit Elias dices se mirari cur hodie scribat בן הנם cum patach aut camets. Nihil mirum. Qui cum patach scribunt, male scribunt. Scriptura haec invaluit apud Iudaeos propter imperitiam antiquitatis. Verissime Chrysostomus:
units.tr: The valley of the son of Hennom is named at Joshua 15:18; in Hebrew בן הנם. The valley of Hennom, and in the old Greek version φαράγξ ... ἴννομ; in Hebrew בני הנם or בן הנם at Joshua 18:16. Here I note what I have from the Masoretes and from Elijah. Elijah the Tishbite: it is found in three places ... "son". These words mean that Gehennom is not found except three times, and in the other places it is written Ge ben Hennó. A notable point in the great Masorah. The passages are Joshua 15:18, 18:16, and Nehemiah 11:30. Elijah adds that he wonders why today people write בן הנם with patach or qamets. Nothing strange: those who write it with patach write it badly. This spelling has prevailed among the Jews through ignorance of antiquity. Most truly Chrysostom: "But the Jews do not know Jewish matters, whereas the Church knows the Christian and the Jewish teachings" [Ἀλλὰ Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν τὰ Ἰουδαϊκὰ οὐκ οἴδασιν, ἡ δὲ ἐκκλησία τὸν χειρῶν οἶδεν καὶ τὰ ἰουδαϊκὰ μαθήματα].

units.la: Ἀλλὰ Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν τὰ Ἰουδαϊκὰ οὐκ οἴδασιν, ἡ δὲ ἐκκλησία τὸν χειςῶν οἶ- δεν καὶ τὰ ἰουδαικὰ μαθήματα.
units.tr: Ἀλλὰ Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν τὰ Ἰουδαϊκὰ οὐκ οἴδασιν, ἡ δὲ ἐκκλησία τὸν χειςῶν οἶδεν καὶ τὰ ἰουδαικὰ μαθήματα.

units.la: Scribi debet בני הנם, id est Gehinnam aut Gehennam. Hiero. in comment. Ierem. 7.
units.tr: It ought to be written בני הנם, that is Gehinnam or Gehennam. Jerome on Jeremiah 7:

units.la: „ Tophet lingua Hebraea interpretatur latitudo: scriptumque fertur in libro Iosuae filij Nun, de hoc loco qui est in valle filij „ Ennom, & Hebraice dicitur Gehennam. Ge quippe φαράγγα, ,, idest vallé, & Hennam vel hominis nomen vel gratiam sonat. parcant mihi manes optimi viri: Hinná hominis nomen, non gratiam sonat. Eadem interpretatio in lib. De nominibus Hebraicis:
units.tr: "Tophet in the Hebrew language is interpreted 'breadth'; and it is said to be written in the book of Joshua the son of Nun, concerning this place which is in the valley of the son of Ennom, and in Hebrew it is called Gehennam. For Ge means 'valley' (φαράγγα), and Hennam means either a man's name or 'grace'." May the shades of that most excellent man spare me: Hinnom means a man's name, not grace. The same interpretation is in the book On Hebrew Names:

units.la: ,, Gehenna vallis gratuita:
units.tr: "Gehenna, the free valley:"

units.la: quasi nihil interfit inter הנם & חנם, hoc est inter he literā & het quae est aspiratio duplex. Idem Ierem. 19
units.tr: as if there were no difference between הנם and חנם, that is between the letter he and the letter het, which is a double aspiration. The same at Jeremiah 19:

units.la: ,, Vallis filij Hennom, quae Hebraicè dicitur Gehinnam. unde & ,, Gehennam appellatam putant.
units.tr: "The valley of the son of Hennom, which in Hebrew is called Gehinnam, whence they think it was called Gehennam."

units.la: Ex his & aliis locis apparet Hieronymum legisse semper גיהנם diale-cto Syriaca etiam in vetere Testamento. Nec miror, cùm sciam, Hebraicis olim literis, raras vocales adscriptas fuisse. Quod me docuit ipsemet Hieronymus in epistola quadam ad Euagrium diserte ita scribens:
units.tr: From these and other passages it appears that Jerome read גיהנם always in the Syriac dialect, even in the Old Testament. Nor am I surprised, since I know that formerly in Hebrew letters few vowels were written. Jerome himself taught me this, writing plainly in a certain letter to Evagrius:

units.la: ,, Nec refert vtrum Salem an Salim nominetur, cùm vocalibus in ,, medio literis perraro vtantur Hebraei, & pro voluntate lectorum, atque varietate regionum eadem verba diuersis sonis atq. ,, accentibus proferantur.
units.tr: "It makes no difference whether it is named Salem or Salim, since the Hebrews very rarely use vowels in the middle of words, and the same words are pronounced with different sounds and accents according to the will of readers and the variety of regions."

units.la: Nota quaeso lector, & define mirari, si tibi mira visa diuersitas scripturae in hac voce. Igitur גיהנם absque punctis vocalibus legebant Gehennó aut Gehennā: quod eo magis credo, quia nusquam adscripta vaf litera, quae solet legi per o: vel sanè quia familiare Syris vt holem mutent in camets. Quod autem apud Euangelistas ferè legitur γέεννα, corruptum est. abest μ similiter vt in μαεία. vide quae notauimus ad illud nomen. Dixi de scriptura, quae sciui, fortasse plura quàm debui: dicam nunc de sensu. sed breuiter, quia nihil habeo praeter alios interpretes.
units.tr: Note this, I beg you, reader, and stop wondering if the variety of spelling in this word seems strange to you. So they read גיהנם without vowel points as Gehennó or Gehennā; I believe this all the more because the letter vav, which is usually read as o, is nowhere written in it; or certainly because it is familiar to the Syrians to change holem into qamets. As for the fact that among the Evangelists it is commonly read γέεννα, that is corrupt; μ is missing, just as in μαεία. See what we have noted on that word. I have spoken of the spelling, as far as I know, perhaps more than I should; now I will speak of the meaning, but briefly, since I have nothing beyond what other interpreters say.

units.la: Gehennam vocat ὁ σωτὴρ locum damnatorum. Sic vsurpatur passim apud scriptores sacros. Suidas γέεννα, καταδ'ικη. Hieron. Matth. 10
units.tr: The Saviour calls the place of the damned Gehenna. Thus it is used throughout the sacred writers. Suidas: γέεννα, condemnation [καταδίκη]. Jerome on Matthew 10:

units.la: ,, Nomen Gehennae in veteribus libris non inuenitur, sed primū ,, à Saluatore ponitur.
units.tr: "The name Gehenna is not found in the old books, but is first put forward by the Saviour."

units.la: Dissentio hic à Hieronymo. Quid ni dissentiam? cùm reperiam in Auoth ניהנם pro inferno, & in Zoar libro antiquissimo,
units.tr: I dissent here from Jerome. Why should I not dissent, since I find ניהנם used for hell in the Auoth, and in the very ancient book Zohar,

units.la: לית ליה תשובה עד דיתרן כריגא רגיהנם
units.tr: "He has no repentance until he is cast down into the pit of Gehenna" [לית ליה תשובה עד דיתרן כריגא רגיהנם],

units.la: quae verba citantur in lib. Musar cap. 6, unde ego eruo. Non dubito, quin aetate Christi visitatissimum fuerit hoc significatu & notissimū in vulgus. Causam rectissimè idé Hieronymus notat his verbis:
units.tr: which words are cited in the book Musar, chapter 6, whence I draw them. I do not doubt that in Christ's time this meaning was most frequent and most widely known among the people. Jerome himself notes the cause rightly in these words:

units.la: Quaeramus ergo quae sit sermonis huius occasio. Idolum Baal fuisse iuxta Ierusalem ad radices montis Moria, in quibus Siloa fluit, non semel legimus. Haec vallis & parua campi planities, irrigua erat & numerosa, plenaque delitijs, lucúsque in ea idolo consecratus erat. In tantam autem dementiam populus Israël venerat: vt deserta templi vicinia, ibi hostias immolaret, & rigorem religionis delitiae vincerent: filiósque suos daemonijs incenderent vel initiarent. Et appellabatur locus ille Gehben Hennom (italeg. non Gehennom) id est vallis filij Hennom. Hoc Regum volumen & Paralipomenon & Ieremias scribunt plenissimè. Et comminatur Deus se locum illum impleturum cadaueribus mortuorū, vt nequaquā vocetur Topheth, & Baal, sed vocetur Polyandrium, id est tumulus mortuorum. Futura ergo supplicia & Poenae perpetuae, quibus peccatores cruciandi sunt, huius loci vocabulo denotantur.
units.tr: "Let us seek, then, what was the occasion of this saying. We have read more than once that the idol Baal stood near Jerusalem, at the foot of Mount Moriah, where the Siloam flows. This valley and small level plain was watered and fertile, full of delights, and a grove consecrated to the idol stood in it. The people of Israel had come to such madness that, deserting the neighbourhood of the temple, they sacrificed victims there, and their pleasures overcame the strictness of religion; they burned their sons in honour of demons or dedicated them to them. And that place was called Gehben Hennom (in italics, not Gehennom), that is, the valley of the son of Hennom. The book of Kings, Paralipomenon and Jeremiah write about this most fully. And God threatens that he will fill that place with the corpses of the dead, so that it shall by no means be called Topheth and Baal, but Polyandrium, that is, the tomb of the dead. The future punishments and the everlasting penalties with which sinners are to be tormented are therefore signified by the name of this place."

units.la: Si recte video, mendum est in illis verbis, vt nequaquam vocetur Topheth & Baal.
units.tr: If I see rightly, there is a fault in those words, "so that it shall by no means be called Topheth and Baal."

units.la: puto Hieronymum scripsisse Topheth & Gehen Hennom. à me est locus Prophetae, quem hic laudat. vide Ierem. 7, 32. Nusquam lectū Baal de loco. sed Βαάλ Iuppiter planeta alio nomine Moloch dictus q. Βασιλεύς, cui infantes immolabant in hac valle. Vide quae notamus ad vocem Moloch. Elias Tisbite: קראו רבורתיו לל מקום ענש הרשעים אחר מורתם גיהנם לפי שגי בן הנם חסמוך לירושלם היה מקום מקנף שטם שרפו את בניהם למלך:
units.tr: I think Jerome wrote "Topheth and Gehen Hennom." The prophet passage he cites here is mine; see Jeremiah 7:32. Baal is nowhere read of the place. But Baal is Jupiter the planet, otherwise called Moloch, which means King, to whom infants were sacrificed in this valley. See what we note at the word Moloch. Elijah the Tishbite: [קראו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה לל מקום ענש הרשעים אחר מותם גיהנם לפי שגי בן הנם שהוא סמוך לירושלם היה מקום מנוול שטמאו שרפו את בניהם למלך].

units.la: id est Vocauerunt Magistri nostri, quorum memoria fausta, locum poenae improborum post mortem Gehinnam, eo quòd vallis filij Hinnom, quae vicina vrbi Ierusalem, locus fuerit pollutus, in quo exurebant filios suos idolo Moloch.
units.tr: That is: "Our masters, of blessed memory, called the place of punishment of the wicked after death Gehinnam, because the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is near the city of Jerusalem, was a polluted place, where they burned their sons to the idol Moloch."

units.la: Dauid Cimhius in commentarijs ad Psal. 27 scribit in valle Hinnom loco prope Ierusalem olim perpetuum ignem fuisse comburendis cadaueribus & corporibus pollutis, quae illò proijciebantur. Dignum nota. quia ἀναμφισβήτως ad illum ignem allusit Seruator Matth. 5, 22, & alibi. Verba Cimhij: גיהנם הוא מקום באר שמוך לירושלם והוא מקום נמאם ומשליכים שם המתאות וחנכלות והיה שם אש תמיד להשרוף המתאות ועצמות לפיכך יקרא על שם ערך משל משפט הרשעים גיהנם: Igitur Gehenna ignis, id valet Ignis gehennæ, potius quàm Gehenna ignita, ex Hebraorum idiotismo, vt superbiæ viri, viri superbi: viriditas herbæ, herba viridis. sermo obuius passim.
units.tr: David Kimchi in his commentary on Psalm 27 writes that in the valley of Hinnom, a place near Jerusalem, there was of old a perpetual fire for burning carcasses and polluted bodies, which were thrown there. This is worth noting, because the Saviour without doubt alluded to that fire, Matthew 5:22, and elsewhere. Kimchi's words: [גיהנם הוא מקום באר שמוך לירושלם והוא מקום נמאס ומשליכים שם המתים והחנקים והיה שם אש תמיד לשרוף המתים ועצמות לפיכך יקרא על שם ערך משל משפט הרשעים גיהנם]. Therefore "Gehenna fire" means "the fire of Gehenna" rather than "burning Gehenna", after the Hebrew idiom, as "the pride of the man" for "the proud man", and "the greenness of the grass" for "the green grass". The expression is common everywhere.

units.la: CAP. XVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVII.

units.la: A. Gregorio Nysseno lux data. B. In Hieronymo restituta duobus locis scriptura vetus. C. Benereem. D. Targum emendatum. E. mos vetus scribendi γ pro y. F. Benereges. G. Causa scripturæ vocis Boanerges.
units.tr: A. Light given by Gregory of Nyssa. B. The old reading of Scripture restored in Jerome in two places. C. Benereem. D. Benereges. E. The old custom of writing γ for y. F. Benereges. G. The reason for the written form Boanerges.

units.la: GREGORIVS Nyssæ episcopus ὁ ἁ βροντῆς υἱὸς cùm ait λόγῳ εἰς τλω ὑπαπαντλῷ τὸ κυρίω significat Iohannem Euangelistam, quod intelligi potest ex eo quod legitur Mar. 3, 17.
units.tr: Gregory, bishop of Nyssa, when he calls John the Evangelist "the son of thunder" [ὁ υἱὸς βροντῆς], says it in his own words, and this can be understood from what is read in Mark 3:17.

units.la: ὡς ἐπωνόμασεν αὐτῖς ὀνόματα Βοανηργὲς, ὅ ἐστιν υἱοὶ βροντῆς.
units.tr: "And he gave them the names Boanerges, which is 'sons of thunder'" [ὡς ἐπωνόμασεν αὐτοῖς ὀνόματα Βοανηργές, ὅ ἐστιν υἱοὶ βροντῆς].

units.la: Quem locum adduxi propter vocem Boanerges, Vetus lectio Benereem. Hieron. in comment. Dan. 1 Filij Zebedæi appellati sunt filij tonitrui: quod non vt plerique putant Boanerges, sed emendatius legitur Benereem.
units.tr: I have cited this passage on account of the word Boanerges, the older reading being Benereem. Jerome, in his commentary on Daniel, chapter 1: "The sons of Zebedee were called sons of thunder," which, as most suppose, is not read as Boanerges but, more correctly, as Benereem.

units.la: Idem Isa. 62.
units.tr: The same, on Isa. 62.

units.la: Filij quoque Zebedæi, quorum vnus vocem tonitrui emittere poterat: In principio erat verbum, & verbum erat apud Deum, & Deus erat verbum, appellati sunt Benereem, quod interpretatur filij tonitrui.
units.tr: The sons of Zebedee also, one of whom could utter the voice of thunder ("In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word"), were called Benereem, which is interpreted "sons of thunder."

units.la: In his duobus locis reposuit nuperus corrector Beneraham. sed libri veteres Benerehem, & recte. In lib. De nom. Hebraicis:
units.tr: In these two places the recent corrector put Beneraham, but the old books have Benerehem, and rightly so. In the book On Hebrew Names:

units.la: Banereem filij tonitrui: quod corruptè Boanerges vsus obtinuit. Noli ambigere quin scribedum Benerec, vt supra. תונר tonitru. Vsus est hac voce Ionathâ interpres Chaldæus Isa. 29, 6; vbi סר scriptum imperitia eorum, qui puncta addiderunt. tu me auctore emenda ex analogia Danielis & Esdræ. antiquè ρμμ aut ρμς in quo duplex archaismus. primum γ loco y, vt in ραγουνλ, ἀμορρα & similibus exemplis: deinde ρμς pro ρμμ, quod fit ad hunc modum. Post abiectâ vltimâ μ, vt in μαςλα & γίννα, additur σῆμα more Græco. Ita solitum facere Græcis nominibus vocali definentibus. vide cap. 15. potest etiâ dici quòd μ mutata sit in σ ex more eo, quo Ἀννίβας dicebant pro Annibal, quem moré notamus in eodem capite. Hoc pono, non statuo. Pro Benereem interpolant alij, in queis Caninius, בני רגש Benereges.
units.tr: "Banereem, sons of thunder," which Boanerges, through corruption, came to prevail. Do not doubt that it should be written Benerec, as above. [תונר] means thunder. The Chaldee paraphrast Jonathan used this word at Isa. 29:6, where [סר] is written through the ignorance of those who added the vowel points. Emend it on my authority, from the analogy of Daniel and Ezra. Formerly it was [ρμμ] or [ρμς], which contains a double archaism. First, γ is used in place of y, as in [ραγουνλ], Amorrha and similar examples. Then [ρμς] is used for [ρμμ], and this happens as follows. After the final μ is dropped, as in [μαςλα] and Gynna, the ending σῆμα is added in the Greek manner. That is what they used to do with Greek names ending in a vowel; see chapter 15. It can also be said that μ was changed into σ in the manner by which they said Annibas for Annibal, a custom we noted in the same chapter. I set this out; I do not assert it. Others, in place of Benereem, put in Benereges, among whom is Caninius, [בני רגש].

units.la: D nereges. Ita Syrus, apud quem corruptè, רוש scriptum pro ריש.causa erroris, vt existimo, quia absque punctis erat רוש, vnde רוש transpositis literis. In declaratione reperio apud eundem בני רעמא. ergo עין vox Syra, & frustra est vir doctus, qui hoc negat. Ausim dicere magis probam vocem esse עין in hoc sensu, quàm רוש. Nam, vt verum fatear, ego בעל pro tonitru adhuc quæro. Non sic finiam caput.
units.tr: D. Benereges. So the Syriac has it, in which [רוש] is corruptly written for [ריש]. The cause of the error, as I think, is that without points it was [רוש], whence [רוש] arose by transposition of letters. In the explanation I find [בני רעמא] in the same source. Therefore [עין] is a Syriac word, and the learned man who denies it is wasting his effort. I would venture to say that [עין] in this sense is a more probable word than [רוש]. For, to tell the truth, I am still searching for [בעל] as the word for thunder. I will not end the chapter here.

units.la: Scire cupiet aliquis causam vulgatæ scripturæ Boanerges. vellem possem certam dicere; sed coniecturis agendum erit. Conijcio primum scriptum fuisse Banerges ex sono antiquo pro Benerges, vt Samuel pro Semuel. quomodo etiam defendi posset Banereem, quod est apud Hieronymum. Porrò Banerges Syriæ quædam dialectus dicit Bonerges, & alioqui a in o facilè migrat. Ex his dialectis conflatū Boanerges. Hæc sunt scripta sine certo sensu.
units.tr: Someone will want to know the reason for the common reading Boanerges. I wish I could give a certain answer, but I shall have to proceed by conjecture. I conjecture, first, that it was originally written Banerges, from an older pronunciation, for Benerges, as Samuel for Semuel. In the same way, Banereem, which is found in Jerome, could also be defended. Further, some dialect of Syria says Bonerges for Banerges, and in any case a changes easily into o. From these dialects Boanerges was compounded. These things are written without any certain meaning.

units.la: CAP. XVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII.

units.la: A. Hieronymo medicina facta semel atque iterum. B. Beliar ex dialecto Syriaca pro Belial. C. ea vox explicata. D. Isidori lapsus.
units.tr: A. Jerome's remedy applied once and again. B. Beliar, from the Syriac dialect, for Belial. C. That word explained. D. Isidore's slip.

units.la: VIDIMUS nuperrimè Hieronymum correctum à Mariano Victorio Reatino. sed Deus bone, quàm multa corrector ille non vidit, aut, si vidit, non correxit: credo, quia ea leuia duxit, nec digna, quæ subirent ipsius censuram. Hieronymus in comment. Ephef. 4.
units.tr: We have recently seen Jerome corrected by Marianus Victorius of Reate. But good God, how many things that corrector did not see, or, if he saw them, did not correct! I suppose he thought them trivial and not worthy of his censure. Jerome, on Ephesians 4, writes:

units.la: ,, Sciendum vbicumque in veteri lege filij pestilentiæ scribantur, ,, sicut ibi, ,, Filij autem Eli, filij pestilentiæ; ibi in Hebraicis voluminibus ,, Belial, hoc est diabolum, pro pestilentia nominari, licet plurimi ,, pro Belial corruptè in Apostolo Beliar legant.
units.tr: "It should be noted that wherever the sons of pestilence are mentioned in the Old Law, as there, 'Now the sons of Eli were sons of pestilence' (1 Sam. 2), there the Hebrew books use 'Belial,' that is, the devil, for pestilence. Although most people in the Apostle read the corrupt form 'Beliar' for Belial."

units.la: Ita restitui: libri vulgati . . . Belian. Simile mendum hæret in hac eadem voce libro De nom. Hebr. ex epist. ad Corinth. 2. ,, Beliar, cœca angustia, vel cœcum lumen, vel filius prœuaricatio,, nis, sed rectius Belial dicitur.
units.tr: I have restored it thus; the printed books have "Belian." The same error clings to this same word in his book On Hebrew Names, drawn from the second Epistle to the Corinthians: "Beliar: blind distress, or blind light, or son of prevarication." But it is more correctly called Belial.

units.la: libri omnes editi Beluir. quod miror episcopum illum non vidisse, qui in Erasmi erratulis tam vidit acutum. Glossæ veteres Belial, absq. iugo: Beliar cœcum lumen aut cœca angustia. locus est 2 Corinth. 6, 15, qui sic legitur in libris Græcis: τίς δὲ συμφώνησις χειστῷ πρὸς βελίαρ; & in Latinis veteribus:
units.tr: All the printed books have "Beluir." I am surprised that bishop did not notice it, since he noticed so keen a point in the minor errors of Erasmus. Old glosses: "Belial, without a yoke"; "Beliar, blind light or blind distress." The passage is 2 Corinthians 6:15, which reads in the Greek books: "What concord has Christ with Beliar?" [τίς δὲ συμφώνησις χριστῷ πρὸς βελίαρ;] and in the old Latin:

units.la: „ Quæ autem conuentio Christi ad Beliar? Visum Hieronymo hanc scripturam mendosam esse, itaque mutauit, Belial, quem secuti sunt pueri omnes interpretes. etiam in Græco βελίαλ repposuerunt homines audaces. Tantæ audaciæ non sim ego. potius dixerim βελίαρ esse pro βελίαλ scribendi ratione olim tralatitia ex proprietate linguæ Syriacæ, quæ mutat λ in ρ. & est alioqui facilis migratio inter has literas. Sicuti enim καλίβαρος dicimus & χρίβαρος: ita pro בליעל credibile est Syros vsitasse בליער, id est βελίαρ. Igitur Belial & Beliar idem sunt. hoc tantum differunt, quòd βελιαρ medij temporis vocabulum sit, & corruptum: Belial, vetus ac probum. est autem βελίαλ archaicòs pro βελιαλ ex more eo quo literam gutturatam in medio abscondunt: de quo more dictum est alias sæpe.
units.tr: "What agreement has Christ with Beliar?" Jerome judged this reading faulty and so changed it to "Belial," which all the later translators followed. Bold men have even put βελίαλ in the Greek. I will not be so bold. I would rather say that βελίαρ is, in the older manner of writing, a traditional form for βελίαλ, from the peculiarity of the Syriac language, which changes λ into ρ. Moreover the interchange between these letters is easy. Just as we say καλίβαρος and χρίβαρος, so it is credible that the Syrians used בליער, that is βελίαρ, for בליעל. So Belial and Beliar are the same. They differ only in this: βελιαρ is a later and corrupted word, while Belial is old and sound. Now βελίαλ is archaic for βελιαλ, in the manner in which a guttural letter is concealed in the middle, a practice I have often spoken of elsewhere.

units.la: Hebraicè בליעל vox haud rarenter vsurpata scriptoribus sacris. à Cimhio interpretatur רשע, id est improbus. Idem ἑτυμολογίζει belial בליעל id est ἄχρηστος, qui nec sibi nec aliis prodest, homo nequam. ante Cimhium sic exposuerunt hanc vocem interpretes iuris. disco ex Lexico iuris, in quo filij Belial בני יועיל. alia expositio Belial בלי עול absque iugo, exlex, tralatio à bubus nullo iugo domitis, qui Festo iniuges dicuntur. In Sanhedrin:
units.tr: In Hebrew, בליעל is a word not infrequently used by the sacred writers. Cimhi interprets it as רשע, that is, wicked. The same man derives belial, בליעל, as ἄχρηστος, one who profits neither himself nor others, a worthless man. Before Cimhi the interpreters of the law explained the word thus. I learn from the lexicon of the law, where we find "sons of Belial," בני יועיל. Another explanation is Belial, בלי עול, without a yoke, lawless, a figure taken from oxen that bear no yoke, which Festus calls iniuges. In Sanhedrin:

units.la: אנשי בני בליעל
units.tr: men, sons of Belial [אנשי בני בליעל]

units.la: glossa Talmudica in Gemara;
units.tr: A Talmudic gloss in the Gemara:

units.la: בְּנֵיּ שֶׁפָּרְקוּ עֹל שָׁמַיִם מִצַּוָּארָן
units.tr: Sons who broke the yoke of heaven from their necks [בְּנֵיּ שֶׁפָּרְקוּ עֹל שָׁמַיִם מִצַּוָּארָן]

units.la: id est filij qui fregerunt iugum cæli, & abiecerunt illud de collo suo.
units.tr: That is, sons who broke the yoke of heaven and cast it from their neck.

units.la: Hieronymus:
units.tr: Jerome:

units.la: „ Diabolus Græcum verbum est, quod Latinè dicitur criminator,
units.tr: "Diabolus is a Greek word, which in Latin is called the accuser (criminator).

units.la: „ lingua verò Hebræa Satan appellatur, id est aduersarius siue
units.tr: In the Hebrew tongue it is called Satan, that is adversary or opponent,

units.la: „ contrarius, & ab Apostolo Belial, id est absque iugo, quòd de collo suo Dei abiecerit seruitutem, què Aquila ἀπὸς ἀτλω transtulit.
units.tr: and by the Apostle Belial, that is, without a yoke, because he cast off from his neck the service of God; Aquila translated this as ἀπὸς ἀτλω."

units.la: Suidas:
units.tr: Suidas:

units.la: βελίαρ τῇ ἑβραίων φωνῇ ἀπὸς ἀτλω δηλοῖ. ὁ ἀπόστολος, τίς δὲ συμφώνησις χειστῷ πρὸς βελίαρ;
units.tr: "Beliar in the Hebrew language signifies 'without a yoke.' The Apostle: 'What concord has Christ with Beliar?'" [βελίαρ τῇ ἑβραίων φωνῇ ἀπὸς ἀτλω δηλοῖ. ὁ ἀπόστολος, τίς δὲ συμφώνησις χριστῷ πρὸς βελίαρ;]

units.la: In fragmentis veterum interpretum ad Psal. 41, 9:
units.tr: In the fragments of the old interpreters on Psalm 41:9:

units.la: דבר בליעל Symmachus λόγος παρανομος, id est sermo iniquus,
units.tr: "דבר בליעל" Symmachus: λόγος παρανομος, that is, an unjust word [λόγος παράνομος].

units.la: Deut. 13, בני בליעל id est filij Belial: LXX παςανόμους. Isidorus Belial absque iugo. Quod autem idem addit Belial Hebraicè Bel dici idolum Niniuitarum, erratum in nomine, transcripsit Belial pro Baal.
units.tr: Deuteronomy 13: "sons of Belial," that is, "sons of Belial"; the Seventy: παράνομοι [lawless]. Isidore: Belial, without a yoke. But his further remark that Belial is called in Hebrew Bel, the idol of the Ninevites, is an error in the name; he copied Belial for Baal.

units.la: CAP. XVIIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIIII.

units.la: A. Quid de Hosanna voce scripserit Elias. B. eius expositio vetus. C. & noua, quae à me. D. locus explicatus Matth. 21, 9. E. Hilarÿ commentum excusatum. F. Prauitas censura Hieronymiana. & alia multa.
units.tr: A. What Elias wrote about the word Hosanna. B. His old explanation. C. And the new one, which is mine. D. The passage explained, Matthew 21:9. E. Hilary's comment excused. F. The perversity of Jerome's censure, and many other things.

units.la: HOSANNA Hebraicam vocem interpretatur Elias, dicens sic appellari ramos salicum in festo tabernaculorum ab adiuncta ipsis acclamatione. Nam qui gestant eos ramos, acclamant idem Hosanna; quę acclamatio solemnis in illo festo. Elias Tisbite: הושענא אנרת ערבי נחל שנוטלין בהג הסכות קריין הושענות לפי שצועקים עליהם הושענא:
units.tr: Elias interprets the Hebrew word Hosanna, saying that the willow branches in the festival of tabernacles are so called from the acclamation attached to them. For those who carry those branches shout the same word, Hosanna, an acclamation solemn in that festival. Elias the Tishbite: "הושענא" [hoshana]: "The willow branches of the brook of Arabah, which are taken up in the festival of Sukkot, are called hoshanot, because they cry out 'hoshana' over them."

units.la: Idem scribit dictionem compositá esse ex הושיעה & נא, vt sit Hosanna, si interpreteris, serua obsecro, aut serua nunc, id est נא הושע. Amplius laudat ex interpretatione ea, quæ Ierosolymitana vocatur; quod legitur Esther 3 ad locum יָשָׁנוּ עִם אָחִיר. עכרין לחון הושענא
units.tr: He also writes that the word is compounded of הושיעה and נא, so that Hosanna, if you translate it, means "save, I beg you," or "save now," that is נא הושע. He further cites from the so-called Jerusalem interpretation, on Esther 3 at the passage "they make for themselves" (עכרין), "hosanna" (לחון הושענא).

units.la: id est faciunt sibi hosanna.
units.tr: That is, "they make for themselves hosanna."

units.la: item וחרין בהושענא
units.tr: Likewise "and they go round carrying hosanna" (וחרין בהושענא).

units.la: id est, & circumeunt gestantes hosanna. Hæc Elias: quibus addo videri sumptum hosanna ex Psal. 118, mutatione facta in הושיעה secundum proprietatem & vsum linguæ. nam & הושיעה dicimus & יושע, & contracte יושע, quæ forma Syris perfamiliaris est, ex quo הושענא, id est hosanna aut hosana vnica: ita enim scribendum; nisi dicamus prius ר esse loco ү, quam sæpe exprimunt per ү, quæ deinde mutata sit in ר sequente altero ר. Exponunt σῶσον δή. Eusebius ἀποδείξ· lib. 9.
units.tr: That is, they go around carrying hosanna. So far Elias. To this I add that hosanna seems to have been taken from Psalm 118, with a change made to הושיעה [hoshiah], according to the nature and usage of the language. For we say both הושיעה [hoshiah] and יושע [yoshia], and in contracted form יושע [yoshia], a form very familiar to the Syrians. From this comes הושענא [hoshana], that is, hosanna or hosana in a single word, and so it ought to be written, unless we say that the ר stands in place of ע [ayin], which they often express by y, and that this was then changed into ר when a following ר came after it. They explain it as σῶσον δή [sōson dē], save now. Eusebius, Demonstration [ἀποδείξεως], book 9.

units.la: ὡς ἀνὰ ἐρμίμενον ἐν δ' ἡλοῖ, σῶσον δή.
units.tr: Eusebius, Demonstratio, book 9: "As is said in the Hebrew, they cry 'Hosanna,' that is, σῶσον δή [save, I pray]."

units.la: Theophylactus Matth. κα.
units.tr: Theophylact on Matthew 21:

units.la: τὸ δὲ ὡς ἀνὰ, οἱ μὲν λέγουσιν ὅτι ὑμνον ἢ ψαλμὸν σημαίνει· οἱ δὲ, ὃ καὶ ἀκελείσεσθαι, σῶσον δή.
units.tr: As for the phrase ὡς ἀνά [hōs ana], some say it signifies a hymn or psalm; others say it is the same as "save, I pray" [σῶσον δή].

units.la: Vide fragmenta veterum interpretum ad versum 25 Psalmi 118. possct possset exponi, serua nos, aut salus nostra: in quo sensu nihil refert Hosanna scribas, an Osanna ϰυϱιον absque adspiratione, forma linguae Syrae, quam vernaculam fuisse in Iudaea aetate Christi extra controversiam est. porro in ea lingua ϰα pronomen est: pro quaeso aut nunc, non reperitur quod sciam. Nec obstat quod supra diximus, sumptum illud videri ex Psal. 118. Nam si forma mutauit a vulgo, quid ni potuit & sensus mutari? Quod dico firmamentum habet in eo quod legimus Matth. 21, 9
units.tr: See the fragments of the old interpreters on verse 25 of Psalm 118. It could be explained as "save us" or "our salvation." In that sense it makes no difference whether one writes Hosanna or Osanna, with the Lord [κύριον] written without aspiration, in the form of the Syriac language, which was beyond dispute the vernacular in Judea in the age of Christ. Moreover, in that language the particle ka [κα] is a pronoun, meaning "I beg" or "now"; as far as I know, nothing of the sort is found in it. Nor does what I said above, that the phrase seems to be taken from Psalm 118, stand in the way. For if the form changed in common use, why could the sense not have changed too? What I say has support in what we read at Matthew 21:9: "Hosanna to the Son of David" [Ωσαννα τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ].

units.la: Ωσαννα τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ.
units.tr: "Hosanna to the Son of David" [Ωσαννα τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ].

units.la: Nam si Hosana valet σῶσον δὴ, quid erit obsecro σῶσον δὴ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ? an non magis erit ex Hebraismo interpretari, tanquam si dictum esset ἡ σωτηρία ἡμῶν τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ? ut, Domino salus, Psal. 3, 9: cuius Hebraismi sensus est, Salus nostra a filio Dauid. Nam quem agnoscebant pro vero Messia, eum laudant tanquam salutis suae authorem. hoc mihi rectum videtur, tamen arbitrarium esto, nolo sit certum. Nolim etiam affirmare; quanquam adducor ut credam tale quid in mente habuisse Hilarium, aut si quis alius fuit, qui Hilarium docuit Hosanna significare quod Hieronymus tantopere exagitat. Na salus nostra, sententia valet, redemptio domus Dauid; tametsi verba multu diuersa sint. Hieronymus epistol. 145 scribes corrupte dici Osanna propter ignorantiam pro Osiana. Quorum ignorantiam? illegible an librariorum & scribarum? [illegible, ~20 letters] In iure Hebraeorum frequens ϰυϱιον, & apud Targumistas locis supra citatis: quae loca clare docent priscos usitasse hosanna, non hosianna. Idem Hieronymus ὡς ἀννά scribit, cum scribendum sit ὡσαννα aut ωσαννα. intelligo cum diuisim scribitur. In libro De nom. Hebraicis ex Matthaeo:
units.tr: For if hosanna means "save, I pray" [σῶσον δή], what, I ask, will "save, I pray, to the Son of David" [σῶσον δὴ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ] mean? Will it not rather be right to interpret it from Hebraism, as if it had been said "our salvation to the Son of David" [ἡ σωτηρία ἡμῶν τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ]? Compare "salvation to the Lord," Psalm 3:9, whose Hebraistic sense is "our salvation from the son of David." For they praised as the author of their salvation the one whom they acknowledged as the true Messiah. This seems right to me, but let it be a matter of opinion; I do not want it to be regarded as certain. Nor would I affirm it, although I am inclined to believe that Hilary had something of this kind in mind, or whoever it was that taught Hilary that hosanna means what Jerome so vigorously attacks. For "our salvation" has the same sense as "the redemption of the house of David," although the words are quite different. Jerome, in letter 145, writes that Osanna is wrongly said through ignorance for Hosiana. Whose ignorance? [illegible] The ignorance of copyists and scribes? [illegible, about 20 letters] In Jewish law "Lord" [κυριον] is frequent, and among the Targumists in the places cited above, which clearly show that the ancients used hosanna, not hosianna. The same Jerome writes ὡς ἀννά [hōs anna], when it should be written ὡσαννα or ωσαννα. I understand this when it is written as separate words. In the book On Hebrew Names, on Matthew:

units.la: „ Osanna saluifica, quod Graece dicitur ὡς ἀννά.
units.tr: Osanna, the saving cry, which in Greek is called hōs anna [ὡς ἀννά].

units.la: Quin vera haec scriptura sit, non ambiget quisquis leget epistolam supra citatam: in ea enim epistola ait Hieronymus:
units.tr: That this is the true reading, no one who reads the letter cited above will doubt, for in that letter Jerome says:

units.la: „ Hosi (vulgo hosiach) ergo saluifica interpretatur. Anna interiectio deprecantis est. Si ex duobus his velis compositum verbum facere, dices hosiana, siue, ut nos loquimur, hosanna, media „ vocali litera elisa, sicuti facere solemus in versibus Virgilij quando pro Mene incepto desistere victam, scandimus Men' incepto.
units.tr: "Hosi (commonly hosiach) therefore means 'save.' Anna is an interjection of one who prays. If you wish to make a single compound word from these two, you will say hosiana, or, as we say, hosanna, with the middle vowel elided, just as we usually do in Virgil's verses when we scan 'Mene incepto desistere victam' as 'Men' incepto.'"

units.la: E Aleph
units.tr: From Aleph

units.la: {D} [illegible, ~10 letters] Aleph namque litera prima verbi sequentis, extremam verbi prioris Iod inueniens, exclusit.
units.tr: {D} [illegible] For Aleph, the first letter of the following word, finding the final letter Yod of the preceding word, has shut it out.

units.la: Ex his verbis apparet Hieronymum legisse apud Dauidem [Hebrew] pro eo quod nunc legimus [Hebrew], hoc est Aleph pro He, litera aspirata Ajin elisa: de qua lectione & simul de loco illo Hieronymi dicam alias plenissime. Osanna aliqua Graecorum pars [Greek] interpretatur, in queis Clemens Alexandrinus & Suidas: sed vt recte Hieronymus obseruat, gloria Hebraice Cabod appellatur, non Osanna. Quod autem Suidas adfert pro confirmatione interpretationis suae,
units.tr: From these words it appears that Jerome read in David [Hebrew] where we now read [Hebrew], that is, Aleph for He, with the aspirate Ajin elided. I will speak fully about this reading, and at the same time about that passage of Jerome, on another occasion. Some part of the Greeks translates Osanna as [Greek], among them Clement of Alexandria and Suidas. But, as Jerome rightly observes, glory is called Cabod in Hebrew, not Osanna. As for what Suidas adduces in confirmation of his interpretation,

units.la: [Greek]
units.tr: [Greek]

units.la: tam ineptum est, vt refutatione nulla opus sit.
units.tr: It is so silly that no refutation is needed.

units.la: CAP. XX.
units.tr: CHAP. XX.

units.la: A. Rabbi, Ribbi & Rab. B. In Epiphanio vox correcta. C. Aquila & Rabaquiba. D. quando vixerit.
units.tr: A. Rabbi, Ribbi and Rab. B. The word corrected in Epiphanius. C. Aquila and Rabaquiba. D. When he lived.

units.la: RABBI. Graeci scribunt [Greek] aut [Greek], de qua scriptura dictum est supra cap. 13. vide quae obseruamus ad eum locum. In libro De nom. Hebraicis:
units.tr: RABBI. The Greeks write [Greek] or [Greek], which was discussed above in chapter 13. See what we note on that passage. In the book On Hebrew Names:

units.la: Rabbi, Magister meus, Syrum est: nescio an error in hac interpretatione. Nam Euangelista interpretatur [Greek] Ioh. 1, 38. contra Elias diserte affirmat Iod in Rabbi pronomen esse. Apud Syrum lego [Hebrew], id est Rabban. Hieronymus in commentariis super Matthaeum:
units.tr: Rabbi, "my master," is Syriac: I do not know whether there is an error in this interpretation. For the Evangelist translates it as [Greek] in John 1:38, whereas Elias clearly affirms that the Iod is a pronoun in Rabbi. In Syriac I read [Hebrew], that is, Rabban. Jerome in his commentary on Matthew:

units.la: Rabbi Latino sermone Magister dicitur.
units.tr: Rabbi is called Magister in Latin.

units.la: ecce discedit a se ipso: ego censerem Rabbi positum pro Ribbi vsitata vocalium mutatione. Amant enim Syri ponere a pro i: quod ita notum, vt exemplis probare nihil opus sit. alias discrimen ponebant veteres inter has voces. Nam Rab vsurpabant proprie de Magistris Babyloniae: Ribbi autem de Magistris terrae Israel. docco ex ipsorum verbis memoratis in Tisbite.
units.tr: Behold, he departs from himself. I would have thought that "Rabbi" was put for "Ribbi" by the usual change of vowels, since the Syrians love to put a for i. This is so well known that there is no need to prove it with examples. Otherwise the ancients did make a distinction between these words. They used "Rab" properly of the teachers of Babylon, but "Ribbi" of the teachers of the land of Israel. I will show this from their own words, cited in the Tisbite.

units.la: [Hebrew]
units.tr: [Hebrew]

units.la: id est ad verbum, O mnis Rab & Mar e Babylonia est: & omnis Ribbi e terra Israel. Ex hac nota medicinam faciam Epiphanio [Greek]. In libris vulgatis:
units.tr: That is, word for word: every Rab and Mar is from Babylonia, and every Ribbi is from the land of Israel. From this note I will make a remedy for Epiphanius [Greek]. In the printed books:

units.la: Niutiea
units.tr: Niutiea

units.la: {Greek}διδάσκαλον αὐτῶν Ἀκιβᾶν, ὅντα καλούμενον ἢ βασιλέα.
units.tr: {Greek} their teacher Akiba, who is called [Greek] or king.

units.la: à mala manu est βασιλέα· tu me consore emenda βασιλέα· emendatio certa. רבי עקיבא ה מדבר ο διδάσκαλος Akiba, id est Magister Akiba. Hieronymus epistola 151. Quæstione 10.
units.tr: The reading βασιλέα is from a bad hand; you, consult me: emend it to βασιλέα. The emendation is certain. [Hebrew], that is, ὁ διδάσκαλος Akiba, that is, Master Akiba. Jerome, letter 151, question 10.

units.la: „ Si quando eos iuxta literam cœperimus arcare, ut non iaceant, non ambulent, non stent, sed tantum sedeant, si velint præcepta seruare; solent respondere & dicere, Rab Akiba, & Symeon, & Hille Magistri nostri tradiderunt nobis, ut bis mille pedes ambulemus in sabbatho, & cætera iustinodi doctrinas hominum præferentes doctrinæ Dei.
units.tr: "If at any time we begin to restrain them according to the letter, so that they do not lie down, do not walk, do not stand, but only sit, if they wish to keep the precepts, they are accustomed to reply and say: Rab Akiba, and Simeon, and Hillel, our masters, handed down to us that we may walk two thousand paces on the sabbath, and other such doctrines of men, preferring them to the doctrine of God."

units.la: Hic obiter lego Hellel siue Hillel, videlicet הלל. nam ita vocatur hic Magister Iudæis. Idem in commentariis Isai. 8
units.tr: Here in passing I read Hellel or Hillel, namely [Hebrew]. For so this master is called by the Jews. The same author, in his commentary on Isaiah 8:

units.la: „ Duas domos Nazarei (qui ita Christum recipiunt ut obseruationes Legis veteris non amittat) duas familias interpretantur, Sammai & Hillel, ex quibus orti sunt scribæ & Pharisæi, quorum fuscepit scholam Akibas, quæ magistrum Aquilæ proselyti autumant. Si hoc vere autumant, vixit Akibas Christi ætate aut paulo post.
units.tr: "They interpret the two houses of the Nazarene (who receive Christ in such a way as not to lose the observances of the old Law) as two families, Shammai and Hillel, from whom arose the scribes and Pharisees, and whose school Akiba took up; they claim that Akiba was the teacher of Aquila the proselyte. If they truly claim this, then Akiba lived in the time of Christ or a little after."

units.la: Nam Aquilam proselytum, qui libros canonicos veteris Testamenti ex Hebraeo vertit in sermonem Græcum, constat fuisse sub Imperatore Adriano circa annum Christi centesimum vigesimum quintum: qua de re fuse dicam in Notis meis ad fragmenta veterum Interpretum in Psalmos.
units.tr: For it is established that Aquila the proselyte, who translated the canonical books of the Old Testament from Hebrew into Greek, lived under the emperor Hadrian around the year of Christ 125. I shall speak about this at length in my Notes on the fragments of the ancient interpreters on the Psalms.

units.la: CAP. XXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXI.

units.la: A. De Pharisæis, eorumque etymo. B. variis appellationibus, C. doctrina & hæresi. D. Nomina septem planetarum. E. 12 signa Zodiaca. F. Epiphanius variis locis sanatus.
units.tr: A. Of the Pharisees and their etymology. B. Their various names. C. Their doctrine and sect. D. The names of the seven planets. E. The twelve signs of the Zodiac. F. Epiphanius, variously healed.

units.la: PHARISÆI dicti quòd legem populo enarrarent. ijdem vocabantur הפרושים, id est sapientes aut philosophi. Gorionides Hist. Iud. lib. 4, cap. 25
units.tr: The Pharisees were so called because they expounded the law to the people. The same were called הפרושים [haperushim], that is, wise men or philosophers. Gorionides, Jewish History, book 4, chapter 25.

units.la: {Hebrew}: id est, Et sedit rex ad mensam cum sapientibus Israel. ipsi sunt Pharisæi, qui legem populo enarrant.
units.tr: [הוא וישב המלך אל השלחן עם חכמי ישראל] That is: "And the king sat at table with the wise men of Israel." These are the Pharisees, who expounded the law to the people.

units.la: reperio & חסידים de Pharisæis apud eundem authorem. Hieronymus in epistola ad Algasiam Quæstione x
units.tr: I also find that they were called חסידים [hasidim] in the same author. Jerome, in his letter to Algasia, question 10.

units.la: E
units.tr: E

units.la: „ Videntur igitur obseruationes Iudaicæ apud imperitos, & vilem „ plebeculam, imaginem habere rationis, humanæque sapientiæ. „ vnde & doctores eorum σοφοὶ, hoc est sapientes vocantur: & si „ quando certis diebus traditiones suas exponunt discipulis suis, so- „ lent dicere, οἱ σοφοὶ διδασκαλοι... id est sapientes docent traditiones.
units.tr: "Therefore the Jewish observances seem to the unlearned and the cheap common rabble to have an image of reason and human wisdom. Hence their teachers are also called σοφοί [sophoi], that is, wise men; and whenever on certain days they expound their traditions to their disciples, they are wont to say, οἱ σοφοὶ διδάσκαλοι [hoi sophoi didaskaloi], that is, the wise teach the traditions."

units.la: οἱ σοφοὶ διδασκαλοι, חכמים תנו. docebant traditiones maiorum religiose seruandas contra Saducæos. Gorionides in loco memorato:
units.tr: οἱ σοφοὶ διδάσκαλοι [hoi sophoi didaskaloi], חכמים תנו [chakhamim tanu]: they taught that the traditions of the elders were to be kept religiously, against the Sadducees. Gorionides in the passage already cited:

units.la: הנה הפרושים היו אומרים נשמור חתורה אשר מסרו אבותינו בידינו מפרשת על פי החכמים אשר פרשו את התורה לקבלה:
units.tr: [הנה הפרושים היו אומרים נשמור התורה אשר מסרו אבותינו בידינו מפורשת על פי החכמים אשר פירשו את התורה לקבלה]

units.la: id est, Ecce Pharisæi dicebant, Seruemus legem, quam tradiderunt nobis patres nostri in manus nostras enarratam à sapientibus &c.
units.tr: That is: "Behold, the Pharisees used to say: Let us keep the law which our fathers handed down to us, as explained to us by the wise men, and so on."

units.la: Graue hac de re dissidium in populo. Pharisæis adhærebat plebs infima & vulgus. Saducæos ditiores ac potentiores sectabantur.
units.tr: There was a serious dispute among the people. The Pharisees were supported by the lowest class and the common folk; the Sadducees were followed by the richer and more powerful.

units.la: Idem ibidem:
units.tr: The same author, in the same place:

units.la: הלא העם הארץ היה עם הפרושים והיו לעורדים מלכי עשירים ונכרים כי היו עם המלך התרוקים ולמלך ולחם היו עשירים:
units.tr: [הלא העם הארץ היה עם הפרושים והיו לעזרם מלכים עשירים ונכבדים כי היו עם המלך והצדוקים והם היו עשירים] Roughly: "Were not the common people with the Pharisees, and did they not help them? The rich and noble kings, however, were with the king and the Sadducees, and they were wealthy."

units.la: id est, Tenuis plebecula cum Pharisæis erat, eósque adiuuabat: at diuites ac potentes è populo erant cum Rege & Saduceis.
units.tr: That is: "The humble common folk were with the Pharisees and helped them; but the rich and powerful men of the people were with the king and the Sadducees."

units.la: Iciunabant bis in septimana, videlicet diebus Lunæ & Iouis. hoc significat Epiphanius his verbis:
units.tr: They fasted twice a week, namely on the days of Monday and Thursday. Epiphanius states this in these words:

units.la: ιτηςυοι δὶς τὰ σαββάτα διυτέραν καὶ πέμπτων
units.tr: they fast twice in the week, on the second and fifth days [ιτηςυοι δὶς τὰ σαββάτα διυτέραν καὶ πέμπτων]

units.la: vbi in sabbatho positum pro, in hebdomade: vt ibi, Iciuno bis in sabbatho. Fato multum tribuebant. Astrologiæ operam dabant. Epiphanius vocabula recenseт Hebraica, quibus appellabat septem stellas, & duodecim signa Zodiaca, quæ adducam boni illius patris bono. Nam obscura pleraque apud ipsum, partim etiam corrupta.
units.tr: where "in the sabbath" is put for "in the week", as there: "I fast twice in the sabbath." They put much trust in fate and devoted themselves to astrology. Epiphanius lists the Hebrew names by which they called the seven planets and the twelve signs of the zodiac. I will cite them with due respect to that good father, for much of what he writes is obscure and some of it is also corrupted.

units.la: Nomina septem planetarum.
units.tr: Names of the seven planets.

units.la: ἥλιος ἡμαχαίσεμες Sol, σελήνη, ἰεριπεγαλέαχα Luna, ἄρης, χωχεδ ὀχιωλ, Mars stella, ἑρμῆς, χωχεδ ὀχμὸδ, Mercurius stella, Ζεὺς, χωχεδ βάχλ, Iuppiter stella, ἀφροδίτη, σεφυα ἠπι λουhd, Venus, κρόνος, χωχεδ σαbnθ, Saturnus stella.
units.tr: Sun [ἥλιος ἡμαχαίσεμες]; Moon [σελήνη, ἰεριπεγαλέαχα]; Mars, a star [ἄρης, χωχεδ ὀχιωλ]; Mercury, a star [ἑρμῆς, χωχεδ ὀχμὸδ]; Jupiter, a star [Ζεὺς, χωχεδ βάχλ]; Venus [ἀφροδίτη, σεφυα ἠπι λουhd]; Saturn [κρόνος, χωχεδ σαbnθ], a star.

units.la: ἡμαχαισεμες. חמה duo vocabula Solis, qui חמה dicitur à calore: σεμες autem à ministerio, tanquam minister & fax diei. In libris
units.tr: ἡμαχαισεμες [hemachaisemes]: two words for the Sun. חמה [chamah] is the Sun, so called from its heat; σεμες [semes], however, comes from its service, as the minister and torch of the day. In the books of the astrologers:

units.la: Astrologorum כּוֹכַב הַמַּח Sol stella.
units.tr: כּוֹכַב הַמַּח [kokhav hamach], the star of the Sun.

units.la: ιερεὺς ... יָרֵחַ וְהַלְּבָנָה. lectio alia ιερεὺς ... ילבנה ... pluma non interest, hoc an illo modo legas. λαβαρα antiquè pro λεβαρα, id est Luna, quæ etiam ירח vocatur. ab hac voce menses dicti sunt יְרָחִים qui lunares olim in Palæstina. Epiphanius:
units.tr: ιερεὺς [iereus] ... יָרֵחַ וְהַלְּבָנָה [yareach vehalevanah]: the Moon. Another reading is ιερεὺς ... ילבנה; it makes no difference which way you read it. λαβαρα [labara], formerly for λεβαρα [lebara], is the Moon, which is also called ירח [yareach]. From this word the months were called יְרָחִים [yerachim], which were lunar months in Palestine of old. Epiphanius:

units.la: ἱερεὺς γὰρ ὁ μὲν λέγεται· μηνῶν δὲ ἡ σελήνη, ὡς καὶ παρ᾽ Ἕλλησι διὰ τὸν μηνᾶ.
units.tr: "For the one is called 'priest'; the Moon, however, is of the months, as also among the Greeks, on account of the month (μήν)."

units.la: ὀχμωλ. hodie vocatur מאדים à rubore, de quo Abenezra in commentarijs Amos 5, 8: quem si rectè capio, dicit esse stellam magnam, quæ Hebraicè אדום vocetur, & in lingua Ismaelitarum סחיל. Pro מאדים quod reperio apud Lexicographos, malim scribi מַאְדִּים quasi ᾠυρρὸς. Hic planeta Aegyptijs πυρόεις appellatur ab igne. eius character δ clypeus Martis cum hasta.
units.tr: ὀχμωλ [ochmōl]: Mars. Today it is called מאדים [adom/ma'adim] from its redness, on which Abenezra in his commentary on Amos 5:8 says (if I understand him rightly) that it is a great star, called in Hebrew אדום [adom], and in the language of the Ishmaelites סחיל [sachil]. Rather than the form מאדים which I find in the lexicographers, I would prefer to write מַאְדִּים [ma'dim], as if it were ruddy (ᾠυρρὸς). This planet is called πυρόεις [pyroeis], fiery, by the Egyptians, from fire. Its symbol is δ, the shield of Mars with its spear.

units.la: ὀχμὼδ. Mercurius: hodie מִרְקוּלִיס aut מִרְקוּלִים voce barbara: aut כּוֹכָב, id est stella sidusue κατ' ἐξοχὴν. Aegyptijs ςίλβων.
units.tr: ὀχμὼδ [ochmōd]: Mercury. Today מִרְקוּלִיס or מִרְקוּלִים [Merkulis], a barbarous word; or כּוֹכָב [kokhav], that is, star, or the heavenly body par excellence. By the Egyptians it is called ςίλβων [silbōn], glittering.

units.la: χωχὰβ βααλ כּוֹכַב בַּעַל quasi κύριος ἢ δεσπότης, aliter צֶדֶק ab æquitate & iustitia. Aegyptijs φαέθων. huius mentio apud Iosephum Gorionis filium.
units.tr: χωχὰβ βααλ [chōkhab baal], כּוֹכַב בַּעַל [kokhav ba'al], as if κύριος [kyrios] or δεσπότης [despotēs], lord; otherwise צֶדֶק [tzedek], from equity and justice. By the Egyptians it is called φαέθων [phaethōn], shining. Josephus, the son of Gorion, mentions it.

units.la: λουσὶ. forte ἱλούντ לוחם hodie נוגה à splendore, Aegyptijs φωσφόρος, id est, Lucifer: Gorionides Hist. Iud. lib. 1. cap. 2.
units.tr: λουσὶ [lousi]: perhaps ἱλούντ [hilunt], לוחם [lochem]; today נוגה [nogah], from its brightness. By the Egyptians it is φωσφόρος [phōsphoros], that is, Lucifer. Gorionides, Jewish History, book 1, chapter 2:

units.la: היכל להציפר הוא חיכל כוכב חנותח
units.tr: [היכל להציפר הוא חיכל כוכב נוגה] "The temple of Lucifer is the temple of the star Nogah."

units.la: Templum Luciferi: hoc est templum Veneris.
units.tr: The temple of Lucifer; that is, the temple of Venus.

units.la: σαβϰ. Saturnus. hodie שַׁבְּתַי. ita dictus propter diem septimū. Idem ibidem סגר היכל סטרנוש הוא כוכב שבתאי
units.tr: σαβϰ [sabk]: Saturn. Today שַׁבְּתַי [Shabbetai], so named on account of the seventh day. The same author, in the same place: [סגר היכל סטרנוש הוא כוכב שבתאי] "He shut the temple of Saturn; this is the star Shabbetai."

units.la: id est, Clausit templum Saturni. ipse est Saturnus stella. eius character ћ falx Saturni. ab Aegyptijs φαίνων nuncupatur.
units.tr: That is, "he shut the temple of Saturn." This is the star of Saturn itself, and its character is ♄, the scythe of Saturn. The Egyptians call it Phaenon [φαίνων].

units.la: 12 signa Zodiaca.
units.tr: The twelve signs of the Zodiac.

units.la: Κριὸς, | τήλαα, | Aries, Ταῦρος, | σωρ, | Taurus, Δίδυμοι, | Ϛωμίμ, | Gemini, Καρκῖνος, | σπεσταν, | Cancer, Λέων, | ἄει, | Leo, Παρθένος, | βεσθουλα, | Virgo, Ζυγὸν, | μαζανη, | Libra, Σκορπίον, | ἀχεσβ, | Scorpio, Τοξότης, | κεσιτ, | Sagittarius, E Αιγόκερως, ג׳די, Capricornus, Τοξότης, ד׳לי, Aquarius, Ιχθύες. דגים, Pisces.
units.tr: Κριὸς [Krios], τήλαα [tēlaa], תלה [tela], Aries (the Ram). Ταῦρος [Tauros], σωρ [sōr], שור [shor], Taurus (the Bull). Δίδυμοι [Didymoi], Ϛωμίμ [Tōmim], תאומים [te'omim], Gemini (the Twins). Καρκῖνος [Karkinos], σπεσταν [spestan], Cancer (the Crab). Λέων [Leōn], ἄει [aei], ארי [ari], Leo (the Lion). Παρθένος [Parthenos], βεσθουλα [besthoula], בתולה [betulah], Virgo (the Virgin). Ζυγὸν [Zygon], μαζανη [mazanē], מאונים [moznayim], Libra (the Scales). Σκορπίον [Skorpion], ἀχεσβ [achesb], עקרב [akrav], Scorpio (the Scorpion). Τοξότης [Toxotēs], κεσιτ [kesit], Sagittarius (the Archer). Αιγόκερως [Aigokerōs], ג׳די [gedi], Capricornus (the Goat). Τοξότης [Toxotēs], ד׳לי [deli], Aquarius (the Water-carrier). Ιχθύες [Ichthyes], דגים [dagim], Pisces (the Fishes).

units.la: τηλα, תלה. σωρ. שור. Θωμμι, תאומים. σαγιττ. מרפא. hæc vera scriptura male apud Epiphanium σαγιτ. ἀει. ארי. perperá ἁρπ apud eundé. βεθθυλα בתולה virgo. μωζαιν aut μωζαιμ. à mala manu est μωμα-ζαιν. μωζαιμ מאונים. αχεφ vel αχεφ עקרב. ita legendum non ἀχεφ, quod est ab iniuria scribarum. ητοιτ משׂ, ג׳די נרי. דלי. In Epiphanio ... heu pessimam scripturam. ἀναμφισβήτως scribendum .דלי, aut דלוי more Chaldaico. ... pisces. Sagittarius à Rabbinis בעל קשת vocatur, id est sagittipotens, quomodo & Cicero eum vocat. Syrum est קשת. In lingua sacra קשת arcus. קשת sagittarius.
units.tr: Here Epiphanius's forms are corrupt, as with τηλα for תלה, σωρ for שור, Θωμμι for תאומים, and σαγιττ, which is the right reading, though Epiphanius wrongly gives σαγιτ. ἀει is ארי. He wrongly gives ἁρπ for the same word. βεθθυλα is בתולה, virgin. μωζαιν or μωζαιμ: a copyist's error has made it μωμα-ζαιν; the correct form is μωζαιμ, מאונים. αχεφ or αχεφ is עקרב, and this should be read ἀχεσβ rather than ἀχεφ, which is the result of scribal error. ητοιτ is משׂ, ג׳די is נרי, and דלי. In Epiphanius there is a most wretched corruption. It must be written without doubt דלי, or דלוי after the Chaldee manner. Pisces. The Rabbis call Sagittarius בעל קשת [baal qesheth], that is, the archer, just as Cicero also calls him. The Syriac is קשת. In the sacred tongue קשת means a bow, and קשת is the archer.

units.la: CAP. XXII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXII.

units.la: A. Talitha. B. Hieronymus in ea voce correctus. C. item Suid.u. D. Tabitha. E. In Targum vox explicata. F. Voces aliquot amatoriae.
units.tr: A. Talitha. B. Jerome corrected in that word. C. likewise Suidas. D. Tabitha. E. The word explained in the Targum. F. Some amatory words.

units.la: TALITHA non Talita, quod hodie scribunt ac legunt Talictha, id est טליתא puella. In libro De nominibus Hebraicis: Tabita cumi, puella surge. mendum manifestum, quod me auctore emendum ex Mar. 5, 4. vbi scriptum ταλιθα κουμ. Noli dubitare quin haec vera scriptura sit. Syrum est טליתא puella: at קומ pariter Syrum & Hebraeum apud Suidam perperam κουμ scriptum pro κουμ.
units.tr: TALITHA, not Talita, which people now write and read as Talictha, that is טליתא, a girl. In the book On Hebrew Names: "Tabita cumi, girl, arise." This is an obvious error, which on my authority is to be corrected from Mark 5:4, where it is written ταλιθα κουμ. Do not doubt that this is the true reading. In Syriac, טליתא means girl; but קומ is likewise Syriac and Hebrew, and Suidas wrongly wrote it κουμ.

units.la: ταλιθα κουμ ηγουν ή ωταις εγειρω.
units.tr: Talitha cum, that is, "Maiden, arise" [ταλιθα κουμ, ἤγουν ἡ ὠταις εγειρω].

units.la: In declaratione Marci:
units.tr: In the explanation of Mark:

units.la: χορα σοι σοι λέγω εγειραι.
units.tr: "Damsel, I say to you, arise" [κόρα, σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειραι].

units.la: verba illa σοί λέγω includenda sunt parenthesi, ne quis putet ea interpretationis esse. huius masculinum apud Chaldaeos טלי & ταλις: à quo ταλις vox reperta à me in authoribus Graecis.
units.tr: The words "I say to you" must be enclosed in parentheses, lest anyone think they belong to the interpretation. Its masculine form among the Chaldeans is טלי, and ταλις in Greek; from this I found the word ταλις in Greek authors.
Acts 9:36.

units.la: ταβιθα ή διερμηνευομένη λέγεται δορκάς.
units.tr: "Tabitha, which being interpreted is called Dorcas" [ταβιθα ἡ διερμηνευομένη λέγεται δορκάς].

units.la: scribo טביתא. Syrum est ex Hebraeo צביה mutatione Tsadi in teth. Babylonij sonant טביתא, id est Tabietha, vt Taliètha, de quo supra.
units.tr: I write טביתא. In Syriac it comes from the Hebrew צביה, with Tsade changed into Teth. The Babylonians pronounce it טביתא, that is Tabietha, as Taliètha, of which above.

units.la: Frequens est apud interpretes Chaldaeos. Vocatur caprea alio nomine mine ארי דסש, quæ vox extat in Ierosolymitana Prouerb. s, 19, vnde Græcum δλζα. Hesychius δlζα, αἰξ. translatio Latina Compluti impressa, exultatio imperitè. Munsterus in Lexico ארי camelopardalis, ex hac nota corrigendus est. In lib. De nom. Hebr. Tabitha, damna aut caprea, leg. dama aut caprea. ita Glo. Vet. Leuia hæc, in quibus hærere pudet pigetque. Chrysostomus apud Theophylactum ad illud ὀνόματι Ταλιθά &c.
units.tr: It is frequent among the Chaldean interpreters. It is called a roe, under another name [ארי דסש], a word found in the Jerusalem Targum on Proverbs 5:19, whence the Greek δορκάς. Hesychius: δορκάς, a goat. The Latin translation printed at Alcalá has "exultation", which is unskilled. Münster, in his Lexicon, renders ארי as "camelopard"; it must be corrected by this note. In the book On Hebrew Names, "Tabitha, damna aut caprea" should be read "dama aut caprea." So too the Old Glossary. These are trifles, over which one is ashamed and sorry to linger. Chrysostom, in Theophylact, on the words "by the name Tabitha", etc.

units.la: τιθησι δὲ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆ, δεικνὺς ὅτι φεραύμος ἦν ὕπνας ἐχρημόρυγα καὶ νήφουσα ὥσπερ δορκας.
units.tr: [τιθησι δὲ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆ, δεικνὺς ὅτι φεραύμος ἦν ὕπνας ἐχρημόρυγα καὶ νήφουσα ὥσπερ δορκας.] He gives her the name, showing that she was gentle and wakeful, and sober like a gazelle.

units.la: hoc verum sit, Deus nouit: dixerim aliud: est caprae vocabulum inter amatoria. Quid si inde nomen mulieris? Apud Salomonem Caprea gratiae, &, Cerua amorum: sicut apud Arabes Corat alhain, id est pupilla oculi, voces sunt blandè compellantis vxorem aut amicam.
units.tr: Whether this is true, God knows. I would suggest otherwise: "caprea" is a word among the amatory terms. What if the woman's name comes from there? In Solomon, "a graceful doe" and "a hind of loves" (Prov. 5:19); as among the Arabs, "Corat alhain", that is "pupil of the eye", are words of tender address to a wife or a friend.

units.la: CAP. XXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXIII.

units.la: A. De Herodianis sententia noua. B. ijdem dicti Dorsiani. C. & Hellemiani à Iustino.
units.tr: A. On the new opinion of the Herodians. B. The same called Dorsians. C. And Hellemians, according to Justin.
