Deinde Gratianus aggreditur secundum, quod est in Apostolo, volens ostendere, quòd, Si forte Maritus aliquis ordinetur, Ordinandus est vnius duntaxat uxoris vir.
units.tr: When the Apostle Paul chose those to be ordained, whether elders or deacons, and whoever is to be ordained to the leadership of the Church, he did not say, "If anyone is without sin." (For if he had said that, every man would be rejected and no one would be ordained.) He said, "If anyone is without crime," such as murder, adultery, some uncleanness, fornication, theft, fraud, sacrilege, and other things of this kind. For a crime is a grave sin, most worthy of accusation and condemnation. Note this well: whoever is to be ordained a bishop must be free from crime not only at the time of his ordination but at all times after baptism. Next, Gratian turns to the second point, which is in the Apostle, wishing to show that if by chance a married man is ordained, the one to be ordained must be the husband of one wife only.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXVI.
units.tr: DISTINCTIO XXVI.

units.la: Sequitur in utráque Epistola.
units.tr: It follows in both Epistles.

units.la: ΜΙΑΣ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΟΣ ΑΝΔΡΑ.
units.tr: OF ONE WIFE A HUSBAND. [ΜΙΑΣ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΟΣ ΑΝΔΡΑ]

units.la: Vnius uxoris virum. Post Baptisma, videlicet, non ante Baptismum.
units.tr: The husband of one wife. That is, after baptism, not before baptism.

units.la: Duobus in locis Gratianus problema disputandum proposuit, Habendus ne sit Digamus is, qui, vnam, antequam baptizaretur, alteram verò post lavacrum, priore mortuâ, duxit vxorē: scilicet, in hac xxvi distinctione, et in quaestione tertia causæ vigesimæ octauæ. Virinque more suo disputans, eadem citat. Errans tamen (vt nimium saepe solet) in authorum titulis Quòd in Digamiam non incurrat ille secundò maritus, probatur. Hieronymus enim scribit ad Oceanum.
units.tr: In two places Gratian has proposed a question for debate: whether a man should be held to be a digamist who, before he was baptized, took one wife, and after the washing, when the first was dead, took another. That is, in this twenty-sixth distinction and in the third question of the twenty-eighth cause. Arguing on both sides in his usual way, he cites the same authorities. Yet, erring (as he very often does) in the titles of the authors, he proves that the second husband does not fall into digamy. For Jerome writes to Oceanus:

units.la: Ministro futuro non obstat Digamia, quæ post Baptismum non contrahitur.
units.tr: Digamy is no hindrance to a future minister, since it is not contracted after baptism.

units.la: VNius uxoris viru̅,id est, Monogamum post Baptifmum: Nam si coniugem prius habuerit, quæ& obierit, A baptismo repetitæ nuptiæ non imputantur ei. Cui prorsus novo homini, nec stupra, nec alia, quæ ante fuerunt, amplius obsunt. Hæc Hieronymi quidem sententia, multis ab eodem rationibus nec uno loco defensa, quas Gratianus hic omisit. Contrà sentit Augustinus in.18. cap. libri De bono coniugali. To.6.
units.tr: "The husband of one wife," that is, a monogamist after baptism. For if he had a wife before, and she has died, the marriage he later contracts is not counted against him from the time of baptism. Former fornications and other things that happened before do no further harm to such a new man. This is indeed Jerome's opinion, defended by him on many grounds and in more than one place, which Gratian has omitted here. Augustine holds the contrary view in book 18, chapter 4 of On the Good of Marriage, vol. 6.

units.la: Vnam qui duxerit ante Baptismum: Postque Baptismum duxerit alteram, non est ordinandus, quia Digamus.
units.tr: He who took one wife before baptism, and after baptism took another, is not to be ordained, because he is a digamist.

units.la: ACutius hoc intellexerunt, qui nec eum, qui Catechumenus, vel Paganus habuerit alteram, ordinandum esse censuerunt: De Sacramento enim agitur, non de peccato: Nam in Baptismo, peccata omnia dimittuntur. Sed qui dixit,— Si acceperis uxorem, non peccasti:&, Si nupserit virgo, non peccat:&, Quod vult faciat, non peccat, si nubat: Satis declarauit nuptias nullum esse peccatum. Propter Sacramenti autem sanctitatem, sicut fœmina, etiamsi Catechumena fuerit vitiata, non potest post Baptismum inter Dei virgines consecrari: Ita non absurdè visum est, eum qui excesserit uxorum numerum singularem, non peccatum aliquod commisisse, sed normam quandam Sacramenti amisisse, non ad vitæ bonæ meritum, sed ad ordinationis Ecclesiasticæ signaculum, necessariam.
units.tr: More acutely, those who considered that a man who had a second wife while still a catechumen or a pagan should not be ordained understood this matter. For it concerns a sacrament, not a sin, since in baptism all sins are forgiven. But he who said, "If you have taken a wife, you have not sinned," and "If a virgin marries, she does not sin," and "Let her do what she wills; she does not sin if she marries," has made it sufficiently clear that marriage is no sin. Yet, on account of the holiness of the sacrament, just as a woman who was violated while still a catechumen cannot after baptism be consecrated among God's virgins, so it has seemed not unreasonable that the man who has exceeded the single number of wives has committed no sin, but has lost a certain rule of the sacrament, which is necessary not for the merit of a good life but for the sign of ecclesiastical ordination.

units.la: Vt allegorica fuit in antiquæ legis Patriarchis uxorum multitudo: Sic est& vnius in nostris.
units.tr: Just as the multitude of wives among the patriarchs of the old law was allegorical, so is the unity of the wife among us.

units.la: §. Ac per hoc, sicut plures uxores antiquorum patrum significauerunt futuras nostras ex omnibus gentibus Ecclesias, uni viro subditas Christo: ita noster Antistes unius uxoris vir, significat ex omnibus gentibus unitatem, uni viro subditam Christo: quæ tunc perficietur, quum revelaverit occulta tenebrarum, & manifestaverit cogitationes cordis, & tunc laus erit unicuique à Deo.
units.tr: §. And therefore, just as the many wives of the ancient fathers signified our future churches from all nations, subject to Christ, the one husband; so our bishop, the husband of one wife, signifies the unity from all nations, subject to Christ, the one husband. This will be perfected when he shall reveal the hidden things of darkness and make manifest the thoughts of the heart, and then every man shall have praise from God.

units.la: Item. Innocentius papa Romæ 1. in cap. 2. Epistolæ suæ 22. quam scripsit ad Episcopos Macedoniæ, Constantio Consule, id est, anno Christi 416. Videtur hæc instituta fuisse disputatio contra Hieronymum: quod deprehendas ex sæpe citata Epistola ad Oceanum: sed antequam foret ille Papa.
units.tr: Likewise. Innocent, pope at Rome, in chapter 2 of his letter 22, which he wrote to the bishops of Macedonia in the consulship of Constantius, that is, in the year of Christ 416. This disputation seems to have been set up against Jerome, as you may gather from the often cited letter to Oceanus; but it was before he was pope.

units.la: Culpa remittitur in Baptismo: Lex vero naturæ, vel coniugij non aboletur.
units.tr: Guilt is forgiven in baptism, but the law of nature, or of marriage, is not abolished.

units.la: DEinde ponitur: Non dici oportere Digamum eum, qui Catechumenus habuerit & amiserit uxorem, si post Baptismum fuerit aliam sortitus: eámque primam videri, quæ nouo homini copulata sit: quia illud coniugium per Baptismi sacramentum cum cæteris criminibus sit ablutum. Quòd cùm de una utique dicitur: certè si tres habuerit in veteri positus homine uxores, erit ei, quæ post Baptismum quarta est, sic interpretantibus, prima. Virginis æque nomen accipiet, quæ quarto loco ducta est. Quis (oro) istud non videat contra Apostoli esse præceptum, qui air, Vnius uxoris virum oportere fieri sacerdote? Sed obiicitur, Quòd in Baptismo totum, quicquid in veteri homine gestum est, sit lotum. Dicite mihi (cum pace vestra loquar) an crimina tantùm dimittuntur in Baptismo: an & illa, quæ secundum Dei præcepta ac Dei instituta complentur? Vxorem ducere, crimen est, an non est crimen? Si crimen est, ergo (præfatâ veniâ dixerim) erit author in culpa: qui, ut crimina committerentur, in paradiso præcepit, cùm ipse eos benedixit. Si verò non est crimen: quia, quod Deus instituit, nefas est crimen appellari: & Salomon addidit: Etenim à Deo præparatur viro uxor: quomodo creditur inter crimina esse dimissum, quod Deo authore legitur consummatum?
units.tr: Next it is laid down that a man should not be called a digamist who, while a catechumen, had a wife and lost her, if after baptism he obtained another; and that the first is seen to be the one joined to the new man, because that marriage was washed away with the other sins by the sacrament of baptism. But when this is said of one wife only, certainly, if he had three wives while he was in the old man, then for those who interpret this way the fourth, taken after baptism, will be the first. He will also receive the name of a virgin, since he was married in the fourth place. Who (I ask) does not see that this is contrary to the precept of the Apostle, who says that a bishop must be the husband of one wife? But it is objected that in baptism whatever was done in the old man is washed away. Tell me (with your permission I speak) whether only sins are forgiven in baptism, or also those things which are fulfilled according to God's commands and God's institutions. Is taking a wife a sin or not? If it is a sin, then (I say this with due respect) the author of it is at fault, who, in order that sins might be committed, commanded it in paradise, when he himself blessed them. But if it is not a sin, because what God instituted cannot rightly be called a crime, and Solomon added, "For a wife is prepared for a man by the Lord," how is it believed that among the sins what is read to have been brought about with God as its author has been forgiven?

units.la: Euangelii christi, Nuptias & Successiones hæreditarias, uti naturales ac legitimas, inter gentiles approbat.
units.tr: The Gospel of Christ approves marriages and hereditary successions, as natural and lawful, among the gentiles.

units.la: §. Quid de talium filiis censetur? nunquid non erunt admittendi in hæreditatis consortium, qui ex ea suscepti sunt, quæ ante Baptismum fuit uxor? erúntque appellandi vel Naturales, vel Spurij? quia non est legitimum matrimonium, nisi illud (ut nobis videtur) quod post Baptismum assumitur. Ipse Deus, cū interrogaretur à Iudæis, si liceret uxorem dimittere: atque exponeret fieri non debere, addidit: Quos Deus coniunxit, homo non separet. An ne de his locutus esse credatur, qui uxores post Baptismum fortiuntur? Meminerint & hoc à Iudæis interrogatum, & etiam Iudæis esse responsum.
units.tr: §. What is judged concerning the sons of such men? Shall they not be admitted to the fellowship of the inheritance, those who were born of the woman who was their wife before baptism? And shall they be called either natural or bastard, because the only lawful marriage is, as it seems to us, the one entered into after baptism? When God himself was asked by the Jews whether it was lawful to put away a wife, and he explained that it ought not to be done, he added, "What God has joined together, let not man put asunder." Or is it to be believed that he spoke of those who obtain wives after baptism? Let them remember that this was asked by the Jews, and that an answer was given to the Jews as well.

units.la: Frater gentilis cum fratre Christiano paternam diuidit hæreditatem.
units.tr: A gentile brother divides the paternal inheritance with a Christian brother.

units.la: §. Quæro, & solicitus quæro, Si una eademque sit uxor eius, qui ante Catechumenus, postea Fidelis: filiósque ex ea, quum esset Cathecumenus susceperit: & postea alios filios cùm sit Fidelis, Vtrum sint fratres appellandi? an non habeant postea, defuncto patre, Ercisцundæ hæreditatis consortium, quibus filiorum nomen regeneratio spiritualis creditur abstulisse? quod cùm ita sentire absurdum est: quæ ratio est hoc defendi, & vacuâ magis opinione iactari, quàm aliquâ authoritate roborari? quum non possit inter peccata deputari, quod lex præcepit, quod Deus iunxit, & Lex iungit.
units.tr: §. I ask, and earnestly ask: if a man who was first a catechumen and later a believer has one and the same wife, and has sons by her while he was a catechumen, and afterwards other sons while he is a believer, are they to be called brothers, or do they not, after the father's death, have a share in the partition of the inheritance? Does spiritual regeneration seem to have taken away the name of sons from those to whom it is believed to have taken it? Since it is absurd to think so, what reason is there for defending this and tossing it about on empty opinion rather than confirming it by any authority? Since what the law commands, what God has joined, and what the Law joins, cannot be counted among sins.

units.la: Virtutis opus Infideli demum prodest, si conuertatur ad fidem.
units.tr: A work of virtue profits an unbeliever only if he is converted to the faith.

units.la: §. Nunquid, si Catechumenus virtutibus studuit, humilitatem secutus est, patientiam tenuit, eleemosynas fecit, morti destinatos quâlibet ratione eripuit, adulteria exhorruit, castitatem tenuit: Quæro, Si hæc omnia, quum factus fuerit fidelis, amittit, quia per Baptismum totum quod vetus homo gesserat, putatur auferri? Aspicias gentilem hominem Cornelium, orationibus atque eleemosynis vacantem, Angelum audientem per revelationem, ipsumque Petrum videntem: nunquid per Baptismum hæc illi ablata sunt, propter quæ ei Baptismus videtur esse concessus? Si ita creditur, mihi credite, non modicum erratur: quia, quicquid bene gestum fuerit, & secundum præcepta legalia custoditum, non potest facientibus deperire.
units.tr: §. Suppose a catechumen has pursued virtues, has followed humility, has kept patience, has given alms, has rescued from any cause those destined to death, has abhorred adulteries, and has kept chastity. I ask: if, when he has become a believer, he loses all these things, because through baptism everything the old man had done is supposed to be taken away? Look at the gentile Cornelius, devoted to prayers and alms, listening to an angel through a revelation, and seeing Peter himself. Were those things taken from him through baptism, on account of which baptism seems to have been granted to him? If that is believed, believe me, it is no small error; for whatever has been done well and kept according to the legal precepts cannot perish for those who did it.

units.la: Nuptiarum copula nectitur à Deo. quam vel Baptismus, vel alia, quæcunque postea recipiuntur, Ecclesiæ sacramenta, dissolvere non possunt. Id etiam probatur in can. Si quis docuerit. 38. dist.
units.tr: The bond of marriage is tied by God, and neither baptism nor any other sacrament of the Church received afterwards can dissolve it. This is also proved in the canon "If anyone has taught," distinction 38.

units.la: §. Nuptiarum ergo copula, quia Dei mandato perficitur, non potest dici peccatum: & quod peccatum non est, solui inter peccata credi non debet. Eritque integrum & salutare existimare, aboleri non posse prioris nomen uxoris: quum non sit dimissum pro peccato, quod ex Dei sit voluntate completum.
units.tr: §. Therefore the bond of marriage, since it is accomplished by the command of God, cannot be called a sin; and what is not a sin ought not to be believed to be dissolved among sins. It will be sound and wholesome to think that the name of the former wife cannot be abolished, since it was not put away as a sin, having been fulfilled by the will of God.

units.la: Item. Ambrosius in libro primo de officiis. cap. vltimo. In Episcopum Mediolanensem vocatus est, Damaso Papa Romæ sedente, maiorèque Valentiniano regnante, circiter annum salutis 370. quum Præses tunc esset Italicæ Galliæ. Demum, Fl. Stilicone res imperij administrante obiit, sub annum 405.
units.tr: Likewise. Ambrose, in book 1 of On the Duties, last chapter. He was called to be bishop of Milan while Damasus was seated as pope at Rome and Valentinian the Elder was reigning, about the year of salvation 370, when he was then governor of Italian Gaul. Finally, when Flavius Stilicho was administering the affairs of the empire, he died, about the year 405.

units.la: Digamus est qui ante Baptismum duxerit vnam, & alteram post Baptismum: Nec enim quandocunque repetita nuptiæ conueniunt sacerdotali castimoniæ.
units.tr: A digamist is one who before baptism took one wife, and after baptism another. For a marriage repeated at any time does not agree with sacerdotal chastity.

units.la: VNa tantùm, nec repetita, nobis copula permittitur: & in ipso coniugio Lex est, non iterare coniugium, nec secunda coniugis sortiri coniunctionem.' Quod plerisque mirum videtur: cur etiam ante Baptismum iterato coniugio, electioni muneris, & praerogatiua ordinationis, impedimenta generentur: quum delicta obesse non soleat, si lauacri remissa fuerint Sacramento. Sed intelligere debemus, quia in Baptismo culpa dimitti potest, Lex aboleri non potest. In coniugio non culpa, sed Lex est quod culpae est igitur, in Baptismo relaxatur: quod Legis est, in coniugio non soluitur. Quomodo autem potest esse hortator viduitatis, qui & ipse coniugia frequentauerit? hic inter ethnicos coniugia vera fuisse docet, adhuc alia ex Euangelio depromptâ authoritate.
units.tr: Only one marriage, and never a repeated one, is permitted to us; and in marriage itself the law is that one should not marry again, nor obtain a second union with a spouse. This seems strange to many: why, even before baptism, does a second marriage create impediments to the choice of an office and to the privilege of ordination, since sins do not usually stand in the way once they have been forgiven in the sacrament of washing? But we must understand that in baptism guilt can be dismissed, whereas the law cannot be abolished. In marriage it is not guilt but law; what belongs to guilt is relaxed in baptism, but what belongs to the law is not loosed in marriage. Yet how can he be a promoter of widowhood who has himself frequented marriages? Here he teaches that among the heathen there were true marriages, and he adds another authority drawn from the Gospel.

units.la: IOannes Baptista, dum Herodem ab incestu prohiberet, dicens: Non licet tibi habere vxorem fratris tui: Euidenter ostendit inter Infidelles coniugia esse.
units.tr: John the Baptist, when he forbade Herod from incest, saying, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife" (Matt. 14.), plainly shows that there were marriages among unbelievers.

units.la: Vnde datur intelligi quòd Digami dicuntur, non solùm qui post Baptisma coniugia frequentant, sed etiam qui ante Baptisinum vnam, & post Baptismum alteram habuisse probantur. Digamus verò in sacerdotem ordinari non debet, non quia deliquerit, secundam accipiendo vxorem, sed quia praerogatiuâ exutus est sacerdotis. Vnde Ambrosius in Epistola 82.libro 10.ad Vercellensem Ecclesiam ait.
units.tr: From this it is understood that those are called twice-married not only who have frequented marriages after baptism, but also who are proved to have had one wife before baptism and another after it. A twice-married man ought not to be ordained a priest, not because he has sinned by taking a second wife, but because he has been stripped of the privilege of the priesthood. Hence Ambrose says in his Epistle 82, book 10, to the Church of Vercelli:

units.la: Non est inquinatus Digamus: non tamen est ad Sacerdotium mundus.
units.tr: A twice-married man is not defiled; yet he is not clean for the priesthood.

units.la: QVi sine crimine, Vnius vxoris est vir, tenetur ad legem sacerdotij suscipiendi, Qui autem iterauerit coniugium, culpam quidem non habet coinquinati, sed praerogatiuâ exuitur sacerdotis. Ergo dispensatorem Ecclesiae non licet ordinari, nisi vnius vxoris virum, Christiane Sacerdos, Caue, ne cum nuptiatoribus Gnosticis existimes hoc esse verbum sancientis, quasi non liceat Episcopum fieri, qui suam non circunducat vxorem. Taccbo de caeteris Apostolis, omnibus fere virginibus, aut caelibus: Ipse Paulus non fuisset Episcopus. Non ergo legem, sed modum ponit. Vt si contigerit a seculi rebus ad hoc caeleste munus quempiam vocari, sit ille Monogamus, Haec omnium, ne vno quidem contradicente, veterum sententia patrum. De qua nos in Canonibus Apostolorum, & in subsequentibus adhuc distinctionibus.
units.tr: "He who is blameless is the husband of one wife" is bound by the law of taking up the priesthood. But he who has married again does not indeed have the stain of guilt, but is stripped of the privilege of the priesthood. Therefore it is not lawful to ordain as steward of the Church anyone except a man of one wife. Christian priest, beware lest you think, with the Gnostic wedding-men, that this is a word enacting a law, as if it were not lawful to become a bishop who does not drag about his own wife. I say nothing of the other apostles, nearly all of whom were virgins or unmarried; Paul himself would not have been a bishop. Therefore he sets down not a law but a measure: so that if anyone is called from worldly affairs to this heavenly office, he should be a man of one marriage. This is the opinion of all the ancient Fathers, with not even one dissenting; on which we shall also touch in the Canons of the Apostles and in the distinctions that follow.

units.la: Post hanc autem verborum significationem sic explanatam, iam res ipsas aggrediamur. Caeterum (quae nostri est infoelicitas /zui) quia moribus tam diuersis hodie viuitur, vt haec omnia iure πκλαιὰ videri queat, ne me forte (quod lex prohibet) πῶς προσβυτέρους κακολογῆν velle suspicetur aliquis, Hic ego praefabor, quod & Hieronymus haec ipsa interpretaturus ad Oceanum scribit; inquiens. ___
units.tr: Now, after this meaning of the words has been explained in this way, let us turn to the matters themselves. Moreover (which is the misfortune of our time), since people live today by such different customs that all these things may rightly seem old-fashioned, lest anyone perhaps suspect that I wish to speak ill of elders (which the law forbids), I shall preface here what Jerome also writes to Oceanus when he is about to explain these very things, saying: ___

units.la: Obsecro, ne quis me in suggillatione istius temporis sacerdotum scripsisse, quę scripsi, exi-stimer: sed in Ecclesiæ vtilitate. Vt enim Oratores & Philosophi, describentes qualem velint esse perfectum Oratorem & Philosophum, non faciunt iniuriam Demostheni & Platoni, sed res ipsas absque personis definiunt: Sic in descriptione Episcopi, & in eorum expositione, quæ scripta sunt, quasi SPECVLVM SACERDOTII proponitur. Iam in potestate & conscientia singulorum est, quales se ipsi aspiciant: vt vel dolere ad deformitatē, vel gaudere ad pulchritudinem possint. Hæc ego, nec alia mente, suscepi modo tractandas ipsas Gratiani uxpiuerus, exordiens à tertia vigesima quinta Distinctionis parte. Can. Vnum oratium, §. Ac primùm.
units.tr: I beg that no one think I have written what I have written as a reproach to the priests of this time, but for the benefit of the Church. For just as orators and philosophers, describing the kind of perfect orator and philosopher they wish to have, do no injury to Demosthenes and Plato, but define the things themselves apart from persons, so in the description of a bishop and in the exposition of what has been written, a MIRROR OF THE PRIESTHOOD is set forth. Now it is up to each man's own conscience how he regards himself, so that he may either grieve at the deformity or rejoice at the beauty. I have undertaken to treat these very things of Gratian's, in no other mind, beginning from the twenty-fifth part of the Distinction. Canon "Unum oratium," §. "Ac primum."

units.la: Auditor Christiane, Non est vana, nec ociosa res, Esse Sacerdotem: Rasum non satis est habere verticem: Pileolo caput, orbiculato quondam, nunc autem cornuto & cristato velare: vestem ad talos demittere: linea superinduere: & alia Sacerdotis externa signa gerere non sufficit: Nisi tu quoque sis internis illis vestitus ornamentis, quae Sacerdotibus per Apostolum suum Christus ipse confuit & concinnauit. Ea modo vobis ipsius Apostoli verbis singula referam: quae sunt huius initio libelli propositia. Deinde cū Gratiano singulorum aggrediemur interpretationem.
units.tr: Christian listener, it is no empty or idle matter to be a priest. It is not enough to have a shaved crown; it is not enough to cover the head with a little cap, once round but now horned and crested; nor to let the garment fall to the ankles, to put on a linen vestment, and to wear the other external signs of a priest. Unless you are also adorned with those inward garments of ornament which Christ himself has arranged and fashioned for priests through his Apostle. I shall report these one by one to you in the very words of the Apostle himself, which are set forth at the beginning of this little book. Then, with Gratian, I shall take up their explanation one by one.

units.la: ΔΕΙ ΤΟΝ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΕΡΟΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ (ut ait Apostolus) Oportet Presbyterum esse.
units.tr: IT IS NECESSARY THAT THE ELDER BE (as the Apostle says): It behoves a presbyter to be [ΔΕΙ ΤΟΝ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΕΡΟΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ].

units.la: ΑΝΕΠΙΛΗΠΤΟΝ, ΚΑΙ ΑΝΕΓΚΛΗΤΟΝ, Id est, Irreprehensibilem & Inaccusabilem.
units.tr: Irreprehensible and unaccused [ΑΝΕΠΙΛΗΠΤΟΝ, ΚΑΙ ΑΝΕΓΚΛΗΤΟΝ]. That is, blameless and unaccusable.

units.la: ΜΙΑΣ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΟΣ ΑΝΔΡΑ. Id est, Vnius uxoris virum, seu maritum.
units.tr: Of one wife a husband [ΜΙΑΣ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΟΣ ΑΝΔΡΑ]. That is, a husband or man of one wife.

units.la: ΝΗΦΑΛΙΟΝ, Id est, Vigilem, Intentu & Sobrium.
units.tr: Sober [ΝΗΦΑΛΙΟΝ]. That is, watchful, attentive and temperate.

units.la: ΣΩΦΡΟΝΑ. Id est, Prudentem, Prouidum, Pudicum.
units.tr: Prudent [ΣΩΦΡΟΝΑ]. That is, wise, provident, chaste.

units.la: ΚΟΣΜΙΟΝ, Id est, Ornatum, Modestum, Benéque moratum.
units.tr: Orderly [ΚΟΣΜΙΟΝ]. That is, well-ordered, modest, and of good behaviour.

units.la: ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΟΝ Id est, Hospitalem, Peregrinos, & absentes à patria benignè suscipientem.
units.tr: Hospitable [ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΟΝ]. That is, welcoming kindly strangers and those absent from their country.

units.la: ΔΙΔΑΚΤΙΚΟΝ, Id est, Qui sic doctrinâ polleat, ut alios docere possit.
units.tr: Apt to teach [ΔΙΔΑΚΤΙΚΟΝ]. That is, one who is so strong in teaching that he can instruct others.

units.la: ΜΗ ΠΑΡΟΙΝΟΝ, Id est, Non vinolentum, nec ebriosum. Quale sit hoc ornamentum videbimus in dist. 44.
units.tr: Not given to wine [ΜΗ ΠΑΡΟΙΝΟΝ]. That is, not drunk with wine, nor a drunkard. What kind of ornament this is we shall see in dist. 44.

units.la: MH ΓΛΗΚΤΗΝ, id est, Non percussorem, nec violentum hominem. Competerit hoc enodatum in dist. 45.
units.tr: Not a striker [ΜΗ ΠΛΗΚΤΗΝ]. That is, not a smiter, nor a violent man. This will be made plain in dist. 45.

units.la: ἈMAXON, id est, A rixis, & altercationibus, & pugnis quibuslibet alienum. Vt ostendetur in dist. 46.
units.tr: Gentle [ἈΜΑΧΟΝ]. That is, free from quarrels, disputes, and any fighting. As will be shown in dist. 46.

units.la: MH ΑΙΣΚΡΟΚΕΡΔΗ. ΑΦΙΛΑΡΓΥΡΟΝ. ΤΟΝ ΙΔΙΟΥ ΟΙΚΟΥ ΚΑΛΩΣ ΠΡΟΙΣΤΑΜΕΝΟΝ. id est, Non turpium lucrorum sectatorem. Non cupidum, nec amantem pecuniae. Familiae suae bene praesidentem. Quae tria declarabuntur in dist. 46.
units.tr: Not greedy of filthy lucre [ΜΗ ΑΙΣΧΡΟΚΕΡΔΗ]. Not lover of money [ΑΦΙΛΑΡΓΥΡΟΝ]. Ruling his own house well [ΤΟΝ ΙΔΙΟΥ ΟΙΚΟΝ ΚΑΛΩΣ ΠΡΟΙΣΤΑΜΕΝΟΝ]. That is, not a pursuer of base gains. Not covetous, nor a lover of money. Well presiding over his own family. These three things will be declared in dist. 46.
14 and 15

units.la: MH ΝΕΟΦΥΤΟΝ. ΚΑΙ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΙΑΝ ΚΑΛΗΝ ΕΧΕΙΝ ΑΠΟ ΤΩΝ ΕΞΩΘΕΝ. id est, Non Neophytum. & ab extraneis etiam probatum, & laudatum. De Notitiis non ordinandis, & de bona fama necessaria presbyteris agetur, in dist. 48.
units.tr: Not a neophyte [ΜΗ ΝΕΟΦΥΤΟΝ], and having a good testimony from those outside [ΚΑΙ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΙΑΝ ΚΑΛΗΝ ΕΧΕΙΝ ΑΠΟ ΤΩΝ ΕΞΩΘΕΝ]. That is, not a novice, and approved and praised also by outsiders. Concerning those not to be ordained who are unknown, and concerning the good reputation necessary for elders, it will be treated in dist. 48.

units.la: Sacerdotales quindecim vestes, nec vnius illas generis, formae, vel coloris, videtis, Auditores Christiani. Quibus quidem, sicut oportet, si nos ornauerimus, si nobis illas adaptauerimus, A frigoribus niuis nihil est, quod timeamus, vestiti duplicibus: vt vestiri monemur, proverb. 31. cap. Nos haec habetes (inquam) vestimenta nuptialia possumus ad Regis nuptias intrepidi accedere. Non eiiciemur. Alioqui, extremo cum probro sumus audituri, Amice, Quomodo huc intrasti non habens vestem nuptialem? Id est, Tu qui Sacerdos & amicus meus dici vis, quo te potes ore Sacerdotem vocare? qua tu fronte nunc audes ad filij mei conuiuium venire, licet inuitatus fueris, non habens eius ordinis insigne gestamen? Suis tandem ministris dicturus est ille magnus Regu rex, Ligatis manibus & pedibus eius, mittite eum in tenebras exteriores. Ibi fletus erit, & stridor dentium. Matthei cap. 22. A nobis Deus auertat iram suam tantam.
units.tr: You see, Christian listeners, fifteen priestly garments, not all of one kind, form or colour. If we adorn ourselves with these, as we ought, if we fit them to ourselves, we have nothing to fear from the cold of snow, being clothed doubly, as Proverbs 31 bids us to be clothed. Having these wedding garments (I say), we may approach the marriage of the King without fear. We shall not be cast out. Otherwise, we shall hear with the utmost disgrace: "Friend, how did you come in here not having a wedding garment?" That is: you, who wish to be called priest and my friend, with what face can you call yourself a priest? With what brazenness do you now dare to come to the feast of my Son, though invited, not having the badge of that office? Finally that great King will say to his ministers, "Bind his hands and feet, and cast him into outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth" (Matt. 22.). May God turn away his so great wrath from us.

units.la: Iam rerum series hoc in Speculo visendarum singulatim proponatur. Dominus iesus oculos nobis aperiat, vt omnia penitissime contemplari valeamus. prima sequitur.
units.tr: Now let the order of the things to be seen in this Mirror be set forth one by one. May the Lord Jesus open our eyes, that we may be able to contemplate all things most thoroughly. The first follows.

units.la: DISTINCTIO. XXV.
units.tr: DISTINCTION XXV.

units.la: ἘΠΊΣΚΟΠΟΣ ἈΝΕΠΊΛΗΠΤΟΣ, ΚΑῚ ἈΝΈΓΚΛΗΤΟΣ.
units.tr: A BISHOP MUST BE UNSEIZABLE, AND UNCHARGEABLE. [ἐπίσκοπος ἀνεπίληπτος, καὶ ἀνέγκλητος]

units.la: In Episcopo quod inesse primū Paulus præcipit, id est, ἈΝ͂ ἢ ἐπίσκοπον ἀνεπίλημπτον εἶναι. Et, ἀξὶ ἢν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνέγκλητον εἶναι. Sic vertūt: Oportet Episcopū irreprehensibilem esse. Et, Oportet Episcopum sine crimine esse, quod idem est, authore Hieronymo. Quum verò Diaconos ipse iubet, in bona conscientia habere mysterium fidei: His verbis (ait Chrysostomus) irreprehensibiles esse debere significat, & sine crimine, siue, nullum crimen habentes. Criminis autem nomine, quodlibet peccatum intelligitur. Hieronymus ad Oceanum, circa finem Epistolæ: Nunquam, fili Oceane. To.1.
units.tr: In a bishop, the first thing Paul enjoins is that he be irreproachable, that is, [ἀνεπίλημπτον εἶναι]. And: that he be blameless [ἀνέγκλητον εἶναι]. They translate it: "A bishop must be irreproachable," and "A bishop must be without crime," which is the same thing, on the authority of Jerome. When Paul orders deacons to hold the mystery of the faith in a good conscience, by these words (says Chrysostom) he signifies that they ought to be irreproachable, and without crime, or having no crime. By "crime," however, any sin is understood. Jerome to Oceanus, near the end of the letter: "Never, son Oceanus."

units.la: Episcopus talis esse debet, vt subditis collatus, reprehensioni non sit obnoxius.
units.tr: A bishop ought to be such that, compared with those under him, he is not liable to reproach.

units.la: OMnes virtutes uno sermone comprehendit: & pe-nè rem contra naturam exigit. Si enim omne peccatum, etiam in otioso verbo, reprehensione dignum est, quis est ille, qui absque peccato, id est, sine reprehensione versetur in hoc mundo? Sed futurus pastor Ecclesiæ talis eligitur, ad cuius comparationē rectè Grex, cæteri nominētur. Idem Hieronymus in primum caput Epistolæ ad Titum. To.9.
units.tr: He sums up all the virtues in one word, and almost demands something contrary to nature. For if every sin, even an idle word, deserves reproof, who is there that lives in this world without sin, that is, without reproach? Yet the one chosen as the future minister of the Church is picked in such a way that, in comparison with him, the others are rightly called the flock. The same Jerome, on the first chapter of the Epistle to Titus.

units.la: Nullius debet infamiā peccati laborare, quisquis ad ministerium capitur Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Whoever is taken up into the ministry of the Church ought not to labour under the infamy of any sin.

units.la: PRimùm quidem, sine crimine sit Episcopus. quod alio puto verbo ad Timotheum nominari, Irreprehensibilem. Non intelligas, quòd eo tantùm tempore, quo ordinādus est, sine vllo sit crimine, quódque præteritas maculas nouâ conuersatione diluerit: sed ex eo tempore, quo in Christo renatus est, nullâ peccati conscientiâ remordeatur: Quomodo enim poterit Præses Ecclesiæ auferre malum de medio eius, qui in delictum simile corruit? Aut quâ libertate peccantem corripere poterit, quum tacitus ipse sibi respondeat, eadem se admisisse, quæ corripit? accepit pro quocunque delicto: & certè, generis vox est, cōplectens omne peccatum, quod ex deliberatione procedit: Attamen coarctant hic ad manifesta, publicáque tantùm, quæ pro tribunali digna sint accusatione, atque damna- tione, quorúmque perpetua est infamia.
units.tr: First of all, the bishop must be without crime, which in another word is called to Timothy "irreproachable." Do not understand this to mean only that he is without any fault at the time he is to be ordained, and that he has washed away past stains by a new way of life; rather, from the time he was reborn in Christ, he should not be troubled by any consciousness of sin. For how will the president of the Church be able to remove evil from its midst if he himself has fallen into a similar offence? Or with what freedom will he rebuke a sinner, when he silently answers himself that he has committed the very things he rebukes? Jerome takes it to mean any offence; and certainly it is a general term, embracing every sin that proceeds from deliberate choice. Nevertheless, they here restrict it to manifest and public sins only, those which are worthy of accusation and condemnation before the tribunal, and whose infamy is lasting.

units.la: LXXXJ. Distinctione. Can. 1.
units.tr: Distinction 81. Canon 1.

units.la: Augustinus Tractatu 41. in Euangelium Ioannis. To.9.
units.tr: Augustine, Tractate 41 on the Gospel of John, vol. 9.

units.la: Omne crimen est peccatum: sed non omne Peccatum est crimen. Ipse idem Augustinus hoc habet in cap.64. Enchiridij. To 3.
units.tr: Every crime is a sin, but not every sin is a crime. Augustine himself has this in chapter 64 of the Enchiridion, vol. 3.

units.la: A Postolus Paulus (quando elegit ordinandos vel Presbyteros, vel Diaconos, & quicunque ordinandus est ad Præposituram Ecclesiæ) non ait: Si quis sine peccato est (Hoc enim si diceret, omnis homo reprobaretur, nullus ordinaretur) Sed ait, Si quis sine crimine est: sicut est homicidium, adulterium, aliqua immunditia, fornicationes, furtum, fraus, sacrilegium, & cætera huiusmodi. Crimen enim est peccatum graue, accusatione & damnatione dignissimum. Gratianus: Ecce. Quisquis ordinandus est in Episcopū, non solùm suæ ordinationis tempore, sed etiam omni tempore post Baptismā, debet à crimine immunis esse. Deinde Gratianus aggreditur secundum, quod est in Apostolo, volens ostendere, quòd, Si forte Maritus aliquis ordinetur, Ordinandus est vnius duntaxat uxoris vir.
units.tr: The Apostle Paul, when he chooses those to be ordained, whether presbyters or deacons, or anyone who is to be ordained to the leadership of the Church, does not say: "If anyone is without sin." (For if he said that, every man would be rejected and no one would be ordained.) Rather he says: "If anyone is without crime," such as homicide, adultery, some impurity, fornication, theft, fraud, sacrilege, and other things of this kind. For a crime is a grave sin, most worthy of accusation and condemnation. Gratian: Behold. Whoever is to be ordained bishop must be free from crime not only at the time of his ordination but also at every time after baptism. Then Gratian turns to the second point, which is in the Apostle, wishing to show that if perhaps some married man is ordained, the one to be ordained must be a man of only one wife.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXVI.
units.tr: DISTINCTIO XXVI.

units.la: Sequitur in utraque Epistola.
units.tr: It follows in both Epistles.

units.la: ΜΙΑΣ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΟΣ ἈΝΔΡΑ.
units.tr: Of one wife a man [μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἀνδρα].

units.la: Vnius uxoris virum. Gratianus: Post Baptisma, videlicet, non ante Baptismum.
units.tr: "Husband of one wife": Gratian: that is, after baptism, not before baptism.

units.la: Duobus in locis Gratianus problema disputandum proposuit, Habendus ne sit Digamus is, qui, vnam, antequam baptizaretur, alteram verò post lavacrum, priore mortuâ, duxit uxorē: scilicet, in hac xxvi distinctione, et in quaestione tertia causæ vigesimæ octavæ. Virinque more suo disputans, eadem citat. Errans tamen (vt nimium saepe solet) iu authorum titulis Quòd in Digamiam non incurrat ille secundò marītus, probatur. Hieronymus enim scribit ad Oceanum.
units.tr: In two places Gratian proposed a question for debate: whether a man should be counted a digamist if he took one wife before he was baptized and, after the washing, when the first had died, took another. That is, in this twenty-sixth distinction and in question three of cause twenty-eight. Arguing both sides in his usual way, he cites the same authorities. Erring, however (as he very often does), in the titles of the authors, he proves that a man who marries a second time does not fall into digamy. For Jerome writes to Oceanus:

units.la: Ministro futuro non obstat Digamia, quæ post Baptismum non contrahitur.
units.tr: Digamy, which is not contracted after baptism, is no obstacle to a future minister.

units.la: VNius uxoris viru̅,id est, Monogamum post Baptismum: Nam si coniugem prius habuerit, quæ & obierit, A baptismo repetitæ nuptiæ non imputantur ei. Cui prorsus novo homini, nec stupra, nec alia, quæ ante fuerunt, amplius obsunt. Hæc Hieronymi quidem sententia, multis ab eodem rationibus nec uno loco defensa, quas Gratianus hic omisit. Contrà sentit Augustinus in.18. cap. libri De bono coniugali. To.6.
units.tr: "Husband of one wife," that is, a monogamist after baptism. For if he had a wife earlier, and she has died, the remarriage is not charged against him from the time of baptism. For to the new man, neither fornications nor other things that were before do any further harm. This is indeed the opinion of Jerome, defended by many arguments from him and not in one place only, which Gratian has omitted here. On the contrary, Augustine holds in chapter 18 of the book On the Good of Marriage, vol. 6.

units.la: Vnam qui duxerit ante Baptismum: Postque Baptisnům duxerit alteram, non est ordinandus, quia Digamus.
units.tr: Whoever took one wife before baptism, and after baptism took another, is not to be ordained, because he is a digamist.

units.la: A Cutiùs hoc intellexerůt, qui nec eum, qui Catechumenus, vel Paganus habuerit alteram, ordinandum esse censuerunt: De Sacramento enim agitur, non de peccato: Nam in Baptismo, peccata omnia dimittuntur. Sed qui dixit,— Si acceperis uxorẽ, non peccasti: &, Si nupserit virgo, non peccat: &, Quod vult faciat, non peccat, si nubat: Satis declarauit nuptias nullum esse peccatum. Propter Sacramenti autem sanctitatem, sicut fœmina, etiamsi Catechumena fuerit vitiata, non potest post Baptismum inter Dei virgines consecrari: Ita non absurdè visum est, eum qui excessit uxorum numerum singularem, non peccatum aliquod commisisse, sed normam quandam Sacramenti amisisse, non ad vitæ bonæ meritum, sed ad ordinationis Ecclesiasticæ signaculum, necessariam.
units.tr: Others have understood this more narrowly, who have judged that a catechumen or a pagan who had taken a second wife should not be ordained either. For the matter concerns a sacrament, not a sin: in baptism all sins are forgiven. But he who said, "If you take a wife, you have not sinned," and "If a virgin marries, she does not sin," and "Let him do what he wishes; if he marries, he does not sin," sufficiently declared that marriage is no sin. But because of the holiness of the sacrament, just as a woman, even if she was violated while a catechumen, cannot after baptism be consecrated among the virgins of God, so it has seemed not unreasonable that a man who has exceeded the single number of wives has committed no sin, but has lost a certain norm of the sacrament, which is necessary not for the merit of a good life but for the seal of ecclesiastical ordination.

units.la: Vt allegorica fuit in antiquæ legis Patriarchis uxorum multitudo: Sic est & vnius in nostris.
units.tr: As the multitude of wives was allegorical among the patriarchs of the ancient law, so also is the unity of one wife among us.

units.la: §. Ac per hoc, sicut plures uxores antiquorum patrum significauerunt futuras nostras ex omnibus gentibus Ecclesias, uni viro subditas Christo: ita nostér Antistes unius uxoris vir, significat ex omnibus gentibus unitatem, uni viro subditam Christo: quæ tunc perficietur, quum revelaverit occulta tenebrarum, & manifestaverit cogitationes cordis, & tunc laus erit unicuique à Deo.
units.tr: §. And so, just as the many wives of the ancient fathers signified our churches to come, from all nations, subject to Christ as one husband, so our bishop, the husband of one wife, signifies the unity from all nations, subject to Christ as one husband. This will be perfected when he reveals the hidden things of darkness and makes manifest the thoughts of the heart, and then there will be praise for each one from God.

units.la: Item. Innocentius papa Romæ 1. in cap. 2. Epistolæ suæ 22. quam scripsit ad Episcopos Macedoniæ, Constantio Consule, id est, anno Christi 416. Videtur hæc instituta fuisse disputatio contra Hieronymi: quod deprehendas ex sæpe citata Epistola ad Oceanum: sed antequam foret ille Papa.
units.tr: Likewise. Pope Innocent at Rome, in chapter 2 of his letter 22, which he wrote to the bishops of Macedonia in the consulship of Constantius, that is, in the year of Christ 416. This argument seems to have been set up against Jerome, as you may gather from the often-cited letter to Oceanus, but before he became pope.

units.la: Culpa remittitur in Baptismo: Lex verò naturæ, vel coniugij non aboletur.
units.tr: Guilt is remitted in baptism, but the law of nature, or of marriage, is not abolished.

units.la: DEinde ponitur: Non dici oportere Digamum eum, qui Catechumenus habuerit & amiserit uxorem, si post Baptismum fuerit aliam sortitus: eámque primam videri, quæ novo homini copulata sit: quia illud coiugium per Baptismi sacramentum cum cæteris criminibus sit ablatum. Quòd cùm de una utique dicitur: certè si tres habuerit in veteri positus homine uxores, erit ei, quæ post Baptismum quarta est, sic interpretantibus, prima. Virginis æque nomen accipiet, quæ quarto loco ducta est. Quis (oro) istud non videat contra Apostoli esse præceptum, qui ait, Vnius uxoris virum oportere fieri sacerdote? Sed obiicitur, Quòd in Baptismo totum, quicquid in veteri homine gestu est, sit totum. Dicite mihi (cum pace vestra loquar) an crimina tantùm dimittuntur in Baptismo: an & illa, quæ secundum Dei præcepta ac Dei instituta complentur? Vxorem ducere, crimen est, an non est crimen? Si crimen est, ergo (præfatâ veniâ dixerim) erit author in culpa: qui, ut crimina committerentur, in paradiso præcepit, cùm ipse eos benedixit. Si verò non est crimen: quia, quod Deus instituit, nefas est crimen appellari: & Salomon addidit: Etenim à Deo præparatur viro uxor: quomodo creditur inter crimina esse dimissum, quod Deo authore legitur consummatum?
units.tr: Next it is laid down that he should not be called a digamist who, as a catechumen, had a wife and lost her, if after baptism he obtained another; and that the first is taken to be the one joined to the new man, because that marriage was removed along with the other crimes by the sacrament of baptism. Since this is said of one wife, certainly if, while in the old man, he had three wives, the one who is fourth after baptism will, on this interpretation, be the first. She will receive the name of virgin, though she was taken in fourth place. Who (I beg) does not see that this is against the precept of the Apostle, who says that a bishop must be the husband of one wife? But it is objected that in baptism everything that was done in the old man is wholly done away. Tell me (with your leave I speak) whether in baptism only crimes are forgiven, or also those things which are fulfilled according to the precepts and institutions of God? Is taking a wife a crime or not? If it is a crime, then (I say this with pardon) the author is in the guilt: he who commanded them, in paradise, to be multiplied, when he himself blessed them. But if it is not a crime, because what God has instituted cannot rightly be called a crime, and Solomon added, "For a wife is prepared for a man by the Lord," how is it believed that what is read to have been accomplished under God as author is forgiven among the crimes?

units.la: Euangeliū christi, Nuptias & Successiones hæreditarias, vti naturales ac legitimas, inter gentiles approbat.
units.tr: The Gospel of Christ approves, among the Gentiles, marriages and hereditary successions as natural and lawful.

units.la: §. Quid de talium filiis censetur? nunquid non erūt admittendi in hæreditatis consortium, qui ex ea suscepti sunt, quæ ante Baptismum fuit vxor? erúntque appellandi vel Naturales, vel Spurij? quia non est legitimum matrimonium, nisi illud (ut nobis videtur) quod post Baptismum assumitur. Ipse Deus, cū interrogaretur à Iudæis, si liceret vxorem dimittere: atque exponeret fieri non debere, addidit: Quos Deus coniunxit, homo non separet. An ne de his locutus esse credatur, qui vxores post Baptismum sortiuntur? Meminerint & hoc à Iudæis interrogatum, & etiam Iudæis esse responsum.
units.tr: §. What is to be thought of the sons of such men? Will not those who were born of the wife who was before baptism be admitted to share the inheritance? Are they to be called either natural or bastards, because the marriage is not lawful except that which (as it seems to us) is entered upon after baptism? God himself, when he was asked by the Jews whether it was lawful to dismiss a wife, and explained that it should not be done, added: "What God has joined together, let not man put asunder." Or is he believed to have spoken of those who obtain wives after baptism? Let them recall that this too was asked by the Jews, and that it was answered to the Jews as well.

units.la: Frater gentilis cum fratre Christiano paternam diuidit hæreditatem.
units.tr: A gentile brother divides the paternal inheritance with a Christian brother.

units.la: §. Quæro, & solicitus quæro, Si una eademque sit vxor eius, qui ante Catechumenus, postea Fidelis: filiósque ex ea, quum esset Cathecumenus suscepit: & postea alios filios cùm sit Fidelis, Vtrum sint fratres appellandi? an non habeant postea, defuncto patre, Ercisçundæ hæreditatis consortium, quibus filiorum nomen regeneratio spiritualis creditur abstulisse? quod cùm ita sentire absurdum est: quæ ratio est hoc defendi, & vacuâ magis opinione iactari, quàm aliquâ authoritate roborari? quum non possit inter peccata deputari, quod lex præcepit, quod Deus iunxit, & Lex iungit.
units.tr: §. I ask, and anxiously ask: if one and the same wife belonged to a man who was first a catechumen and afterwards a believer, and he had sons by her while he was a catechumen, and afterwards other sons while he was a believer, are they to be called brothers, or do they not, after their father's death, share the inheritance, when spiritual regeneration is believed to have taken from them the name of sons? Since it is absurd to think so, what reason is there for defending this, and for being tossed about by empty opinion rather than strengthened by any authority, since what the law commands, what God has joined, and what the Law joins, cannot be counted among sins?

units.la: Virtutis opus Infideli demum prodest, si conuertatur ad fidem. nec secunda coniugis sortiri coniunctionem. Quod plerisque mirum videtur: cur etiam ante Baptismum iterato coniugio, electionis muneris, & praerogativae ordinationis, impedimenta generentur: quum delicta obesse non soleat, si lavacri remissa fuerint Sacramento. Sed intelligere debemus, quia in Baptismo, culpa dimitti potest, Lex aboleri non potest. In coniugio non culpa, sed Lex est quod culpae est igitur, in Baptismo relaxatur: quod Legis est, in coniugio non soluitur. Quomodo autem potest esse hortator viduitatis, qui & ipse coniugia frequentaverit?
units.tr: The work of virtue benefits the unbeliever only if he turns to the faith; nor does a second marriage obtain the conjunction of a wife. This seems strange to most people: why, even before baptism, should impediments to the office of election and the prerogative of ordination arise from a second marriage, when sins do not usually stand in the way if they have been remitted by the sacrament of the washing? But we ought to understand that in baptism guilt can be forgiven, while law cannot be abolished. In marriage it is not guilt but law; what belongs to guilt is therefore relaxed in baptism, but what belongs to law is not dissolved in marriage. How, moreover, can he be an encourager of widowhood who has himself frequented marriages?

units.la: hic inter ethnicos coniugia vera fuisse docet, adhuc alia ex Evangelio depromptâ authoritate.
units.tr: Here he teaches that among the heathen marriages were true, and adds another authority drawn from the Gospel.

units.la: IOannes Baptista, dum Herodem ab incestu prohiberet, dicens: Non licet tibi habere uxorem fratris tui: Euidenter ostendit inter Infideles coniugia esse. Unde datur intelligi quòd Digami dicuntur, non solùm qui post Baptisma coniugia frequentant, sed etiam qui ante Baptisinum unam, & post Baptismum alteram habuisse probantur. Digamus verò in sacerdotem ordinari non debet, non quia deliquerit, secundam accipiendo uxorem, sed quia praerogativa exutus est sacerdotis. Unde Ambrosius in Epistola 82. libro 10. ad Vercellensem Ecclesiam ait.
units.tr: John the Baptist, when he forbade Herod from incest, saying, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife," clearly showed that marriages existed among unbelievers. Whence it is understood that men are called digamists not only if they keep up marriages after baptism, but also if they are shown to have had one wife before baptism and another after it. A digamist, however, ought not to be ordained a priest, not because he has sinned by taking a second wife, but because he has been stripped of the prerogative of the priesthood. Hence Ambrose, in Epistle 82, book 10, to the church of Vercelli, says:

units.la: Non est inquinatus Digamus: non tamen est ad Sacerdotium mundus.
units.tr: A digamist is not defiled; yet he is not clean for the priesthood.

units.la: QVi sine crimine, Vnius uxoris est vir, tenetur ad legem sacerdotij suscipiendi, Qui autem iterauerit coniugium, culpam quidem non habet coinquinati, sed praerogativa exuitur sacerdotis. Ergo dispensatorem Ecclesiae non licet ordinari, nisi vnius uxoris virum, Christiane Sacerdos, Caue, ne cum nuptiatoribus Gnosticis exîstimes hoc esse verbum sancientis, quasi non liceat Episcopum fieri, qui suam non circunducat uxorem. Taccho de caeteris Apostolis, omnibus fere virginibus, aut caelibus: Ipse Paulus non fuisset Episcopus. Non ergo legem, sed modum ponit. Vt si contigeris à seculi rebus ad hoc caelestè munus quempiam vocari, sit ille Monogamus, Haec omnium, ne vno quidem contradicente, veterum sententiis patrum. De qua nos in Canonib. Apostolorum, & in subsequentibus adhuc distinctionibus.
units.tr: He who is without crime, the husband of one wife, is bound by the law of taking up the priesthood; but he who has renewed a marriage does not have the guilt of defilement, yet is stripped of the prerogative of the priesthood. Therefore it is not lawful to ordain a steward of the Church except a husband of one wife, Christian priest; beware lest you think, with the Gnostic despisers of marriage, that this is the word of one who forbids, as if it were not permitted to become a bishop who does not lead about his own wife. Leaving aside the other apostles, nearly all virgins or celibates, Paul himself would not have been a bishop. He therefore lays down not a law but a measure: that if you are called from worldly affairs to some such heavenly office, he should be a monogamist. This is the opinion of all the ancient fathers, with no one contradicting. We treat of it in the Canons of the Apostles, and in the distinctions that follow.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXVII.
units.tr: DISTINCTION XXVII.

units.la: Gratianus, QVOD autem, Vnius vxoris vir, Episcopus iubetur eligi: quæritur, An de tempore ordinationis hoc sit accipiendum? Vt tempore suæ administrationis, eius posset copula frui, quam vnicam & virginem sibi desponsauit. Hoc Martinus papa prohibet: Quo tempore Martinus primus sedem Romanam tenebat, anno circiter 647. Pontifex & doctrina & sanctitate vitæ celebris, alius quidam Martinus in Portugallia Braccharum Episcopus (nunc Braga, metropolis) e Synodis Græcè conscriptis octoginta quinque canones selegit, & Latinè vertit. Is vnus esse potuit ex illu centum & quinque occidentalibus Episcopis, quos Martinus papa Romam vocarat ad Synodum, contra Sergium, & Pyrrum Constantinopolitanos hæreticos. In qua fortè Synodo quum probati canones illi fuissent, ob nominis similitudinem, & approbationem synodicam, citantur & eius nomine concilij, & Martini papæ titulo. Quum reuera dicendum sit, ex Cōcilijs, vel, ex Canonibus Martini Bracchariensis (quos habes in Tomo 2. Conciliorum) Nisi dicere mauis, Episcopos omnes olim solitos appellari Papas. quod in Exegesis prodo dicebamus. Canon præsens inter eos est. 39. Hoc semel annotatum esto pro talibus inscriptionibus obuiis hic frequenter. Sic dicit Papa Martinus.
units.tr: Gratian: But as to the words "the husband of one wife," which require that a bishop be chosen, the question is whether this is to be understood of the time of his ordination, so that in the time of his administration he may enjoy the marital union with the one wife, a virgin, whom he betrothed. Pope Martin forbids this. In the time when Martin I held the Roman see, about the year 647, a pontiff celebrated for his learning and holiness of life, another Martin, bishop of Braga in Portugal (now Braga, a metropolis), selected eighty-five canons from synods written in Greek and translated them into Latin. He could have been one of the one hundred and five western bishops whom Pope Martin summoned to Rome to a synod against the Constantinopolitan heretics Sergius and Pyrrhus. Perhaps in that synod, when those canons were approved, and because of the similarity of the name and the synodal approval, they are cited both under the name of the council and under the title of Pope Martin. Yet it must really be said that they come from the Councils, or from the canons of Martin of Braga (which you have in volume 2 of the Councils), unless you prefer to say that all bishops were once customarily called popes, as I said in the Exegesis. The present canon is among them, number 39. Let this be noted once for all, since such inscriptions occur frequently here. Thus Pope Martin says:

units.la: Diaconus non ordinetur, qui Castitatem non profitetur.
units.tr: A deacon is not to be ordained who does not profess chastity.

units.la: DIaconus, qui eligitur, si contestatus fuerit pro accipiendo matrimonio: & dixerit se in castitate non posse manere, hic non ordinetur. Quod si in ordinatione tacuerit, & ordinatus fuerit, & postea matrimonium desiderauerit: sit alienus à ministerio, & vacet à clero. Gratianus. Hac authoritate datur intelligi, quod illi qui vxores habet, vel accipere volut, nec Diaconi nec Sacerdotes fieri possunt, nisi continentiam profiteantur: 'Si vero Diaconus à ministerio cessare voluerit, contracto matrimonio licitè potest vti. Nam etsi in ordinatione sua castitatis votum obtulerit, tamen tanta est vis in Sacramento coniugij, quòd nec ex latione voti, potest dissolui ipsum coniugium. In quæstionem venit, an vota castitas impediat matrimonium? Nec impedire plane sentit Augustinus in libro de bono viduitatis, scribens ad Iulianam Dei famulam. cap. 9. 10. & 11. To. 4. Gratianus ex locis illis canonem suum collegit sic habentem.
units.tr: A deacon who is chosen, if he has declared that he wishes to take a wife, and has said that he cannot remain in chastity, let him not be ordained. But if he kept silent at his ordination, and was ordained, and afterwards desires marriage, let him be removed from the ministry and deprived of the clergy. Gratian: By this authority it is shown that those who have wives, or wish to take them, cannot become deacons or priests unless they profess continence. "But if a deacon wishes to cease from the ministry, he may lawfully use marriage once contracted. For although in his ordination he offered a vow of chastity, nevertheless the power of the sacrament of marriage is so great that the marriage itself cannot be dissolved even by the taking of a vow." The question arises whether a vow of chastity hinders marriage? Augustine clearly does not think it does, in his book On the Good of Widowhood, writing to Juliana, the servant of God, chapters 9, 10 and 11, volume 4. From those passages Gratian gathered his canon, which reads thus:

units.la: Nuptiæ post votum contractæ, non sunt distrahendæ.
units.tr: Marriages contracted after a vow are not to be dissolved.

units.la: QVidam nubentes post votum asserunt adulteras esse: ego autem dico vobis, quòd graviter peccant, qui tales diuidunt. Item. Theodorus in pœnitentiali. Theodorus papa Romæ sedebat humanæ salutis anno 641. qui de modo & qualitate pœnitentiæ librum composuisse dicitur, inscriptum, Pœnitentiale Theodori. Quem librum nonnulli referunt ad alium Theodorum, Archiepiscopum Cantuariensem, Vitaliani papæ tempore, videlicet, anno 670 Non extat, quod sciam. Sæpe tamen citatur ab antiquis Ecclesiasticorum Decretorum compilatoribus, qui nunquam Papæ nomen addunt, vt solent in alijs.
units.tr: Some who marry after a vow claim that they are adulterers; but I tell you that those who separate such people sin grievously. Likewise, Theodore in the Penitential. Pope Theodore sat at Rome in the year of human salvation 641; he is said to have composed a book on the measure and quality of penance, entitled the Penitential of Theodore. Some refer this book to another Theodore, Archbishop of Canterbury, in the time of Pope Vitalian, that is, in 670. It does not survive, so far as I know. Yet it is often cited by the ancient compilers of ecclesiastical decrees, who never add the title of Pope, as they usually do in other cases.

units.la: Si
units.tr: If

units.la: SI vir Votum virginitatis habens, adiungitur Vxori, postea non dimittat uxorem: sed tribus annis poenitneat. Hinc videtur, quòd matrimonio contrahendo non obstat votum continentiae. Neque propter solutum votum, soluitur & coniugium. Sed aliud videtur authoritatibus contrariis asserendum. Ex eodem nempe Augustino colligitur in supradictio cap. 9.
units.tr: If a man who has taken a vow of virginity is joined to a wife, he must not afterwards put away his wife, but must do penance for three years. Hence it seems that the vow of continence does not stand in the way of contracting marriage. Nor is the marriage dissolved because the vow was dissolved. But the opposite view seems to be asserted by other authorities. Indeed, from the same Augustine a conclusion is drawn in the chapter cited above, number 9.

units.la: Damnabilis est, post votum continentiae, vel solus nubendi voluntas.
units.tr: After a vow of continence, even the mere will to marry is blameworthy.

units.la: VOuentibus virginitatem, nō solùm nubere, sed etiam velle, damnabile est. Item. Hieronymus libro primo contra Iouinianum.
units.tr: For those who vow virginity, it is blameworthy not only to marry but even to wish to marry. Likewise Jerome, in the first book against Jovinian.

units.la: Damnanda est virgo nubens post votum virginitatem.
units.tr: A virgin who marries after a vow of virginity is to be condemned.

units.la: SI nupserit virgo, non peccauit. Non illa virgo quae semet Dei cultui dedicauit. Harum enim si qua nupserit, habebit damnationem, quia primam fidem irritam fecit. Si quis autem de viduis hoc dictum obiecerit, quanto magis de virginibus praevalebit, quum etiam his non liceat, quibus aliquando licuit?
units.tr: If a virgin has married, she has not sinned, provided she is not one who has dedicated herself to the worship of God. For if any of these has married, she will incur condemnation, because she has made void her first pledge. But if anyone should object this saying about widows, how much more will it prevail over virgins, since it is not lawful even for those for whom it was once lawful?

units.la: Item. Nicolaus Papa, ad Adaluuinum sanctae Viuacensis Ecclesiae Archiepiscopum. ΝΑΛΑΔ ex Iuonis Pannomiae libro tertio, cap. De virginibus, viduis & abbatissis. Hunc puto fuisse Nicolaum 2. de quo nos in distinct. 31. Gratianus, & Iuo (qui non raro citabitur hic) fere aequales annis, utrque sub Innocentio 2. Primum fuit Iuo Praefectus Ecclesiae S. Quintini in Viromanduis, postea electus in Episcopum Carnotensem. Pannomiae compilator. Indidit hunc titulum libro, quo varios priscorum patrum Canones compendiose conclusit, anno circiter 1136. Nam citat Iuo ipsius Innocentij secundi decreta, qui creatus fuit Pontifex anno Dn. 1130. Gratianus autem scripsit, anno salutis 1150.
units.tr: Likewise Pope Nicholas, to Adalwin, archbishop of the holy church of Vienne, from Ivo's Pannomia, book three, the chapter "On virgins, widows and abbesses." I think this was Nicholas II, whom we cite in distinction 31. Gratian and Ivo (who will often be cited here) were nearly contemporaries, both under Innocent II. Ivo was first provost of the church of St Quentin in Vermandois, and afterwards was elected bishop of Chartres. He was the compiler of the Pannomia. He gave this title to the book in which he concisely gathered the various canons of the ancient Fathers, around the year 1136. For Ivo cites the decrees of Innocent II himself, who was made pope in the year of the Lord 1130. Gratian, however, wrote in the year of salvation 1150.

units.la: Omnem fictionem religionis, & hypocrisin Sacramentorum, Canones improbant.
units.tr: The canons condemn every feigning of religion and the hypocrisy of the sacraments.

units.la: QVod interrogasti de foemina, quae post obitum mariti sui, sacrum velamen super caput suum imposuit, & finxit se sub eodem velamine Sanctimonialem esse, postea vero ad nuptias rediit. bonum mihi videtur: quia per hypocrisin, ecclesiasticam regulam conturbare voluit, & non D legitimè in voto suo permansit, vt pœnitentiam agat de illusione nefanda, & reuertatur ad id, quod spopondit, & in sacro ministerio permaneat, quod inchoauit. Nam, si consenserimus, quòd omnia Sacramenta ecclesiastica quisque, prout vult, fingat, & non verè faciat, omnis ordo Ecclesiasticus turbabitur: nec catholicæ fidei Iura consistunt, nec Canones sacri ritè obseruantur. Quid enim profuit Simoni Mago Baptismum sacrum fictè suscipere, & in Christianitate se permansurum finxisse, quum per Apostolum, fraude eius detectâ, quid sibi futurum esset pronunciatum fuit? Ait enim: Pecunia tua tecum sit in perditionem: cor enim tuum non est rectum coram Deo. Pœnitentiam itaque age de hac iniquitate tua, & roga Deum, vt forte remittantur tibi cogitationes cordis tui. In felle enim amaritudinis, & obligatione iniquitatis video te esse. Ideo tales, nisi resipiscant, spirituali gladio percutere censemus. Non enim fas est Spiritui sancto mentiri, sicut Ananias & Saphira mentiti sunt, & statim perierunt.
units.tr: As to what you asked about the woman who, after the death of her husband, placed the sacred veil upon her head and pretended to be a nun under that same veil, and afterwards returned to marriage: it seems good to me, since through hypocrisy she wished to upset the ecclesiastical rule, and did not remain lawfully in her vow. Let her do penance for the abominable deception, return to what she promised, and remain in the sacred ministry that she began. For if we agree that each person may pretend, as he wishes, to the ecclesiastical sacraments without truly performing them, the whole ecclesiastical order will be thrown into confusion: the laws of the Catholic faith will not stand, and the sacred canons will not be duly observed. For what did it profit Simon Magus to receive holy baptism feignedly, and to have pretended that he would remain in Christianity, when, once his deceit was detected by the Apostle, it was declared what would become of him? For he says: "Let your money perish with you, because your heart is not right before God. Repent therefore of this your wickedness, and pray God that perhaps the thoughts of your heart may be forgiven you. For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and the bond of iniquity." Therefore we judge that such persons, unless they come to their senses, are to be struck with the spiritual sword. For it is not right to lie to the Holy Spirit, as Ananias and Sapphira lied, and at once they perished.

units.la: Item Calixtus Papa. Dum cum suis, Theutonicus rex Henricus quintus ad Ecclesiæ Romanæ ritus & vnionem rediisset, Calixtus tum Papa Romæ 2.ita constituit, anno Domini circiter 1120.
units.tr: Likewise Pope Callixtus. When Henry V, king of the Germans, had returned with his people to the rites and unity of the Roman Church, Callixtus, then pope at Rome, decreed as follows, in the year of the Lord about 1120.

units.la: In Sacris ordinibus constituti non ducant vxores: & si duxerint, à ductis separarentur. Concubinas non habeant.
units.tr: Those who are established in holy orders shall not take wives; and if they have taken them, they shall be separated from those they took. They shall not have concubines.

units.la: PResbyteris, Diaconis, Subdiaconis, & Monachis concubinas habere, seu matrimonia contrahere, penitus interdicimus: contracta quóque matrimonia ab huiusmodi personis, disiungi, & personas ad pœnitentiam redigi debere, iuxta sacrorum Canonum diffinitionem iudicamus. Gratianus. Hic distinguendum est, quòd Voucntium alij sunt simpliciter vouentes: de quibus Augustinus, & Theodorus locuti sunt: Alij sunt, quibus post votum, Benedictio accedit consecrationis, vel Propositum religionis: de quibus idem Augustinus, & Hieronymus, & Nicolaus, & Calixtus scripserunt. Unde Hieronymus idem libro nunc citato dixit.
units.tr: We absolutely forbid presbyters, deacons, subdeacons and monks to keep concubines or to contract marriages; and we judge that marriages contracted by such persons must be dissolved, and the persons brought to penance, according to the definition of the sacred canons. Gratian. Here a distinction must be made: some of those who vow are simply vowing, and of them Augustine and Theodore spoke; others are those to whom, after the vow, the blessing of consecration or the profession of religious life is added, and of these the same Augustine, and Jerome, and Nicholas, and Callixtus wrote. Whence Jerome, in the same book just cited, said:

units.la: Incestuosæ sunt Nonnarum nuptiæ.
units.tr: The marriages of nuns are incestuous.

units.la: VIrgines, quæ post consecrationem nupserint, non tam adulteræ sunt, quàm incestæ. Concludas. Solemne votum nuptiis obstat: Simplex minimè.
units.tr: Virgins who have married after consecration are not so much adulterous as incestuous. Conclude thus: A solemn vow stands in the way of marriage; a simple vow by no means does.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXVIII.
units.tr: DISTINCTION XXVIII.

units.la: Gratianus. ECCE. Ostensum est breviter, quòd nolentes vouere continentiam, nec ad subdiaconatum, nec ad superiores gradus conscendere possunt. Unde ad Subdiaconatus accedentes, non sine voto castitatis iubentur admitti, authoritate beati Gregorij, qui scribens Petro Subdiacono, Epistolâ 41. libro primo, ait. Gregorius papa primus, ex Monacho S. Benedicti, Pontificatum gerere cœpit, paulò post annum Do. 590. Moritur anno 2. Phocæ Imperatoris, id est, anno 605. Benedictus Cassini montis abbas claruit anno Do. 534. Totiâ vastante Italiam.
units.tr: Gratian. Behold. It has been shown briefly that those who are unwilling to vow continence can neither ascend to the subdiaconate nor to the higher orders. Hence those who approach the subdiaconate are ordered to be admitted not without a vow of chastity, on the authority of the blessed Gregory, who, writing to Peter the subdeacon, says in Epistle 41 of the first book: Gregory the first pope began to hold the pontificate, having come from being a monk of St Benedict, shortly after the year of the Lord 590. He died in the second year of the emperor Phocas, that is, in the year 605. Benedict, abbot of Monte Cassino, flourished in the year of the Lord 534, while all Italy was being laid waste.

units.la: Ab Hypodiaconis, etiam Græcis, Gregorius exigi castitatem voluit.
units.tr: Gregory wished chastity to be demanded also from the Greek hypodeacons.

units.la: NVllum facere Subdiaconum præsumat Episcopi, nisi qui se castè victurum promiserit: quia nullus ad ministerium altaris accedere debet, nisi cuius castitas ante susceptum ministerium fuerit approbata. Item. Ex Concilio Toletano. 2. ca. 1. circiter annum Do. 530. Ioanne. 2. Papâ.
units.tr: Let no bishop presume to make a subdeacon unless he has promised that he will live chastely, because no one ought to approach the ministry of the altar unless his chastity has been approved before he has received the ministry. Likewise, from the Second Council of Toledo, chapter 1, about the year of the Lord 530, under Pope John II.

units.la: A primis pueribus annis, ad octavum decimum usque probari debent Ecclesiæ futuri ministri: psalmis, & lectionibus exerceri: postea castitatem pollicentes, nec aliter, Hypodiaconi possunt fieri.
units.tr: From their earliest boyhood, up to their eighteenth year, future ministers of the Church ought to be tested and exercised in the psalms and lessons; afterwards, pledging chastity, and not otherwise, they may be made hypodeacons.

units.la: DEhis, quos voluntas patentum à primis infantiæ annis in Clericatus officio, vel Monachali posuit, id statuimus observandum. Vt mox quum detonsi, vel ministerio lectorum contraditi fuerint, in domo Ecclesiæ sub Episcopali præsentia, à Præposito sibi debeant erudiri. At ubi octavum decimum ætatis suæ compleuerint annum, coram totius Cleri, Plebísque cóspectu, voluntas eorum de expetendo coniugio ab Episcopo perscrutetur: quibus, si gratia castitatis, Deo inspirante, placuerit, & promissionem castimoniæ suæ absque coniugali necessitate sese sponderint seruaturos, hi, tanquam appetitores arctissimæ viæ, leuissimo Domini iugo subdantur: Ac primùm, Subdiaconi ministerium, habitâ probatione professionis suæ, à vicesimo anno suscipiant. Quòd si inculpabiliter ac inoffensè. XX. & V. annum peregerint, ad Diaconi officium (si scientes adimplere id posse ab Episcopo probantur) promoueri debent. Cauendum est tamen his, ne quãdo suæ sponsionis immemores, aut ad terrenas nuptias, aut ad furtiuos concubitus ultro concurrant: quod si forte fecerint, vt sacrilegii rei, ab Ecclesia habeantur extranei. Quibus autem voluntas propria, interrogationis tempore, desiderium nubendi persuaserit, concessam ab Apostolo licentiam auferre non possumus. Ita, vt quum provectæ ætatis in coniugio positi, renuntiaturos se pari consensu operibus carnis sponderint, ad Sacros ordines aspirent. Item Innocentius secundus. In Panomiæ libro octauo, cap. vlti. refertur hoc decretum, ex cap. 5. Synodi cuiusdam Romanæ, sub Innocentio 2. habitæ, circiter annum Do. 1131.
units.tr: Concerning those whom the will of their parents placed from their earliest infancy in the office of the clergy or in monastic life, we decree that this be observed: that as soon as they have been tonsured, or committed to the ministry of readers, they are to be educated by the provost in the house of the Church, under the presence of the bishop. But when they have completed their eighteenth year, in the sight of the whole clergy and people, the bishop is to examine their will regarding the desire for marriage. To those whom the grace of chastity, God inspiring it, has pleased, and who pledge that they will keep the promise of their chastity without any marital necessity, let these, as seekers of the most narrow way, be brought under the lightest yoke of the Lord. And first, after their profession has been tested, let them receive the ministry of subdeacon from their twentieth year. But if they have passed their twenty-fifth year blamelessly and without offence, they ought to be promoted to the office of deacon, provided that the bishop finds that they know they can fulfil it. Yet these men must be cautioned, lest at some time, forgetful of their promise, they rush headlong either into earthly marriage or into furtive concubinage; if perhaps they do so, they are to be held by the Church as strangers, as guilty of sacrilege. But to those whose own will, at the time of questioning, has persuaded them to desire marriage, we cannot take away the permission granted by the Apostle. So that, when those who have entered marriage at an advanced age have pledged that they will with equal consent renounce the works of the flesh, they may aspire to the sacred orders. Likewise Innocent II. This decree is cited in the eighth book of the Panormia, last chapter, from chapter 5 of a certain Roman synod held under Innocent II, about the year of the Lord 1131.

units.la: Ab Hypodiacono, ad Episcopum, si quis Vxore, vel Concubinâ non abstinuerit, officio deponitur.
units.tr: From hypodeacon to bishop: if anyone has not abstained from a wife or concubine, he is deposed from office.

units.la: DEcernimus, vt ij, qui in ordine Subdiaconatus, & suprà, vxores duxerint, aut concubinas habuerint, officio, & Ecclesiastico beneficio careant. Quum enim ipsi, templum Dei, & vasa Domini, & sacratum Spiritus sancti debeant esse & dici: indignum est eos cubilibus, & immunditiis deseruire. Decet igitur Hypodiaconos ab omni se continere concubitu. Sed sequentia videntur aduersari: Primum, ex Concilio Toletano quar· 10. 10. cap. 26. Anno Do. circa 630. dum Romæ præsideret Honorius primus.
units.tr: We decree that those who have taken wives, or kept concubines, in the order of subdeacon and above, shall lose their office and ecclesiastical benefice. For since they ought to be, and be called, the temple of God, the vessels of the Lord, and consecrated to the Holy Spirit, it is unworthy that they should be slaves to beds and uncleanness. It is fitting, therefore, that hypodeacons abstain from all intercourse. But the following seem to conflict with this. First, from the Council of Toledo, the tenth, chapter 26, in about the year of the Lord 630, while Honorius I presided at Rome.

units.la: A Presbyteris, & Diaconis perpetua promittenda est castitas.
units.tr: Perpetual chastity must be promised by presbyters and deacons.

units.la: QVando Presbyteri, & Diaconi per parœcias constituuntur, oportet eos professionem Episcopo suo facere, vt castè & purè viuant sub timore Dei: vt dum eos talis professio obligat, vitæ sanctæ disciplinam retineant. Item Gregorius nobilibus ciuibus Neapolitanis. Epist. 40. lib. 8.
units.tr: When presbyters and deacons are appointed in the parishes, they must make a profession to their bishop that they live chastely and purely under the fear of God, so that, being bound by such a profession, they may retain the discipline of a holy life. Likewise Gregory to the noble citizens of Naples, Epistle 40, book 8.

units.la: Episcopi futuri testatissima debet esse continentia: Incontinentiam verò patris arguit ætas liberorum.
units.tr: The continence of a future bishop ought to be most fully attested; the age of his children proves the father's incontinence.

units.la: PRiusquam scripta ad nos vestra recurrerent, Ioannem Diaconum, qui ab altera parte electus est, paruulam habere filiam quorundam relatione cognouimus. Vnde si rationem voluissent attendere, nec alij eum eligere, nec ipse debuerat consentire. Nam, quâ præsumptione audet ad Episcopatum accedere, qui adhuc longam corporis sui continentiam, filiolâ teste, conuincitur non habere? Item Ex Concilio Arelatensi. 2. cap. 2. Anno Do. 326. Siluestro 1. Papâ.
units.tr: Before your letters came back to us, we learned from the report of certain persons that John the deacon, who was elected on the other side, has a little daughter. Hence, if they had wished to attend to reason, neither should others have elected him, nor should he himself have consented. For by what presumption does he dare to approach the episcopate, who is convicted, with his little daughter as witness, of not having long continence of body? Likewise, from the Council of Arles, second, chapter 2, in the year of the Lord 326, under Pope Silvester I.

units.la: Coniugio renuntiet, oportet, qui Sacerdotium, vel Diaconiam quærit in Ecclesia.
units.tr: He who seeks the priesthood or the diaconate in the Church must renounce marriage.

units.la: ASsumi aliquem ad Sacerdotium non posse in coniugij vinculo constitutum statuimus: nisi fuerit promissa conuersio. Item. Ex eodem Arelatensi Concilio secundo, & 3. Gratianus (quod sæpe solet) ex aliquot authorum sanctorum, vel conciliorum definitionibus ac Decretis componit Canones: quos in locis ab eo citatis minimè quæas inuenire, si verba tantum consideres: attamen ille sensum reddit: quod hominem fecisse puto, quò breuior esset: quoties occurret, auditorem monebo Verùm, præstat hic (ad rem siquidem nostram valde pertinent) illos adscribere canonas, è quibus Gratianus sequentem perquam breuiter excidit. In capite 3. dicti modò Concilij 2. cautum sic legitur.
units.tr: We decree that no one bound in the marriage tie can be assumed to the priesthood, unless a conversion has been promised. Likewise, from the same Second Council of Arles and the Third. Gratian, as he often does, composes canons from the definitions and decrees of certain holy authors or councils; you would not find them in the places he cites if you considered only the words, yet he renders the sense. I think he did this to make it shorter; whenever it occurs, I will warn the reader. But here it is better (since they bear greatly on our matter) to set out those canons from which Gratian very briefly excerpted what follows. In chapter 3 of the said Second Council it is laid down thus.
