units.la: SI quis de Clericis, à gradu Diaconatus, in solatio suo mulierem (præter auiam, matrem, sororem, filiam, neptem, vel conuersam secum uxorem) habere præsumpserit, à communione alienus habeatur. Anno posteà Do. 455. dum Leo primus Pontificatum Romæ gereret, in Arelatensi Concilio.3. rursus Decretum legimus in cap. 2. sic.
units.tr: If any of the clergy, from the grade of deacon upwards, presumes to have in his household a woman (other than a grandmother, mother, sister, daughter, granddaughter, or a wife living with him), let him be held as alien from communion. In the year 455, while Leo I held the pontificate at Rome, we read again in the Third Council of Arles a decree in chapter 2, as follows.

units.la: NVllus Metropolitanorum cuicúnque Laico dignitatem Episcopatus tribuat. Sed nec reliqui Pontifices, Presbyterij, vel Diaconatus honorem conferre præsumāt, nisi anno integro fuerit ab eis præmissa conuersio. more suo, Concilij verba relinquens, ipsorū sententiam completi voluit hoc sequenti Canone.
units.tr: No metropolitan shall bestow the dignity of bishop on any layman whatever. Nor should the other bishops presume to confer the honour of presbyter or deacon unless a conversion has been promised by them for a whole year. Following his usual manner, leaving the words of the council, he wished to complete their meaning in the following canon.

units.la: PRæterea placuit, vt deinceps non ordinentur Diaconi coniugati, nisi qui priùs conuersionis proposito cõfessi fuerint castitatem. Gratianus. Verùm, illà priori authoritate, Diaconis videtur permitti coniugium, quum ad Sacerdotium tantùm coniugati prohibentur assumi. Porrò, in sequenti videtur permitti authoritate Subdiaconis, cùm de Diaconis specialiter præcipitur, vt sine probatione castitatis non ordinentur. Hoc idem in Ancyritana synodo videtur esse permissum, in qua sic statutū est Can.10. anno Do. plus minus 300.
units.tr: Moreover, it has been resolved that henceforth married deacons are not to be ordained, unless they have first professed chastity by a purpose of conversion. Gratian. But by that earlier authority it seems that marriage is permitted to deacons, since only married men are forbidden to be assumed to the priesthood. Moreover, in the following it seems to be permitted by authority to subdeacons, since it is specially prescribed about deacons that they are not to be ordained without proof of chastity. The same seems to have been permitted in the Synod of Ancyra, in which it was laid down in canon 10, in about the year of the Lord 300, more or less.

units.la: Diaconus ob nuptias non arceatur à ministerio, si protestetur in ordinatione se continere non posse.
units.tr: A deacon is not to be barred from the ministry on account of marriage, if he declares at his ordination that he cannot contain himself.

units.la: DIaconi quicunque, quum ordinantur, si in ipsa ordinatione protestati sunt, dicentes † se velle habere uxores, nec posse se continere: hi si postea ad nuptias peruenerint, maneant in ministerio: propterea quòd his Episcopus licentiam dederit. Quicunque sanè tacuerint, & susceperint manus impositionem, professi continentiam, si postea ad nuptias peruenerint, à ministerio cessare debebunt. Item. Ex Concilio Neocæsariensi, Can.1. an.Do.plus minus 300. Quàm celebris fuerit Ecclesia Neocæsariensis in Ponto Polemoniaco videre licet ex multis Basilij magni, & Gregorij Nanziazeni epistolis. Inter alias videnda est.63. & 64. Basilij Epistola. Huic synodo subscripsere patres Episcopi septemdecim: quibus Vitalis præfuit, Episcopus Zelamitanus. Zela est oppidum Cappadociæ apud Plinium cap. 5. lib. 6. In Gratiano perperam legitur Salonitanus. Ecclesiam Neocæsariensem duo fratres, Origenis discipuli, Gregorius (qui magnus cognominatur) Et huius frater Athenodorus instituerunt. De quibus apud Eusebium cap. 30. libri sexti, & cap. 28. libri 7. Gregorij vitam mirabilem Basilius describit in libro de Spiritu sancto.cap.29. Ad Canonem.
units.tr: Whatever deacons, when they are ordained, have in the very ordination protested, saying † that they wish to have wives and cannot contain themselves: if afterwards these come to marriage, let them remain in the ministry, because the bishop has given them licence. But whoever have kept silent and received the laying on of hands, having professed continence, must cease from the ministry if they afterwards come to marriage. Likewise, from the Council of Neocaesarea, canon 1, in about the year of the Lord 300, more or less. How celebrated the Church of Neocaesarea was in Pontus Polemoniacus may be seen from many letters of Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen; among others, Basil's letters 63 and 64 are to be consulted. Seventeen bishops, the fathers, subscribed to this synod, presided over by Vitalis, bishop of Zela. Zela is a town of Cappadocia, in Pliny, book 6, chapter 5. In Gratian it is wrongly read as Salonitanus. The Church of Neocaesarea was founded by two brothers, disciples of Origen, Gregory (who is called the Great) and his brother Athenodorus, concerning whom see Eusebius, book 6, chapter 30, and book 7, chapter 28. Basil describes the wonderful life of Gregory in his book On the Holy Spirit, chapter 29. To the canon.

units.la: Presbyter vxorem ducens ab ordine deponitur: Adulter & Scortator ab Ecclesia propellitur.
units.tr: A presbyter who takes a wife is deposed from his order; an adulterer and fornicator is cast out of the Church.

units.la: PResbyter, si vxorem duxerit, ab ordine illum deponi debere. Quòd si fornicatus fuerit, vel adulterium commiserit: † extra Ecclesiam abiici, & ad pœnitentiam inter Laicos redigi oportet. Item. Gregorius. Epist. vltimâ, lib. II.
units.tr: A presbyter who takes a wife ought to be deposed from his order. But if he has committed fornication or adultery, he ought to be cast out of the Church and reduced to repentance among the laity. Also Gregory, last letter, book 2.

units.la: Culpam committit, qui temerè culpam remittit.
units.tr: He commits a fault who rashly remits a fault.

units.la: QVia sunt culpæ, in quibus culpa est relaxare vindictam, quærenda est semper veritas: vt inquiri debeat, vtrùm accusatum noxa condemnet, an à pœna, innocentia patefacta subducat.
units.tr: Since there are faults in which it is itself a fault to relax punishment, the truth must always be sought: it must be inquired whether the accused is condemned by his guilt or, once his innocence is shown, is released from punishment.

units.la: Quamuis in epistolæ parte sequeti nihil decidatur (Nudè nanque factiũ narrat) hinc tamen obseruare licet, Si qua mulier impudica, se viro cuipiam coniunxit, quem defunctum postea non luxit, inter eos coniugium fuisse non præsumitur. Ergo, Lugubria sunt in mulicre quædam prateriti matrimonij signa.
units.tr: Although nothing is decided in the part of the letter that follows (for it narrates the matter plainly), one may still observe from it that if an immodest woman has joined herself to some man, and afterwards did not mourn him when he died, it is not presumed that there was a marriage between them. Therefore certain signs of a past marriage lie in a woman's mourning.

units.la: § Itaque peruenit ad nos, Fantinum defensorem, vltionem exercere in Petrum latorem præsentium voluisse, pro eo quòd (quantùm dicitur) relictam cuiusdam Diaconi, tempore quo conductor fuit, marito tradiderit: sed quoniam iste coniugem Diaconi asserit non fuisse, dicens nec eam virginem ad eum peruenisse, denique nec religiosam mutasse vestem, postquam ille in ordine sacro promotus est: adiiciens etiam, prius quam ad Diaconum peruenisset, posteáque, praua illam mulierem opinione vixisse.
units.tr: § Thus it has come to us that Fantinus the defender wished to take vengeance on Peter, the bearer of these presents, because (so it is said) he handed over to a husband a certain deacon's widow, at the time when he was steward. But since Peter asserts that she was not the deacon's wife, saying that she did not come to him as a virgin, nor even changed her religious dress after he was promoted to the sacred order, adding also that, both before she came to the deacon and afterwards, she lived under a bad reputation.

units.la: Huiusce partis, duorumque sequentium Canonum summa est. Vxor Episcopi, Presbyteri, vel Diaconi non debet amplius alij viro coniungi. Contrauenientium pœna statuitur in illis canonib.
units.tr: The substance of this part and of the two canons that follow is this: the wife of a bishop, presbyter or deacon must not be joined to another man. The penalty for those who contravene is laid down in those canons.

units.la: § Ideo, Fraternitatem tuam his hortamur affatibus, ut cum Dei (sicut decet) timore, causam hanc subtili omnino inuestigatione perquiras: & si in coniugio Diaconi mulierem, de qua agitur, fuisse constiterit: suprascriptus lator memorato Defensori & Rectori patrimonij ad vindictam, modis omnibus, tradatur: & cum competenti emendatione, hi, qui male sociati sunt, desiungatur: Si vero in eius coniugio non fuerit, memoratum Fantinum ex nostro mandato commonere te volumus, ut ei facere nil praesumat: nec falsa illum accusatio in aliquo praegrauet.
units.tr: § Therefore we exhort your Fraternity with these words, that with the fear of God (as is fitting) you investigate this cause with thorough inquiry; and if it is established that the woman in question was the wife of a deacon, the aforesaid bearer is to be handed over in every way to the said Defender and Steward of the patrimony for vengeance, and those who were wrongly joined are to be separated with due correction. But if she was not his wife, we wish you to warn the said Fantinus on our mandate that he presume to do nothing to him, nor let a false accusation weigh him down in any way.

units.la: Item. Ex Concilio Aurelianensi primo, Can. 15. circiter annum Do. 510. Symmacho Papa. tum Clodouæus regnabat in Gallia.
units.tr: Also, from the First Council of Orléans, canon 15, about the year of the Lord 510, under Pope Symmachus, when Clovis then reigned in Gaul.

units.la: SI se cuiquam mulier Presbyteri vel Diaconi relicta, duplici coniugio coniunxerit: aut castitate fruantur, aut separentur: aut certè, si in criminis intentione perstiterint, pari excommunicatione plectantur. Item. Ex Concilio Martini Papae, cap. 19. De Martino Canonum compilatore diximus in can. 1. supra 17. Dist. Vocatur à Glossa, Canonum renouator. in can. propter, 17. Dist.
units.tr: IF a woman left by a presbyter or deacon joins herself to a man in a second marriage, let them either live in chastity or be separated; or certainly, if they persist in the intention of the crime, let them be struck with the same excommunication. Also, from the Council of Pope Martin, chapter 19. We have spoken of Martin, the compiler of the canons, in canon 1 above, distinction 17. The Gloss calls him the renewer of the canons, in the canon "Propter," distinction 17.

units.la: SI qua vidua Episcopi, vel Presbyteri, aut Diaconi, maritum acceperit, nullus clericus, nulla religiosa persona cum ea conuiuium sumat: nunquam communicet. Morienti tamen ei sacramenta subueniant. Item. Pelagius Cethego Patricio. Siue is relegius primus fuerit, anno Do 558. (quæ fuisse puto) sive secundus, anno Do 580. cui successit Gregorius magnus, Vtérque literis & sanctitate venerabilis Pontifex. Vtriusque sunt & alia nonnulla decreta, religionis plena: sed huius Epistolæ nihil aliud extat, quam quod hic legitur, Ecclesiasticæ politiæ apprimè necessarium.
units.tr: IF any widow of a bishop, presbyter or deacon takes a husband, no clergyman or religious person is to share a meal with her, and they are never to communicate with her. Yet let the sacraments be brought to her when she is dying. Also Pelagius to Cethegus the patrician. Whether he was the first Pelagius, in the year of the Lord 558 (which I think is the year), or the second, in the year 580, whom Gregory the Great succeeded, a pontiff venerable both for learning and for holiness; both have other decrees full of piety, but of this letter nothing else survives than what is read here, which is most necessary for the polity of the Church.

units.la: Non protinus ad placitum Principis, aut voluntatem Populi debet Episcopus approbari, vel recipi: sed silum post multam disquisitionem, & cum magno morum scrutinio.
units.tr: A bishop ought not to be approved or received at once by the pleasure of the Prince or the will of the People, but only after long inquiry and a great scrutiny of his character.

units.la: DE Syracusanæ urbis Antistite optaueramus in ipso initio, gloriæ vestræ desideriis obedire, nisi nos multiplex ratio ipsius non paucis temporibus ordinationem differre Sacerdotij coëgisset: ob hoc autem, quod vel personæ qualitas (sicut & vos melius noftis) vel superstes uxor, aut filij (per quos Ecclesiastica solet periclitari sub- stantia) nostros animos diutius ab eius ordinatione suspederet: quantùm ad cautelam humanam pertinet, integro penè anno distulimus, opinantes quòd in melius Syracusanorum prouenire posset electio.
units.tr: CONCERNING the bishop of the city of Syracuse, we had hoped at the very beginning to comply with the desires of your glory, but his manifold circumstances compelled us to defer the ordination to the priesthood for not a few times. This was on account of the person's quality (as you also know better) or a surviving wife or sons (through whom the Church's substance is usually put in danger), which held our minds in suspense for longer about his ordination. As far as human caution is concerned, we put it off for almost a whole year, thinking that the election of the Syracusans might turn out for the better.

units.la: Propter Idoneorum penuriam, & inhabitantum molestiam (Id est, molestos & im- probos mores & clamores) Ecclesia volens nolens non solum recipit, sed aliis etiam præficit homines indignos. Hæc est diuina eius œconomia, quam nos attigimus in can. Diaconi, su- perius hâc dist.
units.tr: Because of the scarcity of suitable men and the troublesomeness of the inhabitants (that is, troublesome and wicked morals and clamours), the Church, willy-nilly, not only receives but also sets over others unworthy men. This is its divine economy, which we touched on in the canon "Diaconi" above in this distinction.

units.la: § Sed quia in voluntatis suæ proposito irrevocabiliter perstiterunt: & nullus est alius in eadem repertus Ecclesia, nisi longioribus adhuc temporum differretur spatiis ne amplius insanirent (sicut filij vestri magnifici Prætoris testificatione didicimus) inter huiusmodi ambiguitates, illud consultius iudicauimus faciendum, vt congruâ prouidentiâ causam, propter quam Principalis constitutio, Habentem filios & vxorem, ad Episcopatus ordinem promoueri prohibet, salua dispositione Cocilij, muniremus.
units.tr: But since they persisted irrevocably in the purpose of their will, and no other suitable person was found in the same Church, unless the matter were deferred for yet longer spaces of time, lest they should rage further (as we learned from the testimony of your son, the illustrious Praetor), among such uncertainties we judged it more prudent to do this: to safeguard, by fitting providence and saving the arrangement of the Council, the cause for which the imperial constitution forbids one who has sons and a wife to be promoted to the rank of bishop.

units.la: Quisquis ordinatur Episcopus, Bona quæcunque sua profiteri iubetur: ne propria communibus, id est, ecclesiasticis prophana confundantur. Sed ille sua sibi suisque, Sua quoque sibi suisque salua, semper habeat ecclesia.
units.tr: Whoever is ordained bishop is ordered to declare whatever goods he has, lest his own property be confused with common, that is ecclesiastical, property. But let the Church always keep his own things safe for him and for his own, and his own things safe for his own.

units.la: § Qua de re, summo studio ab eodem Syracusanæ vrbis Episcopo, priusquam à nobis in Episcopum contingeret ordinari, huiusmodi exegimus cautionem: Per quam & suam fateretur, quantula esset, præsentis temporis habitâ rerum descriptione, substantiam: Et nihil vnquam perse, aut per filios, & vxorem, siue quamlibet propinquam, aut domesticam, vel extraneam forte personam, de rebus audeat vsurpare Ecclesiæ: Et vniuersa, sui Episcopatus quaesita tempore, Ecclesiae suae dominio sociaret: nihil ultra id, quod modo descriptum est, filiis suis, vel haeredibus relicturus. Gratianus, Ecce. Hâc authoritate, electus in Episcopum non prohibetur habere vxoré, & filios. Eligi autē ad Episcopatū nō debet, nisi aut Sacerdos, aut Diaconus: Subdiaconus verò nō, nisi necessitate cogēte. Siue ergo Presbyter, siue Diaconus, siue Subdiaconus fuerit, apparet, quòd in praefatis ordinibus constituti, licitè matrimonio vti possunt. Quia ergo authoritate Gregorij, Qui relictam Diaconi vxorem marito tradidit, puniendus est. Item, in Neocaesariensi Concilio, Presbyter ducens vxorem, non Diaconus, iubetur deponi. Item, in Ancyritana synodo, Diaconi, qui in ordinatione sua dicūt se velle habere vxores, si postea ad nuptias venerint, nō prohibentur à ministerio. Patet quòd nec Diaconi, nec Subdiaconi sunt prohibēdi à coniugio. Respondet obiectu Gratianus. Sed quod de electione obiicitur, Verum quidem est, In Episcopum non eligendum esse, nisi in sacris ordinibus constitutum: sed ipsum habere vxorem & filios, non repugnat praemissis authoritatibus, De continentia clericorum: In Laicali enim habitu, vel in minoribus ordinibus constitutus, potuit habere vxorem & filios. Sed si postea ex consensu vxoris continentiam professus, Subdiaconatum, vel Diaconatum, vel Presbyterii gradum adeptus fuerat: attamen vxori & filiis ipsum necessaria ministrare oportebat. Illud autē Gregorii duobus modis soluitur: vel quia Ecclesia illa, cui Diaconus ille militauerat, nondum continentiae votum susceperat in Diaconis, & reliquis ministris: Vel quia(sicut de electo in Episcopum supra scriptum est)ante Subdiaconatum memoratus Diaconus eam in vxorem duxerat. Illud autem Neocaesariensis Concilii, & Ancyritanae Synodi, Vel ex tempore, vel ex loco intelligitur. Ex tempore: quia nondū erat introducta continentia ministrorum altaris. Ex loco: quia vtraque Synodus Orientalis est: & Orientalis Ecclesia non suscipit generale votū castitatis. Hoc tamen diligēti obseruatione custodit, Vt post adeptum Sacerdotium, defuncta priori vxore, cum qua Sacerdos factus fuerat, si alteram duxerit, deponatur. Hic non contentus Gratianus, alia quoque Nuptiatorum clericorum profert argumenta, quibus sua cum mulieribus contubernia defendebant.
units.tr: § For this reason, with the utmost diligence, before he was to be ordained bishop by us, we required from the same Bishop of Syracuse a caution of this kind: by which he should declare how modest his property was, with a description of his holdings as they then stood, and that he would never presume to usurp anything of the Church's goods, either himself or through sons, wife, or any relative or household member, or perhaps a stranger; and that he would join everything acquired during his episcopate to the ownership of his Church, leaving to his sons or heirs nothing beyond what has now been described. Gratian, Behold: by this authority, a man elected bishop is not forbidden to have a wife and sons. But no one ought to be elected bishop unless he is a priest or deacon; a subdeacon may be chosen only if necessity compels. So whether he is a presbyter, deacon or subdeacon, it is clear that men established in those orders may lawfully use marriage. Therefore, on the authority of Gregory, one who gave a deacon's widow to a husband is to be punished. Also, at the Council of Neocaesarea, a presbyter who takes a wife, not a deacon, is ordered to be deposed. Also, in the Synod of Ancyra, deacons who at their ordination say they wish to have wives, if they afterwards come to marriage, are not barred from the ministry. It is clear that neither deacons nor subdeacons are to be forbidden marriage. Gratian replies to the objection. But as to what is objected about election: it is true that one is not to be elected bishop unless he is already established in the sacred orders; but that he himself had a wife and sons does not contradict the aforesaid authorities, on the continence of clergy. For in lay dress, or while in the lesser orders, he could have had a wife and sons. But if afterwards, with his wife's consent, having professed continence, he attained the subdiaconate, the diaconate, or the rank of presbyter, nevertheless he had to supply necessities to his wife and sons. That saying of Gregory is resolved in two ways: either because that Church in which the deacon had served had not yet taken a vow of continence among its deacons and other ministers, or because (as has been written above concerning the one elected bishop) the said deacon had taken her as his wife before the subdiaconate. But that of the Council of Neocaesarea and of the Synod of Ancyra is understood either in respect of time or of place. In respect of time, because the continence of altar ministers had not yet been introduced. In respect of place, because both synods are Eastern, and the Eastern Church does not accept a general vow of chastity. Yet it keeps with careful observance that a priest who, after obtaining the priesthood, has lost the wife with whom he was made a priest, and then takes another, is deposed. Gratian, not content with this, brings forward other arguments of married clerics, by which they defended their cohabitation with women.

units.la: Item. Opponitur illud; quod legitur in Canone Apostolorum sexto.
units.tr: Likewise, there is an objection in what is read in the sixth Canon of the Apostles.

units.la: Ecclesiastici ministerij praetextu, non est vxoris cura deponenda.
units.tr: On the pretext of the ecclesiastical ministry, a wife's care is not to be laid aside.

units.la: S I quis docuerit Sacerdotem, sub obtentu religionis, pro- priam vxorem contemnere, Anathema sit. Item. Ex Concilio Gangrensi. cap. 4. circiter an. Do. 330. Siluestro Papā.
units.tr: If anyone teaches that a priest, under the pretext of religion, should despise his own wife, let him be anathema. Likewise, from the Council of Gangra, canon 4, about the year of the Lord 330, under Pope Sylvester.

units.la: Presbyteri legitimam habentis vxorem ἐυλαγίαν, καὶ κοινωνίαν, id est, Benedictio & Communio, non est denegnanda. Videto Socratem cap. 43. lib. 2.
units.tr: A presbyter who has a lawful wife is not to be refused the eulogia and the koinonia, that is, the blessing and the communion [ἐυλαγίαν, καὶ κοινωνίαν]. See Socrates, chapter 43, book 2.

units.la: S I quis discernit Presbyterum coniugatum, tanquam occasione nuptiarum quòd offerre non debeat, & ab eius
units.tr: If anyone separates a married presbyter, as though, because of marriage, he ought not to offer, and abstains from his oblation, let him be anathema.

units.la: † μὴ χρῆναι ἀλιτουργηστεῖν τὸς αὐτῶ πρὸ φορᾶς ματαιολαμβάνειν. eius oblatione ideo abstinet, Anathema sit. Item. Ex sexta Synodo.can. 16. Integer, non est hic traductus. Integra tamen fide sensus est redditus. De qua Bedam legito ca. 67. De temporibus: Et etiam quae post Canonem statim subiiciemus.
units.tr: that those who are married ought not to take part in the liturgy with those who receive the offering [μὴ χρῆναι ἀλιτουργηστεῖν τὸς αὐτῶ πρὸ φορᾶς ματαιολαμβάνειν]. The canon has not been translated here in its entirety, but its sense has been rendered with full fidelity. On this, see Bede, chapter 67, On Times; and also what we shall add immediately after the canon.

units.la: Presbyter in gradu, vel officio non retinetur, qui nuptiis detinetur.
units.tr: A presbyter who is held back by marriage is not retained in his rank or office.

units.la: PResbyterum non legalibus nuptiis detentum, cathedrā quidē habere, sed ab officio abstinere praecipimus.
units.tr: We order that a presbyter who is not bound by a lawful marriage may indeed keep his seat, but must abstain from the office.

units.la: Huiusce versiculi periocha sumitur ex cap. 7. ad Hebraeos ubi est. — Sine ulla contradictione, Quod minus est, à meliore benedicitur. can. denique 21. dist.
units.tr: The summary of this verse is taken from chapter 7 of Hebrews, where it reads: "Without any contradiction, the less is blessed by the better." Canon, finally, dist. 21.

units.la: § Sufficit enim huiusmodi indulgentia ei: quia benedicere aliis eum, qui vulnera sua debet curare, consequens non est: Benedictio enim, sanctificationis traditio est. Qui vero hanc non habet, propter delictum ignorantiae, quomodo aliis tradet?
units.tr: § Such an indulgence is enough for him, since it does not follow that he should bless others when he must himself have his wounds tended. For blessing is the handing on of sanctification. But he who does not have this, on account of the sin of ignorance, how will he hand it on to others?

units.la: Pro versus istius epitome adscribam domini praeceptum, Levitici. cap. 21. Sacerdos, qui habuerit maculam, non offeret panes Deo suo: Nec accedet ad ministerium eius. Attamen vescetur panibus, qui offeruntur in sanctuario. can. Sacerdotes. 1. q. 1. Corporis illic macula consideratur: hic Animae.
units.tr: As a summary of this verse I shall add the Lord's command, Leviticus chapter 21: "A priest who has a blemish shall not offer bread to his God, nor approach his ministry. Yet he shall eat of the bread that is offered in the sanctuary." Canon Sacerdotes, 1 q. 1. There the blemish of the body is considered; here, that of the soul.

units.la: § Nō enim publicè, neque privatè benedicat, nec corpus Domini dispensset aliis, nec alio modo ministret: sed sufficiat ei quòd praesidet, & imploret à Deo, ut dimittatur ei iniquitas ignorantiae suae.
units.tr: § For he may bless neither publicly nor privately, nor distribute the body of the Lord to others, nor minister in any other way. But it is enough for him that he presides, and prays to God that the iniquity of his ignorance be forgiven him.

units.la: Si quis illegitimas nuptias per errorem contraxerit, Errore cognito, debet has distrahere.
units.tr: If someone has contracted an unlawful marriage through error, once the error is known, he ought to dissolve it.

units.la: § Manifestum est autem, quòd & huiusmodi non legitimae nuptiae soluantur: & nullatenus vir accessum habeat ad eam, propter quā sacro ministerio privatus est.
units.tr: § It is clear, moreover, that such unlawful marriages are also to be dissolved, and that the man should in no way have access to the woman on account of whom he has been deprived of the sacred ministry.

units.la: Est, quod hic immorer diutiusculè. Quandoquidem Nuptiatores clerici (contra quos Gratianus hic integras octo distinctiones coacervauit) suas plusquam comicas impudicitias, sub Graecorum pallio semper agere conati sunt. Nec habent, quo speciosius furta sua (matrimonia, scilicet, ab eis inita) celent. Pro sua passim libidine, Sacerdotes Graecos aut tumāt uxores impunè duxisse. Canon præsens istos valdè confutat. Eiusdémque Synodi ca-non tertius: quem propterea Græcum totum subiecit: quò nos etiam discrimen non magnū cognosamus inter has duas Ecclesias, Latinam Græcamque, fuisse circa Sacerdotum cœlibatum.
units.tr: There is something here I must dwell on a little longer. Since the marrying clergy (against whom Gratian here heaps up eight whole distinctions) have always tried to carry on their more than comic immodesties under the cloak of the Greeks, and have no more specious way to hide their thefts (that is, the marriages they entered into), Greek priests have, wherever their lust led them, taken wives with impunity. The present canon refutes them thoroughly. And the third canon of the same Synod, which for this reason we have subjoined in full in Greek, so that we may also recognise that there was no great difference between these two Churches, the Latin and the Greek, concerning the celibacy of priests.

units.la: ΚΑΝΩΝ. Γ. ΕΚΤΗΣ ΣΥΝΟΔΟΥ.
units.tr: CANON 3 OF THE SIXTH SYNOD [ΚΑΝΩΝ. Γ. ΕΚΤΗΣ ΣΥΝΟΔΟΥ.]

units.la: Ἐπειδὴ δὲ, ὁ σεβάσμιος καὶ φιλόχριστος ἡμῶν βασιλεὺς, τῇ ἁγίᾳ τῶν [?] καὶ οἰκουμενικῇ πεοσφώνησιν σωσόλω· ὥστε οὖν ἐν κλήρῳ κατὰ λειτουργοὺς, καὶ ἀνδρὸς τὰ θεῖα ἐμπρεσβεύοντας, καὶ ἀκροατὰς ἀρχῆναι, καὶ λειτουργοὺς ἀμώμους, καὶ τῆς νοερᾶς τῆς μεγάλου θεοῦ θυμάτος, καὶ ἀρχιερέως θυσίας ἀξίους. ἀνακαθαρεῖ τε τὰ ἐξ ἀδικμοργμ χάμωμ τούτοις ἐμμένειν μύσῃ. πρὸς τούτῳ δὲ, τὴν τῆς ἐφ ταμείων ἁγιωτάτης ἐκκλησίας τὴν τῆς ἀκριβείας τὴν ἡμῶν καὶ παρεμβ[?]ῶν πεοπ ἡμείλιν ὡ. τὴν δὲ οἰκοῦ τὴν τοῦ θεοφυλάκτου ταύτης καὶ βασιλίδος τῶν λεω ὁ ἡ θρόνου. Τὸ τῆς φυλαρχωπίας, καὶ συμπαθείας εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἀμφότερα μίξαντες, πατρικῶς ὁμοῦ καὶ φιλοκλῆς, ὡς μή τὸ πέαν ἐκλύτου μὴ συφὸν τὸ αὐκηρὸν καταλείψομεν· ἡ μάλιστα τῆς ἐξ ἀγγελίας πῶματος εἰς ὁ ὀλίγῳ ἀνδρῶν τοῖ ὀ θάνηλον ἴλως ἀνδρῶν. ὥστε οὖν μὴ δυσὶ γάμοις ποιεῖτε ρῆντας, ὦ μέχρι τὴν πεντεκαιδεκάτης τῆς δεκάλιτος ἰανναρίου μηνός, τῆς * ταρούσης τετάρτης † ἰνδικτίονος, ἐτ[?]ς ς.ἐναδθου ἐνεγκησθου ἐνάτῃ, δουλεδίντας τὴν ἁμαρτίᾳ, καὶ μὴ ἐκνήξαι ταύτης πεοελομένους, καθαιρέσει κανονικῇ ὑπορβαλεῖν. τοὺς δὲ ζῶ τοιούτῳ μὲν τῆς δυνάμεως πάθει * ὠδεπεσόντας, περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμῶν ὑδιγνώσεως ἀγ συμφέρον ἐπιγνωκότας, ὥ ἄν κακὸν ἐξ ἑαυτῶν ἀποκινήσαντας, καὶ ἐξέρῳ πῶ ξενῷ παντῶ, καὶ νόμον συμπλοκῶ ἐκδιώξαντας· ἢ καὶ ἂν αἱ κατὰ δεύτερον γάμου γυναῖκες ἤδη πεπλευτήκασι· ἢ καὶ αὐτοὶ πρὸς ὑδιγροφῷ ἐμάρῳ μεταμαθόντες πῶ ὀφφοσιῶν, καὶ τὴν πεῶν αὐτῶν παρανομίαν τὰ χαῖρε ὑδιλαδύμενοι, εἴπε πεισβύτεροι, εἴπε διάκονοι ὄντες τυγχάνοιεν. τούτους ἐδοξε ὠπαῦσαι μ πάσης ἱεραρχικῆς λειτουργίας
units.tr: Since our most reverend and Christ-loving emperor, in the holy and ecumenical ... has provided that those in the clergy, as ministers and ... who deal with divine things, and as readers, and as blameless ministers, and worthy of the spiritual sacrifice of the great God and the high priest's offering, should be cleansed of ... and should keep themselves from this defilement; and, moreover, regarding the strict observance of the most holy Church of God, and ... the house of this God-guarded city and royal throne. Mingling in ourselves both the care of the flock and sympathy, we have resolved, fatherly and together, not to leave unrepaired what needs correcting, and especially so that the affairs of the clergy may not be made a matter of ... Therefore, those who have been joined in two marriages, up to the fifteenth day of the month of January, in the fourth indiction, in the year ... (as they were previously taught), and who have not ceased to live in sin, shall be cast out by canonical deposition; and those who have fallen into this passion of ... and who have not come to know the gift of our ... shall be expelled from the clergy, whether they are presbyters, deacons, or those in the catalogue.
