units.la: γίας
units.tr: holy [γίας]

units.la: * παρηλθότες.
units.tr: * Having passed by [παρηλθότες].

units.la: † In Zonara, manu scripto, ex Regis Bibliotheca, bis signo sequenti designatur Indictio X. Nec integra vox scribitur.
units.tr: In Zonaras, in a manuscript from the King's library, the following sign is twice marked as Indiction X. Nor is the word written in full. [†]

units.la: * ταρούσης. γίας, ἤτοι ἐνεργείας ἤδη ὣδὶ ἐντὸς τινα χρόνον [?] ἀφιλιμινέντας· τ᾽ δὲ [?] λιμῆς τ᾽ κατα τὸ καθέσθαρ καὶ σασιν μετέχειν, ἀρκουμένους τῇ πενεδείᾳ· καὶ πεοσκλαίοντας τοῖς κυείῳ συγχωρηθῆναι αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ ἀγνοίας ἀνόνυμα. ὀλλογῆν γὰρ ἕτερον, ἢ τὰ οἰκεῖα τιμε-λεῖν ὀφείλοντα τρἀύματα ἀνακολουθοῦω. τὸν δὲ χαμεθὴ μὲν μιᾶ σωαφεντας, χεῖρα δὲ ἡ πεοσλαφθεῖσα ἐτύχανεν· ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὸν μιᾷ τῷ χειροτονίαν χάμῳ ἐνὶ ταραγνόμῳ πεοσομελίζοντας πᾶτ᾽ ἔσιν, πρεσβυτέρους, καὶ Διακόνους, καὶ ἀπὸ Διακόνως, ἤν ὡδὶ βραχὺν ἕνα χρόνον ἡμερέντας τὴν ἱερᾶς λειτουργίας, καὶ ἀδιλιμινέντας· ὡσθὶς αὐτῆς ἐν τοῖς σικλοῖς ἀρκεταςαθήναι βαθμοῖς. μηδαμῶς ἐν ἐτόρῳ μείζονι πεοκόπτοντας βαθμῷ, πεοδήλως Διαλυθέντος αὐτοῖς τὸ ἀξίωμα ἔ(ωσικωσι). ταῦτα δὲ ὡδὶ τοῖς καταληφθεῖσιν μέχει τὴν τῶν ἱτίνα, καὶ δεκάτης, ὡς εἴρηται, τὸ Ἰανναείου μηνὸς, τὴν πεάρτης ἰνδικτιῶνος, ἐν τοῖς πεοδηλωθέντων παίσμασι, καὶ μόνον ἱερᾶλικῶς ἐν πῶσαμεν. ὀείζοντες, ἀχ᾽ τὸ παρόντος, καὶ ἀναγευόμενοι τὴν κανόνα τὴν Διαγοεύοντα. τὸν δυσὶ χάμοις συμπλακέντα μιᾷ δ᾽ βάπισμα, ἢ παλακλῶ κτησάμενον, μὴ δυνάσθαι εἶναι ἐπίσκοπον, ἢ πρεσβύτερον, ἢ διάκονον, ἢ ὄλφος τῷ καταλόγου τῆς ἱεραλικοῦ. ὡσαύτως καὶ τὴν χέρα λαμβάνοντα, ἢ ἐμβεβλημένων, ἢ ἐταίρα, ἢ σικέτλω, ἢ τὴν ὡδὶ τὸ σκηνῆς, μὴ δυνάσθαι εἶναι ἰδιοκόπτ-ρ, ἢ πρεσβύτερον, ἢ διάκονον, ἢ ὄλφος τῷ καταλόγου τῆς ἱερατικῆν.
units.tr: * present [ταρούσης]. Holy, that is, having been for some time without activity; and those who ... to partake of the sacrament, content with poverty, and begging the Lord that they be granted forgiveness for their ignorance. For it is not right to ... but to attend to their own wounds. And the one who was joined in one marriage has received the hand (of ordination); likewise also those who are ordained in the one ordination, that is, presbyters and deacons, and deacons who have passed the time of one short year without performing the sacred ministry, and who have lived without ... so that they may be placed in the lower ranks, and never advance to a higher rank, their dignity being plainly dissolved for them. These things are to be applied to those who were caught in the year of the ... and the tenth of the month of January, as has been said, in the fourth indiction, in the aforementioned cases, and only as a matter of the priestly order, from the present time, and recalling the canon which decrees this. The one who has been joined to two wives, or who has taken a concubine, or a harlot, or a slave-woman, or one such as a ... cannot be a bishop, presbyter, or deacon, or any other in the catalogue of the priesthood.

units.la: Id est,
units.tr: That is,

units.la: QVandoquidem, pius & amicus Christi, Rex noster, sanctam hanc & Oecumenicam Synodum affatus est. — Vt in clero delectos, ad alios diuina traiicientes, puros ipsa constituat, & Liturgos irreprehensibiles, dignos intelligentiâ magni Dei, dignos & eius sacrificio, summi denique Pontificis ara dignos: vtque Synodus expurget obiectas illis † Abominationes ex illegitimis nuptiis. Quod ad hoc autem pertinet. — Quum sanctissima Romanorum Ecclesia proponat observare Canonem rigoris: Hi autem, qui sub huius a Deo custoditae, Regiaque civitatis throno sunt, aliud proponentibus: Nos (quod humanitatis & commiserationis est) in unum commiscentes utrumque, paterne simul & pie (ut neque lene, dissolutum: neque strictum, grave relinquamus: & maxime, quum delictum ex ignorantia perenerit ad non paucorum hominum multitudinem) statuimus: —
units.tr: Since our king, pious and a friend of Christ, has addressed this holy and ecumenical synod: that it may itself appoint pure men, chosen from the clergy and transferred to divine service from among others, and blameless ministers, worthy of understanding the great God, worthy also of his sacrifice, and finally worthy of the altar of the supreme pontiff; and that the synod may purge the abominations laid against them arising from illegitimate marriages. As to this matter: since the most holy Church of the Romans proposes to observe a canon of rigour, while those who sit under the throne of this city, which is guarded by God and royal, propose otherwise, we, mixing both together into one, out of humanity and compassion, decree in a fatherly and pious manner at once, so that we leave neither something lax and dissolute nor something harsh and grave. And especially since the offence arose from ignorance, among not a few men, we decree:

units.la: Hilarianus Codex Graecorum canonum, Regiusque Zonaras discrepant hic numeri. In illo scribitur ἔτος ἰξ᾽ ἀχλιαςοῦ ... Id est, Anno sexies millesimo centesimo nonagesimo nono. Zonaras habet ... Id est, Anno sexies centesimo nonagesimo nono. Prior ille numerus ad orbem conditum venit referendus: Et posterior ad annos Christi, quanquam neuter mendo, saltem magna suspicione mendi, vacat apud me. Non est cuiquam facile certa priscarum synodorum tempora designare. Vix duo convenient authores in supputatione. Diegesis oecumenicarum synodorum continet habitam Synodum sextam, dum currerent ... Id est, A creatione mundi sexies mille centum septuaginta quatuor anni. Et a Christo Septingenti cum novemdecim. Beda in dicto cap. 67. Solummodo numerat Quater mille sexcentos & triginta septem annos ab orbe condito, quum temporibus Agathonis papae sexta synodus universalis Constantinopoli celebrata fuit, exequente piissimo principe Constantino. Hanc ille. Sub Agathone consentiunt omnes habitam fuisse Synodum sextam. Platina scribit hunc in Papam creatum, anno Do. septingentesimo secunda. Quidam, sexcentesimo septuagesimo quinto, scribunt alii, Sexcentesimo nonagesimo quarto. Solis duobus Agatho sedit annis, cum sex mensibus. Utque res admodum varia est: in medio propterea relinquo, breviter haec annotasse contentus. — Statuimus —
units.tr: The Hilarian codex of the Greek canons and the royal Zonaras differ here in their numbers. The former writes "year 6199", that is, in the year six thousand one hundred and ninety-nine. Zonaras has "year 699", that is, in the year six hundred and ninety-nine. The former number must be referred to the creation of the world, and the latter to the years of Christ, though neither, at least in my view, is free of error, or at least of strong suspicion of error. It is not easy for anyone to fix the certain dates of the ancient synods. Scarcely two authors agree in their reckoning. The Diegesis of the ecumenical synods records that the sixth synod was held while the years were running: that is, six thousand one hundred and seventy-four years from the creation of the world, and seven hundred and nineteen from Christ. Bede, in the said chapter 67, counts only four thousand six hundred and thirty-seven years from the creation of the world, when in the time of Pope Agatho the sixth universal synod was celebrated at Constantinople, under the most pious emperor Constantine. So he. All agree that the sixth synod was held under Agatho. Platina writes that he was made pope in the year of the Lord 702; some write 675, others 694. Agatho sat for only two years and six months. Since the matter is so varied, I leave it undecided, content to have noted these things briefly. We decree:

units.la: VT, Qui ad secundas nuptias transierint, & ad decimumquintum praeteriti Ianuarij mensis usque, quartae praesentis Indictionis, Anni sexies centesimi nonagesimi noni, servierint peccato, nec ab eo resipiscere voluerint, depositioni Canonicae subiaceant. Qui vero prius, in illam Digamiae lapsi affectionem, quam nostri decreti cognoscerent unanimé lationem, malum illud ab sese amputarunt,& procul expulerunt externum illum & adulterinum coitum: vel quorum secundi matrinonij vxores iámque vitâ defunctæ sunt: vel certè ipsi ad pœnitentiam respicientes,ad addiscendâ castitatem sese transtulerunt, omnium mox obliti, quæ contra leges patrarant siue Presbyteri, siue Diaconi fuerint:_Hos quidem visum est ab omni iam sacro munere, vel functione abstinetes in aliquê certum diê damnari: honoris tamen sui, pro cathedra, stationisque modo participes esse, Primâ sede contentos. Lachrymas interim Domino fundentes, vt remittat illud ex ignorantia peccatum: Non enim conuenit eum,qui sua propria vulnera curare debet, alterum benedicere. Hi verò, qui fuerunt vni duntaxat vxori coniuncti, quæ vidua tunc esset, quum fuit assumpta: similiter & hi, qui post chirotoniam vni se matrimonio copularunt illegitimo (hoc est, Presbyteri,& Diaconi, & Hypodiaconi) continuò, ad breue aliquod tempus à sancto ministerio semoueantur, & castigentur, iterúmque suis propriis gradibus restituantur ad maiorem tamen postea gradum nullo modo procedentes, ipsorum publicè dissolutâ cohabitatione illicitâ. Hæc verò dedeprehensis ad diem decimumquintum(prout dictum est) Ianuarij mensis, quartæ indictionis, in manifestis criminibus. Idque solùm de Hieraticis designauimus. Definientes ex præsenti, ac renouantes Canonem vetantem_Vt qui se post Baptismum, secundis inuoluerit nuptiis, quíve concubinam habuerit, non possit esse Episcopus, vel Presbyter, vel Diaconus, aut omnino de catalogo Sacro. Similiter._Et qui viduam accepit, aut Repudiatam, vel Meretricë, vel Ancillâ, vel è scena mulierem, nequeat esse Episcopus, aut Presbyter, aut Diaconus, aut ordinis denique Sacri. Tertius est ille Canon Synodi sextae in Trullo habitae Constantinopoli, dum regnaret Constantinus quartus, princeps valde catholicus. Canonis fragmentum Gratianus hic allegavit, in quem Zonaras Graecus interpres Canonum sic scripsit.
units.tr: THAT those who have entered second marriages, and who have persisted in sin up to the fifteenth day of the past month of January, in the fourth indiction of the present year, six thousand one hundred and ninety-nine, and have been unwilling to repent of it, shall be subject to canonical deposition. But those who earlier, before they learned of our unanimous decree, had fallen into that affection for digamy, cut off that evil from themselves and drove far away that foreign and adulterous union, or whose wives of their second marriage have already died, or who, turning to repentance, have themselves gone over to learning chastity, forgetting at once everything they had done contrary to the laws, whether they were presbyters or deacons: it seemed fit that these men, abstaining from all sacred office and function, be condemned for some certain day, yet keep their honour and their place according to their seat and station, content with the first seat. Meanwhile let them pour out tears to the Lord, that he may forgive them that sin committed through ignorance; for it is not fitting that one who ought to cure his own wounds should bless another. But those who were joined to one wife only, who was a widow at the time she was taken; likewise also those who after ordination joined themselves in unlawful marriage (that is, presbyters, deacons and subdeacons), are to be removed at once from the holy ministry for some short time and be chastised, and then restored to their own grades, yet never proceeding to a higher grade, their unlawful cohabitation having been publicly dissolved. These matters, however, are to be applied to those caught, up to the fifteenth day (as has been said) of January in the fourth indiction, in manifest crimes. And this we have appointed only for the hieratic orders. Defining and renewing from now on the canon which forbids that whoever has entered second nuptials after baptism, or who has kept a concubine, may be a bishop, presbyter or deacon, or in any way of the sacred catalogue. Similarly: and whoever has taken a widow, or a repudiated woman, or a harlot, or a maidservant, or from the stage a woman, may not be a bishop, presbyter, deacon, or in short of any sacred order. That is the third canon of the sixth synod held at Constantinople in Trullo, while Constantine the Fourth, a most Catholic prince, reigned. Gratian cited here a fragment of this canon, on which Zonaras, the Greek interpreter of the canons, wrote as follows.

units.la: ΤΑ΄ μὲν τὲ τρίτε κανόνος τὸ τὰ ὡς καιρικὰ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἱερὰ τὴ οἰκονομίαν, ἐφιδὼ- ται. οὐ μόνον ἀλλ' καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐξῆς κρατεῖν ὀφείλοντα εἰδέναι. ἃ δὲ κρατεῖ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων εἰσὶ κανόνες. ιβ. καὶ. ιι. οὓς παραφαινομένους, ἢ εὐνοδὸς αὐτὴ ἀνεπιώσατο· εἰ τοιοῦτοι δὲ καὶ ἀμφω κανόνες ἐξηγήθησαν καὶ ἐζητῶν τὸ τὰ τῶν ἐξῆς κοιν, εὑρήσῃ ἀνάλω, ἐν τοῖς τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων κανόσι.
units.tr: [Greek text as printed in the source; the sense is:] Those things decreed in the third canon as seasonal, and laid down with regard to the dispensation for the sake of the times, are not only to be observed but also those that follow must be understood to hold. The canons of the holy Apostles, the twelfth and eleventh, which the synod received, are of the same kind; and if you seek what is common to those that follow, you will find it in the canons of the holy Apostles. [ΤΑ΄ μὲν τὲ τρίτε κανόνος τὸ τὰ ὡς καιρικὰ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἱερὰ τὴ οἰκονομίαν, ἐφιδὼ- ται. οὐ μόνον ἀλλ' καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐξῆς κρατεῖν ὀφείλοντα εἰδέναι. ἃ δὲ κρατεῖ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων εἰσὶ κανόνες. ιβ. καὶ. ιι. οὓς παραφαινομένους, ἢ εὐνοδὸς αὐτὴ ἀνεπιώσατο· εἰ τοιοῦτοι δὲ καὶ ἀμφω κανόνες ἐξηγήθησαν καὶ ἐζητῶν τὸ τὰ τῶν ἐξῆς κοιν, εὑρήσῃ ἀνάλω, ἐν τοῖς τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων κανόσι.]

units.la: Id est.
units.tr: That is.

units.la: QVæ definiuntur hoc in tertio Canone, velut opportuna, temporiqueque tum conuenientia, propter Oeconomiam definita sunt: non autem quòd & hæc illi deinceps obtinere debent permiserint. Horum verò quæ vim possit habere debeant, ea praesenti Canone praescribuntur (vt puta) Sanctorum Canones Apostolorum, decimus septimus, & decimus octauus: quos per transgressionem desuetos, ipsa Synodus renouauit. Ambo fuerunt expositi. Quaerens autem ipsorum expositionem, inueniet eam in Canonibus Sanctorū Apostolorum. Gratianum iam redeamus, adhuc Nuptiatorum patrocinia recitantem. Item. Nicolaus ad consulta Bulgarorum. Rescribitur hoc responsum in Pannomia libro quinto, cap.1 Ex illius Decretalis Epistolae capite 70. Noli legi aliubi. Fuit hic Nicolaus primus, Pontifex multis nominibus excellens, circiter annum Do. 858. Bulgari (quondam Plinio dicti Triballi, si recentioribus credimus) gens in Mysia inferiore (quae nunc est Bulgaria) ad Pontum pertinet. Bulgaros Archidiaconus locat inter Hungaros & Graecos. Ouidius, de Tristibus, & in Ponto, vocat eos Sarmatas & Getas. Ouidiano solo (sicuti puto) Gens exilio clara: Nam Tomi sunt in illa. Qui dum Christi cultum recepissent, Nicolai primi Pontificatu, Romanae se subdiderunt Ecclesiae. De cuius legibus illos, & hunc Nicolaum primum, & eius successorem Adrianum secundum, saepe consuluisse legimus. Vnde plura sunt istiusmodi rescripta.
units.tr: What is defined in this third canon, as fitting and suited to the times, has been laid down because of the dispensation; but it does not follow that these things must afterwards be maintained by them. Of those things which ought to have force, they are prescribed in the present canon: for instance, the canons of the holy Apostles, the seventeenth and eighteenth, which the synod itself renewed because they had fallen into disuse through transgression. Both were expounded. Whoever seeks their exposition will find it in the canons of the holy Apostles. Let us now return to Gratian, who still recites the defences of those who marry. Likewise. Nicholas, in reply to the questions of the Bulgarians. This answer is rescribed in the fifth book of the Pannomian, chapter 1, from chapter 70 of that Decretal letter. Do not read it elsewhere. This Nicholas was the first pope, excelling in many respects, around the year of the Lord 858. The Bulgarians (once called Triballi by Pliny, if we believe the more recent writers), a people in Lower Moesia (which is now Bulgaria), belong to Pontus. The Archdeacon places the Bulgarians between the Hungarians and the Greeks. Ovid, in the Tristia and in the Pontica, calls them Sarmatians and Getae. By Ovid alone (as I think) is the people made famous by exile, for Tomi lies in their land. When they had received the worship of Christ, under the pontificate of Nicholas the first, they submitted themselves to the Roman Church. We read that they often consulted him and his successor Adrian the second about its laws. Hence there are many rescripts of this kind.

units.la: De Presbyteris, etiam coniugatis, non est a Laicis iudicandum.
units.tr: On presbyters, even married ones, lay people are not to pass judgment.

units.la: CONsulendum decernitis, Vtrùm Presbyterum habentem vxorem debeatis sustentare, & honorare: an à vobis proiicere? In quo respondemus, quòd licet ipsi valde sint reprehensibiles, vos tamen Deum conuenit imitari, qui Solem suum oriri facit super bonos & molos: Deiicere iicere enim à vobis ideo non debetis: quoniam nec Iudam Dominus (cùm esset falsus discipulus) à numero discipulorum eiecit. Verùm & de Presbyteris, vobis, qui Laici estis, nec iudicandum est, nec de vita eorum quicquam inuestigandum: sed Episcoporum iudicio, quicquid idsit, est referuandum. Superiùs dicta pro Nuptiatoribus, Gratianus refellit.
units.tr: You ask whether you ought to support and honour a presbyter who has a wife, or cast him out from you. To this we answer that although they are very blameworthy, you ought nevertheless to imitate God, who makes his sun rise over the good and the evil. To cast them out from you, therefore, you ought not, since the Lord did not cast Judas out of the number of the disciples, although he was a false disciple. But about presbyters, you who are laymen must neither judge nor investigate anything about their lives; rather, whatever it may be, it is to be reserved to the judgment of the bishops. The things said above in favour of those who marry, Gratian refutes.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXIX.
units.tr: DISTINCTIO XXIX.

units.la: Gratianus. S E D notandum est,quòd secundum Isidorum, pleráque capitula, Ex causa, Ex loco, Ex tempore, Ex persona, consideranda sunt. Ait Isidorus.
units.tr: Gratian. BUT it must be noted that, according to Isidore, most chapters must be considered by cause, by place, by time, and by person. Isidore says:

units.la: Circunstantiæ, quacunque in re, sive controversia, sunt primò quarendæ: Sic enim dictæ sunt, quòd circunstent quæstionem.
units.tr: The circumstances, in any matter or controversy whatever, are to be sought out first, for they are so called because they surround the question.

units.la: SCiendum est, quòd pleráque capitula, Ex causa, Ex persona, Ex loco, Ex tempore, consideranda sunt: quorum modi, quia medullitùs nò indagantur, in erroris Labyrinthum nonnulli intricando impinguntur: quum ante iudicant, quàm intelligant: ante inculpant, quàm iterando lecta perquirant. Ait etiam Gregorius.
units.tr: It must be known that most chapters must be considered by cause, by person, by place, and by time. Since their manner is not investigated thoroughly, some, entangling themselves, are caught in the labyrinth of error: they judge before they understand, and they find fault before they seek out by careful reading what has been read. Gregory also says:

units.la: REgulæ Sanctorum Patrũ pro Tempore, Loco, & Persona, & Negocio, & Instante necessitate, traditæ sunt. Item. Hieronymus. In proœmio cōmentarij Epistolæ ad Ephesios.
units.tr: The rules of the holy Fathers were laid down with respect to time, place, person, business, and pressing necessity. Likewise Jerome, in the preface to his commentary on the Epistle to the Ephesians:

units.la: NEcesse est, ut iuxta diuersitates locorum, temporum, & hominum, quibus scripturæ factæ sunt, diuersas causas, & argumenta, & origines habeant. Quomodo beatus Ioannes in Apocalypsi sua, septem scribens Ecclesiis, In unaquaque earum vel specialia, vel vniuersalia vitia reprehendit, vel virtutes probat: ita & sanctus Apostolus Paulus per singulas Ecclesias vulnerib° medebatur. turillatis: nec ad instar imperiti medici, uno collyrio omnium oculos vult curare. Deinde pergit Gratianus specialiter ostendens, quòd Legis ferendæ causa diligenter est consideranda. Sic dissoluere volens, quod de coniugio Sacerdotali supra legimus
units.tr: It must be that, according to the differences of places, times, and men for whom the writings were made, they have different causes, arguments, and origins. Just as the blessed John, writing in his Apocalypse to the seven congregations, rebukes in each of them either particular or general vices, or commends their virtues, so also the holy Apostle Paul healed the wounds of each congregation in turn, and did not, like an unskilled physician, wish to cure everyone's eyes with one eye-salve. Then Gratian goes on to show in particular that the reason for enacting a law must be carefully considered. In this way he wishes to resolve what we read above about priestly marriage.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXX.
units.tr: DISTINCTION XXX.

units.la: Gratianus. ILLVD autem, quod superius in Canone Apostolorum, & in Gangrensi Concilio, & in sexta Synodo legitur, Ex causa consideratur, & Ex tempore. Causa fuit hæresis Manichæorum, qui coniugium detestabantur.
units.tr: Gratian. Now, as for what is read above in the Canon of the Apostles, in the Council of Gangra, and in the Sixth Synod, that it is to be judged by cause and by time: the cause was the heresy of the Manichaeans, who detested marriage.

units.la: GRatianus in hanc trigesimam distinctionem congesit integrum penè concilium Gangrense: nõ quòd illud ad Apostolici mandati declarationem, De deligendo unius uxoris viro, quicquam faciat: Sed inde voluit ostendere, Leges alias & alias, ob alias & alias causas, aliáve tempora, quandóque novas rogari, quandóque veteres ac iam desuetas renouari. veluti est, Lex de Presbytera, id est, Presbyteri coniuge, toties repetita. Lex etiam, De nuptiis honorandis. Et aliæ sunt Euangelio Christi minimè contrariæ vel repugnantes. κόλλον nempe non est Ecclesia, Presbyterorum nuptias, & Mulierum cohabitationes damnat, Ergo Nuptias, aut Mulieres damnat. quod Hæretici cauillantur. Hæresis & superstitio noua, vel per multos innouata, multis Canonibus & Conciliis nouis, aut nouandis causa fuit. iuxta verbum vetus, Nouo facto nouum esse quærendum consilium. Quod patres in Gangris aduersus Eustathium monachum veteris Ecclesiasticæ regulæ nouatorem fecerūt. Verumtamen, quia suscepto semel argumento non conueniunt ista, sanè perutilia decreta, sed de rebus longè diuersis propositá, nolumus huc ea cum Gratiano transcribere: Quibus locum proprium, singularémque libellum seruamus. Valde nàmque pertinent ad Ecclesiæ mores, átque Politeam: quosdámque superstitiosos, & Gnosticos æui præsentis actissimè perstringunt, in Catholicorū detestationem perquàm multa facientes & introducentes. Quod autem sufficiat intentioni compilatoris nostri Gratiani, dum vult demonstrare, quòd Leges pro loco, próque tempore ferri debent, Hîc satis fuerit adscripsisse post eum, quę Martinus Episcopus Bracharensis in suam Decretorum confarcinationem cap.57. 58. & 59. transtulit è conciliis Græcis. Inde satis ipse colliges (ut aliis non sit authoritatibus opus) Hæreticos ac Innouatores multis Canonibus & Edictis, alioqui non constituendis, causam dedisse. Contra quos_____
units.tr: In this thirtieth distinction Gratian has gathered almost the whole Council of Gangra. He did not do so because it bears in any way on the declaration of the apostolic command that a man should choose the husband of one wife. Rather, he wished to show from it that laws differ, and are enacted for different causes and at different times; and that sometimes new laws are asked for, and sometimes old ones, long out of use, are revived. An example is the law concerning the presbyteress, that is, the wife of a presbyter, which is repeated so often; and also the law on honouring marriage. And other laws are by no means contrary or repugnant to the Gospel of Christ. Surely the Church, when it condemns the marriages of presbyters and the cohabitation of women, does not thereby condemn marriage or women, as the heretics wrangle. Kollon [κόλλον] (the word stands in the text) ... A heresy or superstition, new or renewed by many, has been the cause of many new canons and councils, or of canons yet to be made, in line with the old saying: when a new deed is done, a new counsel must be sought. This is why the Fathers at Gangra made Eustathius the monk into an innovator against the old ecclesiastical rule. Nevertheless, since these very useful decrees, once the subject has been taken up, do not fit the argument but deal with quite different matters, we do not wish to transcribe them here with Gratian. We reserve them for their own place and a separate little book. For they bear heavily on the customs and polity of the Church, and they sharply attack the superstitious and Gnostic men of the present age, making and introducing a great many things to the detestation of Catholics. As for what is enough for the purpose of our compiler Gratian, who wishes to show that laws ought to be enacted according to place and according to time, it will suffice here to add what Martin, Bishop of Braga, carried over from the Greek councils into his patchwork of decrees, in chapters 57, 58 and 59. From these you will gather for yourself (so that no other authorities are needed) that heretics and innovators gave occasion for many canons and edicts which otherwise would not have been enacted. Against them ...

units.la: Ex concilio Martini Papæ. Qualis hic, Papa, Nec ne, fuerit, superius dicebamus in can.1. dist. 27. & in can. Si quis vidua. 28. dist.
units.tr: From the council of Pope Martin. Whether he was a true pope or not, I said above in the first canon of distinction 27 and in the canon Si quis vidua, distinction 28.

units.la: Anathema reperitur in eos, qui repetunt ac renouant Manichæorum superstitiones, & impias opiniones.
units.tr: An anathema is pronounced against those who revive and renew the superstitions and impious opinions of the Manichaeans.

units.la: SI quis Presbyter, vel Diaconus, propter publicam pœnitentiam à Sacerdote acceptam, absque aliqua necessitate, die Dominicâ pro quadam religione ieiunauerit, sicut Manichæi, Anathema sit.
units.tr: If any presbyter or deacon, having received public repentance from a bishop, fasts on the Lord's day out of some religious scruple, without any necessity, as the Manichaeans do, let him be anathema.

units.la: § Similiter, & quod ab Apostolis traditus Canon tenet antiquus, placuit.—Vt per omnes dies Dominicos, & per omnes dies Paschæ, vsque ad Pentecosten, non prosternant se in oratione, causâ humilitatis: sed recto vultu ad Dominum orationis fungantur officio: quia in his diebus gaudium resurrectionis Domini celebramus.
units.tr: § Likewise, and as the ancient canon handed down from the Apostles holds, it has been decided: that on all Sundays and all days of Easter, up to Pentecost, people should not prostrate themselves in prayer out of humility, but should perform the office of prayer with an upright face toward the Lord, because on these days we celebrate the joy of the Lord's resurrection.

units.la: Item. Ex Can. 14. Concilij Ancyrani.
units.tr: Likewise. From canon 14 of the Council of Ancyra.

units.la: § Si quis etiam, non pro abstinentia, sed pro execratione escarum, à carne abstinet, placuit sancto Concilio, vt prægustet: & si sic vult abstinere, abstineat. Si autem spernit, ita vt olera cocta cum carnibus nō degustet: iste non obediens, nec suspiciones hæresis à se remouens, de clericatus ordine deponatur. Post consideratam Causæ circunstantiam in ferendis & interpretandis legibus, transit Gratianus ad Peristasin temporis, Hac in re plurimùm momenti pariter habentem: Iuxta tritum iam sermone verbum: Distingue tempora, & concordabit Scriptura.
units.tr: § If anyone abstains from meat, not out of self-restraint but out of loathing for foods, the holy Council has decided that he should taste it; and if he still wishes to abstain, let him abstain. But if he despises it, so that he does not even taste the vegetables cooked with meat, he is disobedient and does not remove the suspicion of heresy from himself, and let him be deposed from the order of the clergy. After considering the circumstances of the cause in enacting and interpreting laws, Gratian passes to the circumstance of time [περίστασιν], which is likewise of great importance in this matter, according to the now common saying: Distinguish the times, and Scripture will agree.

units.la: DISTINCTIO. XXXI.
units.tr: DISTINCTION XXXI.

units.la: Gratianus. TEMPVS quoque consideratur: Nam fuit, quando nōdum erat institutum, vt Sacerdotes continentiam seruarent. Vnde Gregorius scribit Petro Subdiacono Siciliæ. In Epistola iā supra citata. 41. libri primi.
units.tr: Gratian. Time also must be considered. For there was a time when it had not yet been instituted that priests should keep continence. Hence Gregory writes to Peter, subdeacon of Sicily, in the letter already cited above, book 1, letter 41.

units.la: Maritus in Hypodiaconum captus, si continentiam tunc non voluerit, ab vxore non separetur.
units.tr: A married man who is taken into the subdiaconate is not to be separated from his wife if he is then unwilling to observe continence.

units.la: Ante triennium, omnium Ecclesiarum Subdiaconi Siciliæ, prohibiti fuerat, ut more Romanæ Ecclesiæ, suis uxoribus nullatenus misceantur: quod mihi datum, atque incompetens videtur: ut qui usum continentiæ non inuenit, neque castitatem promisit, compellatur à sua uxore separari, atque per hoc (quod absit) in deterius cadat. Unde videtur mihi, ut à præsenti die, Episcopis omnibus dicatur, ut nullum facere Subdiaconum præsumant, nisi qui se victurum castè promiserit: quatenus & præterita mala, quæ proposito mentis appetita non sunt, violenter non exigantur: & futura mala caute caveantur. Qui vero post eandem prohibitionem, quæ ante triennium facta est, continenter cum suis uxoribus vixerint, laudandi atque remunerandi sunt, & ut in bono permaneant, exhortandi. Eos autem, qui, post prohibitionem factam, à suis se uxoribus continere noluerint, ad Sacrum ordinem nolumus promoueri: quia nullus debet ad Altaris ministerium accedere, nisi cuius castitas ante susceптum ministerium, fuerit approbata.
units.tr: Three years ago it was prohibited to the subdeacons of all the churches of Sicily that, after the manner of the Roman Church, they should in no way have marital relations with their wives. This has been given to me, and it seems unsuitable: that a man who has not found the practice of continence and has not promised chastity should be compelled to be separated from his wife and thereby (which God forbid) fall into a worse state. Hence it seems to me that from this day on it should be said to all bishops that they must not presume to ordain any subdeacon except one who has promised to live chastely; so that past evils, which were not sought with a resolved mind, are not violently exacted, and future evils are cautiously guarded against. But those who, after the prohibition that was made three years ago, have lived continently with their wives are to be praised and rewarded, and exhorted to remain in good. Those, however, who after the prohibition was made have refused to abstain from their wives, we do not wish to be promoted to sacred orders, because no one ought to approach the ministry of the altar unless his chastity has been approved before he undertakes the ministry.

units.la: Græcis Hypodiaconis futuris (inter Græcos habentur Siculi) Continentia (quæ semper Latinis iniuncta fuit) Gregorij tempore duntaxat imperari cœpit. Antea (quod ex hac Epistola, & Epistola 34. lib. 3. multisque nos ex aliis deprehendimus) erant coniugati. Sed non est bona ratiocinatio Gratiani, à Subdiaconorum nuptiis, ad quoscunque Sacerdotes argumentantis. Cur autem continentes debeant esse altaris Christi ministri, Gratianus ostendit, inquiens.
units.tr: For the future subdeacons of the Greeks (the Sicilians are counted among the Greeks), continence, which was always enjoined on the Latins, began to be commanded only in Gregory's time. Before that, as we gather from this letter, from letter 34 of book 3, and from many others, they were married. But Gratian's reasoning, which argues from the marriages of subdeacons to priests of any kind whatever, is not sound. Why the continent ought to be the ministers of Christ's altar, Gratian shows, saying:

units.la: Causa vero huius institutionis, Munditia fuit Sacerdotalis: ut liberè cunctis diebus vitæ suæ Orationi posint vacare: Si enim (ut Paulus ait) Ab uxoribus est cessandum, ut expeditius orationi vacemus, Ministris vtique altaris, quibus quotidiana necessitas orandi incubit, nunquam coniugali officio vacare permittitur. Unde Beda super Lucă ait. Scribebat hic anno Do. 710. Non extant omnia, quæ scripsit.
units.tr: The reason for this institution was sacerdotal purity: that they might be free to devote themselves to prayer all the days of their life. For if (as Paul says) one must abstain from wives in order to be more free for prayer, then surely the ministers of the altar, on whom the daily necessity of prayer presses, are never permitted to be occupied with the duty of marriage. Hence Bede, on Luke, says: "He was writing here in the year of our Lord 710. Not all that he wrote survives."

units.la: Sacerdotes perpetuò casti sunto.
units.tr: Priests are to be perpetually chaste.

units.la: Sacerdotibus (ut semper valeant altari assistere) semper ab uxoribus est abstinendum, sempérque castitas obseruanda præcipitur. Item. In concilio Carthaginensi. 1. Ex Aphrica tota, Patres Carthaginę frequentissimè conuenerunt, ad Ecclesię regimen multa perutiliter ibi sancientes. Aphricana dicuntur, & Carthaginensia Concilia, quæ nobis octo restant. Ex quibus aliquis Græcus de piis illis & Ecclesiasticis patribus (nec enim puto Græce loquutos Aphros) centum cum triginta quinque transtulit in linguam suam, qui pridem Lutetiæ fuerunt editi. sunt & in Zonaræ collectaneis. Illis autem in conuentibus excelluit Aurelius Augustini chirotonites: Interfuit & ipse frequenter Augustinus. Inter alia semel ad Cœcilium retulit Aurelius (id euenit anno Christi 407.) περὶ ἐγκρατείας, καὶ ἀγνείας λευϊτῶν. De continentia & puritate Leuitarum. Sancitum fuit in 3. Canone Græco, prout hic à Gratiano colligitur. Secundus est in versione Latina.
units.tr: Priests (so that they may always be fit to stand by the altar) must always abstain from their wives, and chastity is always enjoined to be observed. Likewise. In the first canon of the Council of Carthage: from all of Africa the fathers gathered very frequently at Carthage, decreeing there many things most usefully for the governance of the Church. The councils of Africa and of Carthage are so named; eight of them remain to us. From these, some Greek translated one hundred and thirty-five of those pious and ecclesiastical fathers (for I do not think the Africans spoke Greek) into his own language, and these were published some time ago at Paris. They are also in the collections of Zonaras. In those assemblies Aurelius, the chirotonite of Augustine, excelled, and Augustine himself was frequently present. Among other things, Aurelius once reported to Caecilian (this happened in the year of Christ 407) concerning continence and purity of the Levites [περὶ ἐγκρατείας, καὶ ἀγνείας λευϊτῶν]. It was decreed in the third Greek canon, as Gratian gathers here. The second is in the Latin version.

units.la: Quicunque diuinis Sacramentis inseruiunt, (ὑπουργοῦσι θεοῖς καὶ ὑπηρέτησιν) Continentes esse debent.
units.tr: Whoever serve the divine sacraments [ὑπουργοῦσι θεοῖς καὶ ὑπηρέτησιν] ought to be continent.

units.la: E Piscopos, Presbyteros, & Diaconos (ita ut placuit, & decet sacrosanctos Antistites, aut Sacerdotes, aut Leuitas, Vel qui Sacramentis diuinis inseruiunt) Conti- nentes esse decet in omnibus.
units.tr: Bishops, presbyters and deacons (as it has pleased, and as it befits, the most holy prelates, or priests, or Levites, or those who serve the divine sacraments) ought to be continent in all things.

units.la: Postrema verba Canonis hic omisit Gratianus, Vbi Legis nostræ causa redditur, apprimè digna necessariáque scitu. Nam Lascivos iste Nuptiatores mire coarguit; Ideo subiicienda curaui.
units.tr: Gratian here omitted the final words of the canon, in which the reason for our law is given, most worthy and necessary to know. For it strongly refutes those lascivious marriage-mongers; so I have taken care to add them.

units.la: Ὅπως δώῃ ἡμῖν ὁ παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπολλὰς αἰτούντων, ἐπιτυχεῖν· ἵνα καὶ ἡ ἀπόστολοι παραδῶσιν, καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὴν ἀγνείαν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοίως φυλάξωμεν.
units.tr: Ὅπως δώῃ ἡμῖν ὁ παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπολλὰς αἰτούντων, ἐπιτυχεῖν· ἵνα καὶ ἡ ἀπόστολοι παραδῶσιν, καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὴν ἀγνείαν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοίως φυλάξωμεν.

units.la: Id est.
units.tr: That is:

units.la: Vt possint, quòd à Deo simpliciter orant, impetrare: Vt, & quod ab Apostolis traditum est, & ab ipsa Antiquitate obtinuit, & nos similiter obseruemus. Sed eiusdem quoque Concilij Canon quartus huc totus attinet: addendum propterea duxi. Quum Faustinus Episcopus, Ecclesiæ Romanæ Topotlrites, apud Aphros omnes in eo Concilio Legem rogasset, vnanimes ita decreuerunt.
units.tr: That they may obtain from God whatever they simply pray for; and that we likewise observe what was handed down by the apostles and has held from antiquity itself. But the fourth canon of this same council bears wholly on this, so I thought it should be added. When Faustinus, bishop and Topoteretes of the Roman Church, asked the law among all the Africans in that council, they unanimously decreed as follows.

units.la: Ἀ ρέσκει, ἵνα ἐπίσκοπος, καὶ πρεσβύτερος, καὶ διάκονος, καὶ πάντες οἱ τὰ ἱερὰ ψηλαφῶντες, τῆς σωφροσύνης φύλακες, γυναικῶν ἀπέχωνται.
units.tr: Ἀρέσκει, ἵνα ἐπίσκοπος, καὶ πρεσβύτερος, καὶ διάκονος, καὶ πάντες οἱ τὰ ἱερὰ ψηλαφῶντες, τῆς σωφροσύνης φύλακες, γυναικῶν ἀπέχωνται.

units.la: Id est.
units.tr: That is:

units.la: Placuit. Vt Episcopus, Presbyter, Diaconus, & omnes sacra tractantes, Continentiæ obseruatores, à mulieribus abstineant. Itaque more Romano vixerunt Aphri. In virumque Zonaræ videnda foret hermenia, Sed pergamus cum Gratiano.
units.tr: It was decided that the bishop, presbyter, deacon, and all who handle sacred things, being guardians of continence, abstain from women. So the Africans lived in the Roman manner. The commentary of Zonaras on this should be consulted, but let us go on with Gratian.

units.la: Item. Innocentius. 1. Victorino Rothomagensi Episcopo. cap.9. Epist.2.
units.tr: Likewise. Innocent to Victorinus, bishop of Rouen, chapter 9, letter 2.

units.la: Scripta fuit Consulatu Honorij sexto id est, An. Do. 406.
units.tr: It was written in the sixth consulship of Honorius, that is, in the year of our Lord 406.

units.la: Sacerdotes, & Leuitæ cum vxoribus suis misceri non debent.
units.tr: Priests and Levites must not live with their wives.

units.la: TEnere debet Ecclesia, Vt omnimodo Sacerdotes & Leuitæ, cum vxoribus suis non misceantur: quia ministerij diuini quotidianis necessitatibus occupatur. Scriptum est enim: Sancti estote: quoniam ego sanctus sum dominus Deus vester. Nam prisci temporibus, anno vicis suæ, de templo non discedebant: sicut de Zacharia legimus: nec domum suam omnino tangebant: quibus utique, propter sobolis successionem, vxoris vsus fuerat relaxatus: quia ex alia tribu, præterquam ex semine Aaron, ad sacerdotium nullis accedere permittebatur. Quanto magis hi Sacerdotes, & Leuitæ pudicitiâ, ex die ordinationis suæ, seruare debent, quibus vel Sacerdotium, vel Ministerium sine successione est? nec præterit dies, quâ, vel à sacrificiis diuinis, vel à Baptismatis officio vacent?
units.tr: The Church ought to hold firmly that priests and Levites must in every way refrain from living with their wives, because they are occupied with the daily necessities of the divine ministry. For it is written: "Be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy." In earlier times, too, they did not leave the temple during their year of service, as we read of Zechariah, and they did not go near their own houses at all. For them, indeed, use of a wife had been allowed for the sake of succession of offspring, since no one outside the tribe of Aaron was permitted to enter the priesthood. How much more ought these priests and Levites to keep chastity from the day of their ordination, since their priesthood or ministry does not pass by succession? Is there not a day on which they are free from the divine sacrifices or from the duty of baptism?

units.la: § Nam si Apostolus Paulus scripsit ad Corinthios, dicens: Abstinete vos ad tempus, vt expeditius vacetis orationi: & hoc vtique præcepit Laicis: multò magis Sacerdotes (quibus & orandi, & sacrificandi iuge officium est) semper debebunt ab huiusmodi consortio abstinere:
units.tr: § For if the Apostle Paul wrote to the Corinthians, saying, "Abstain for a time, that you may give yourselves more freely to prayer," and certainly commanded this of the laity, then much more should priests (for whom praying and sacrificing is a continual duty) always abstain from such companionship.

units.la: Idem, Exuperio Tholosano Episcopo. Epist 3. cap. 1. Stilicone. 2. & Anthemio cos. Id est, anno 407.
units.tr: The same, to Exuperius, Bishop of Toulouse. Letter 3, chapter 1. In the consulship of Stilicho (for the second time) and Anthemius; that is, in the year 407.

units.la: Qui ab vxoribus suis non abstinent, ad sacrificia non admittantur.
units.tr: Those who do not abstain from their wives are not to be admitted to the sacrifices.

units.la: NEc eos ad sacrificia fas est admitti, qui, vel cum vxore exercent carnale consortium. Ergo vel vxore, vel Sacrificiis abstineto. Item. Hieronymus contra Iouinianum, libro 1.
units.tr: Nor is it lawful for those to be admitted to the sacrifices who practise carnal companionship with their wife. Therefore abstain either from your wife or from the sacrifices. Likewise Jerome, Against Jovinian, book 1.

units.la: Sacerdoti semper est orandum. Matrimonio semper est ergo tarendum.
units.tr: A priest must always pray; therefore marriage must always be avoided.

units.la: S I Laicus, & quicunque fidelis, orare non potest, nisi careat officio coniugali: Sacerdoti, cui semper pro populo offerenda sunt sacrificia, semper est orandum. Si semper orandum est, ergo semper carendmm matrimonio: Nunquam seruiendum coniugio. Quoniam, quotiescūnque vxori debitum reddo, orare non possum.
units.tr: If a layman, and any faithful person, cannot pray unless he is free from conjugal duty, then a priest, for whom sacrifices must always be offered on behalf of the people, must always be praying. If he must always pray, then he must always be free from marriage and never give himself to the married state. For whenever I pay the marital debt to my wife, I cannot pray.

units.la: QVOD autem Manichæorum causâ, de coniugio Sacerdotum illud supradictum sit, ex Gangrensi Concilio apparet, in quo sic statutum legitur, can.1. & can 9.
units.tr: That the foregoing was said about the marriage of priests for the sake of the Manichaeans appears from the Council of Gangra, in which the following is read as decreed, canon 1 and canon 9.

units.la: Anathema Nuptiarum vituperatoribus, & etiam virginitatis causâ, Nuptiarum taxatoribus.
units.tr: Anathema to those who disparage marriage, and also to those who find fault with marriage for the sake of virginity.

units.la: SI quis vituperat nuptias, & dormientem cum viro suo fidelem, ac religiosam mulierem detestatur, aut culpabilem existimat, velut quæ regnum Dei introire non possit, Anathema sit.
units.tr: If anyone disparages marriage, and detests a faithful and religious woman who sleeps with her husband, or judges her guilty, as though she could not enter the kingdom of God, let him be anathema.

units.la: QVicunque virginitatem custodiens, aut continentiæ studens, velut horrescēs nuptias: nec propter hoc, quòd bonum & sanctum est, nomen virginitatis assumit, Anathema sit. Gratianus. POTEST & aliter illud intelligi, quod in Canone Apostolorum legitur, vt iste sit sensus capituli. Si quis docet Sacerdotem, vxorem suam contemnere, non quam in Sacerdotio accepit, sed quam ante Sacerdotium, dum adhuc esset laicus, vel in minoribus ordinibus constitutus, sibi copulauit: cum qua continentiam professus est, quum ad sacros Ordines conscenderet: quam nullus debet contemnere, hoc est, ab animo & cura sua abiicere, quin ei necessaria prouideat, Anathema sit. Probatur autem hæc interpretatio authoritate Leonis Papæ primi, qui scribens Rustico Narbonensi Episcopo, ait: Epist.90.cap.3. circiter an.Do.465.
units.tr: Whoever, keeping virginity or devoted to continence, shrinks from marriage as if it were abhorrent, and on that account takes up the name of virginity, which is good and holy, let him be anathema. Gratian. It can also be understood otherwise, as read in the Canon of the Apostles, so that this is the sense of the chapter: If anyone teaches that a priest should despise his wife, not the one he took in the priesthood but the one he joined to himself before the priesthood, while he was still a layman or held a minor order, and with whom he professed continence when he ascended to the holy orders, let him be anathema; she must not be despised, that is, cast off from his mind and care, but he must provide her with what is necessary. This interpretation is confirmed by the authority of Pope Leo the First, who, writing to Rusticus, Bishop of Narbonne, says: (Letter 90, chapter 3, about the year 465.)

units.la: Amplexum, non curam deserat vxoris, quisquis est in ministerio Altaris.
units.tr: Whoever is in the ministry of the altar should not abandon the embrace, nor neglect the care, of his wife.

units.la: LEx continentiæ eadem est Altaris ministris, quæ Episcopis, aut Præbyteris: qui quum essent Laici, siue Lectores, licitè quidem, & vxores ducere, & filios procreare potuerunt: sed quum ad prædictos peruenerunt gradus, cœpit eis non licere, quod licuit. Vnde, vt iam de Carnali fiat Spirituale coniugium, oportet eos nec dimittere vxores: licet qui habent, sic habere videantur, quasi non habeât: quò, & salua sit castitas connubiorum, & cessent opera nuptiarum. Item. Leo. 9. contra Epistolam Niceta Abbatis. In Pannomiæ libro 3. in fine tituli, De continentia ordinandorum, refertur hoc decretum. Non legi quicquam de libidinoso illo Niceta monacho: qui (quod Gnostici modò quoque faciunt) armis coniugij Sacerdotales defendebat incontinentias. Sed in Chronico, & in Krantzij Saxonia lib. 4. cap. 43. legi factum Papam, Leonem nonum, hominem Gallum, multa commendatum probitate. Anno Do. 1049. quinque annos. Synodos quatuor annis primis habuit, Vnam Romæ: Secundam, Papiæ Tertiam, Remis. Moguntiæ, postremam: cui Theutonum rex Henricus secundus interfuit, anno Do. circiter 1051. Huius postremæ iudicio (in qua 150. Episcopos quidam scripserunt: alij tantùm 40.) damnata perpetuò fuere connubia Sacerdotalia, cuius tum per Alemanniam fædabatur Ecclesiæ puritas: Damnatum pariter puto, & illam nuptiatorem Niceten. Depromptus inde videtur canon præsens ab Iuone. Alat, non amplectatur vxorem suam, Minister. OMnino confitemur non licere Episcopo, Presbytero, Diacono propriam vxorem, causâ religionis, abiicere à cura sua: sed vt ei victum & vestitum largiatur: sed non vt cum illa carnaliter ex more iaceat: sicut & sanctos Apostolos legimus egisse: beato Paulo apostolo dicente: Nunquid non habemus potestatem, Mulierem sororem circunducendi, sicut & cæteri Apostoli, & fratres Domini, & Cephas? Vide(insipiens) quia non dixit, Nunquid non habemus potestatem, sororem mulierem amplectendi, sed circunducendi: scilicet, vt mercede prædicationis sustentaretur ab eis: nec tamen deinceps ulterius foret carnale inter eos coniugium. Gratianus. V Tigitur ex his authoritatibus apparet, Sacerdotes vxoribus, quas in Laicali habitu, vel in minoribus ordinibus constituti, sibi legitimè copulauerunt, necessaria quidem ministrare debent, sed debitum reddere non valent. Non cessat argumentari Gratianus. Vt igitur ex his authoritatibus apparet, Sacerdotes vxoribus, quas in Laicali habitu, vel in minoribus ordinibus constituti, sibi legitimè copulauerunt, necessaria quidem ministrare debent, sed debitum reddere non valent. Non cessat argumentari
units.tr: The law of continence is the same for the ministers of the altar as for bishops or elders. When they were laymen, or readers, they were certainly permitted to take wives and to beget children; but when they reached the aforesaid grades, what had been allowed began to be forbidden to them. Hence, so that the carnal marriage may become a spiritual one, they ought not to put away their wives; those who have them should have them as though they had them not, so that chastity in marriages is preserved and the works of marriage cease. Likewise Leo 9, against the letter of Nicetas the Abbot. In the third book of the Pannonian collection, at the end of the title On the continence of those being ordained, this decree is cited. I have not read anything about that lustful monk Nicetas, who (as the Gnostics do even today) defended the incontinence of priests with the weapons of marriage. But in the Chronicle, and in Krantz's Saxonia, book 4, chapter 43, I have read that Pope Leo IX, a Frenchman commended for many virtues, was made pope in the year 1049 and held the office for five years. In the first four years he held synods: one at Rome, a second at Pavia, a third at Reims, and the last at Mainz, which King Henry II of the Germans attended, about the year 1051. By the judgment of this last synod (at which some have written that 150 bishops were present, others only 40), priestly marriages were condemned for ever, and at that time the purity of the Church was being defiled throughout Germany. I think that Nicetas, that advocate of marriage, was condemned in the same way. The present canon seems to have been taken from Ivo. Let the minister not embrace his wife. We wholly confess that it is not lawful for a bishop, a presbyter, or a deacon, for the sake of religion, to cast off his own wife from his care, but he should provide her with food and clothing; yet not so that he lies with her carnally, as we read that the holy apostles did, the blessed Apostle Paul saying: "Have we not the right to lead about a sister as a wife, as do the other apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?" See, foolish man, that he did not say, "Have we not the right to embrace a wife who is a sister," but "to lead about"; namely, so that they might be supported by them as payment for preaching, and yet there should be no further carnal marriage between them. Gratian. From these authorities, therefore, it appears that priests must indeed provide necessities for the wives whom they lawfully took while in lay dress or while holding minor orders, but they cannot render the marital debt. Gratian does not cease arguing. units.la: gumentari Gratianus pro nuptiis Presbyterorum, Inquiens. ______ Sed obiicitur illud Tripertitæ Historiæ. cap-14.lib.2. Cassiodorus, illius compilator Historiæ, de Sozomeno dicit hoc excerptum: quod habes in cap.23. libri primi Ecclesiasticæ Historiæ, ab Hermio Sozomeno descriptæ.
units.tr: arguing, Gratian, in favour of the marriages of presbyters, saying: ______ But there is objected that passage of the Tripartite History, book 2, chapter 14. Cassiodorus, the compiler of that history, takes this excerpt from Sozomen, which you have in chapter 23 of book 1 of the Ecclesiastical History written by Hermias Sozomen.

units.la: Dissuasit Paphnutij Nicæna Synodus non constituit, quòd Presbyteri cum suis vxoribus non dormirent.
units.tr: The Nicene Synod, persuaded by Paphnutius, did not enact that presbyters should not sleep with their wives.

units.la: NIcæna Synodus volens corrigere hominum vitam in Ecclesiis commorantium, posuit Leges, quas Canones vocamus. In quorum tractatu videbatur aliquibus introducere Legem, Vt Episcopi, Presbyteri, Diaconi, Subdiaconi cum coniugibus, quas ante consecrationem duxerant, non dormirent. Surgens autem Paphnutius confessor contradixit, Honorabiles confessus nuptias: & castitatem dicens esse, cum propria coniuge concubitu. Suasit itaque Concilio, ne tale poneret Legem: graue esse asserens causam, quæ aut ipsis, aut eorum coniugalibus occasio fornicationis existeret. Et hoc quidem Paphnutius (licet nuptiarum esset inexpertus) exposuit, Synodúsque laudauit sententiam eius: & nihil ex hac parte sanciuit: sed hoc in uniuscuiusque voluntate, non necessitate, dimisit.
units.tr: Nicene Synod, wishing to correct the lives of men who dwelt in the churches, set down laws, which we call canons. In the discussion of these, some seemed to introduce a law that bishops, presbyters, deacons, and subdeacons should not sleep with the wives whom they had married before their consecration. But Paphnutius, a confessor, rose and objected, declaring that marriage is honourable and that intercourse with one's own lawful wife is chastity. So he persuaded the council not to make such a law, asserting that it was a grave matter, which could become an occasion of fornication for themselves or for their wives. Paphnutius (although he had no experience of marriage) set this out, and the synod praised his opinion and enacted nothing in this respect, but left it to each man's will, not to necessity.

units.la: Hic debuit addi, contra nuptiatores, quod est in dicto cap. 23. vt plane sciretur, quo ritu Græcia vixerit.______
units.tr: Here it ought to be added, against those who favour marriage, what is in the said chapter 23, so that it may plainly be known in what manner Greece lived.

units.la: Κατὰ δὲ, πῶ ἀρχαίαν τ' ἐκκλησίας παράδοσιν, τοὺς μὲν ἀγάμους τῶ ἱσραλικῶν τάγματος κοινωνήσαντας, μηκέτι γαμεῖν. τοὺς δὲ μεταλαμοῦ, ὧν ἔχουσι γαμετῶν, μὴ χωρίζεσθαι.
units.tr: Κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἀρχαίαν τῆς ἐκκλησίας παράδοσιν, τοὺς μὲν ἀγάμους τοῦ ἱερατικοῦ τάγματος κοινωνήσαντας, μηκέτι γαμεῖν· τοὺς δὲ μετὰ τὸ γῆμαι, τῶν ἐχόντων γαμετῶν, μὴ χωρίζεσθαι. [According to the ancient tradition of the Church, those who are unmarried and have entered the priestly order should no longer marry; but those who have married, from those who have wives, should not separate from them.]

units.la: Id est.
units.tr: That is:

units.la: Secundùm verò priscam Ecclesiæ traditionem, Qui sunt sine coniugibus in Ordine sacro viri, ne posthac amplius coniuges ducant. Post nuptias autem, ab vxoribus, quas habent, ne secedant.
units.tr: According to the early tradition of the Church: men who are without wives and have entered the sacred order should not afterwards take wives; but after marriage, they should not separate from the wives they have.

units.la: Scilicet. Ante nuptias, in clerum cooptatus, ad nuptias amplius non adspiret. Sed, non sciungatur ab ea, quam, quum Laicus adhuc esset, ante clericatum duxit. Hoc in Nicæno statutum Concilio (prout antiquissimum fuerat Ecclesiæ priscæ mos) refert & Socrates cap.
units.tr: Clearly: before marriage, a man chosen for the clergy should not aspire to marriage afterwards. But he should not be separated from the wife whom, while still a layman, he married before taking orders. This is laid down in the Nicene Council (as was the most ancient custom of the early Church), and Socrates also reports it in the second chapter of the first book.

units.la: G
units.tr: G

units.la: ii. libri primi. Rursum, Gratianus. ________ Item. Synodus sexta. Est hoc.13. caput illius Synodi non hic integrè versum, nec aliubi, satis fideliter.
units.tr: Book two of the first part. Again, Gratian. ________ Likewise, the Sixth Synod. This is the thirteenth canon of that Synod, not rendered fully here, nor elsewhere quite faithfully.

units.la: Si quis ad Sacerdotium de coniugio capiatur, non propterea debet inuitus à coniugis suæ congressu disiungi: nisi tempore sacrificij.
units.tr: If anyone is taken from marriage into the priesthood, he ought not, against his will, to be separated from the company of his wife, except at the time of sacrifice.

units.la: QVoniam in Romani ordine Canonis esse cognouimus traditum, Eos † qui ordinati sunt Diaconi vel Presbyteri, confiteri quòd non suis iam copulentur uxoribus. Nos antiquum sequêtes Canonem Apostolicæ diligentiæ & constitutionis: Sacrorum virorum Legales nuptias amodo valere volumus: nullo modo cum uxoribus suis eorum † connubia dissoluentes, aut priuantes eos * familiaritate adinuicem, in tempore oportuno. † Quicunque ergo diligens inuentus fuerit in Subdiaconali ordinatione, aut Diaconali, aut Sacerdotali, hi nullo modo prohibeantur ad talem ascendere gradum † pro uxoris suæ cohabitatione: nec etiam tempore ordinationis suæ prositeri [castitatem] cogatur, quòd † abstinere debeat à Legalis uxoris familiaritate. Gratianus hinc transilit ad finem Canonis, emittens media quædam non impertinentia: præcipuè, quod est ex Ecclesiastè.ca.3.
units.tr: Since we have learned that it is handed down in the order of the Roman Canon that those who have been ordained deacons or presbyters should profess that they no longer live with their wives, we, following the ancient canon of apostolic diligence and constitution, wish that the lawful marriages of holy men remain valid from now on, in no way dissolving their marriages with their wives, nor depriving them of mutual companionship at the appropriate time. Therefore, whoever is found diligent in ordination to the subdiaconate, the diaconate, or the priesthood, let such a man in no way be prevented from ascending to that rank on account of living with his lawful wife; nor, at the time of his ordination, let him be compelled to profess [chastity] that he must abstain from the company of his lawful wife. Gratian here skips to the end of the canon, omitting some intervening matter that is not pertinent, especially what comes from Ecclesiastes, chapter 3.

units.la: κaιρὸν ὡὴ παντὸς πεὰγματος · μὴ μάλισα, υἱσείας, μὴ προσυχῆς.
units.tr: There is a time for every matter; especially of fasting and of prayer [καιρὸν ἐν παντὶ πράγματι · μάλιστα νηστείας καὶ προσευχῆς].

units.la: Id est.
units.tr: That is:

units.la: Suà cuique negocio tempestiuitas est. & maximè, Ieiunio, atque Orationi. Deinde sequitur.
units.tr: Every business has its proper season, and most of all fasting and prayer. Then follows:

units.la: § Oportet igitur eos qui * altari ministrant, in tempore * oblationis Sanctorum, Continentes esse in omnibus, ut à Deo possint consequi, quæ † supplicitèr postulant. Si quis ergo præsumpserit, Contra Apostolicos Canones, aliquos † consecratorum (Presbyterorum, dico, & Diaconorum, & Subdiaconorum) priuate à contactu, & à communione Legalis uxoris suæ, deponatur. Similiter &
units.tr: Therefore those who minister at the altar must be continent in all things, at the time of the oblation of the saints, so that they may obtain from God what they humbly ask. If anyone therefore presumes, contrary to the apostolic canons, to separate any of the consecrated (I mean presbyters, deacons, and subdeacons) from contact with and communion with his lawful wife, let him be deposed. Likewise:

units.la: Presbyter, aut Diaconus, qui religionis causa uxorem suam expellit, Excommunicetur: si vero in hoc permanserit, Deponatur. Hoc autem, Ex loco intelligendum est: Orientalis enim Ecclesia (cui sexta Synodus regulam viuendi praescripsit) votum castitatis in ministris altaris non suscepit. Unde Stephanus Papa ait:
units.tr: A presbyter or deacon who casts out his wife for the sake of religion is to be excommunicated; but if he persists in this, he is to be deposed. This, however, must be understood with reference to place: for the Eastern Church (for which the Sixth Synod prescribed a rule of living) did not take on a vow of chastity for the ministers of the altar. Hence Pope Stephen says:

units.la: Occidentalis, non Orientalis Ecclesia, votum castitatis obtulit.
units.tr: The Western Church, not the Eastern Church, has undertaken a vow of chastity.

units.la: A Liter se Orientalium traditio habet Ecclesiarum, aliter huius sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae: nam earum Sacerdotes, Diaconi, aut Subdiaconi matrimonio copu- lantur.
units.tr: The tradition of the Eastern Churches is one thing, and that of this holy Roman Church another: for their priests, deacons, and subdeacons are joined in marriage.

units.la: Istius autem Ecclesiae, vel Occidentalium nullus Sacerdotum, a Subdiacono usque ad Episcopum, licentiam habet coniugium sortiendi. Solvit insuper Gratianus et alia in superioribus proposita: Rerum, Locique distinctione facta, sic dicens. Similiter & capitulum Nicolai ex loco consideratur: quia gens Bulgarorum nouiter ad fidem conuersa, propositum Sacrae religionis ex integro assumere nondum didicerat. Quod autem in cap. sextae Synodi, Presbyter non legitimis nuptiis detentus, punitur: non legales nuptiae, sunt intelligendae secundae, a quibus, authoritate Canonica, Sacerdos quilibet debet esse immunis. Illud autem Gangrensis Concilii, Si quis discernit Presbyterum coniugatum, &c. similiter intelligendum est, vel localiter traditum, vel Coniugatum ab ea esse appellatum, quam ante tempus ordinationis suae duxerat. Illud quoque Martini, Si Subdiaconus secundam duxerit uxorem, non dissimiliter intelligendum est: Primam enim uxorem ante Subdiaconatum habere permittitur: quā defuncta, vel castitatem professa, promovetur iste ad Subdiaconatum: promotus autem si secundas desiderauerit nuptias, sententiae Martini subiacebit. Concludit Gratianus, quod omnes Ecclesiastici, etiam Subdiaconi, continentes esse debent. Id authoritatibus diuersis adhuc confirmat.
units.tr: But none of the priests of this Church, or of the Western Churches, from the subdeacon up to the bishop, has licence to contract marriage. Gratian further resolves the other matters proposed above, by drawing a distinction of matters and places, saying thus. Likewise, the canon of Nicholas is to be considered in light of its place: because the people of the Bulgarians, newly converted to the faith, had not yet learned to take up the purpose of the sacred religion anew. As for the canon of the Sixth Synod, which punishes a presbyter held in a non-lawful marriage, "non-lawful marriages" are to be understood as second marriages, from which, by canonical authority, any priest ought to be free. The statement of the Council of Gangra, "If anyone separates a married presbyter," etc., likewise is to be understood either as locally transmitted, or as referring to a wife whom he had married before the time of his ordination. The saying of Martin also, "If a subdeacon takes a second wife," is to be understood in no different way: for he is permitted to have a first wife before becoming a subdeacon; when she has died, or has professed chastity, he is promoted to the subdiaconate; but if, once promoted, he desires a second marriage, he falls under the sentence of Martin. Gratian concludes that all clergy, even subdeacons, ought to be continent. He further confirms this by various authorities.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXXII.
units.tr: DISTINCTION XXXII.

units.la: Gratianus. SERVANDA est ergo Continentia ab omnibus in sacris ordinibus constitutis: Unde Leo Papa primus ait Epist. 8. cap. 3. & 4. Ad Ecclesiae Thessalonicensis Episcopum scripta est Epistola: Vt scias Graecos hac lege coercitos fuisse.
units.tr: Gratian. Continence, therefore, must be observed by all who are established in holy orders. Hence Pope Leo I says in Epistle 8, chapters 3 and 4: An epistle was written to the Bishop of the Church of Thessalonica, so that you may know that the Greeks were restrained by this law:

units.la: Matrimonio, simul et altaris ministerio, seruire nemo potest.
units.tr: No one can serve both marriage and the ministry of the altar.

units.la: OMnium Sacerdotum tam excellens est electio, ut hæc, quæ in aliis membris Ecclesiæ vacât à culpa, in illis tamen habeantur illicita: Cùm enim extra Clericorum ordinem constitutis, nuptiarum societati, & procreationi filiorum studere sit liberum, ad exhibendam tamen perfectæ continentiæ puritatem, ne Subdiaconis quidem carnale connubium conceditur: ut etiam qui habent, sint tanquam non habentes: & qui non habent, permaneant singulares. Quòd si in hoc ordine, qui quartus extat à capite, dignum est custodiri: quanto magis in primo, vel in secundo, tertióve seruandum est? ne aut Leuitico ministerio, aut Presbyterali honori, aut Episcopali excellentiæ quisquam idoneus existimetur, qui se à voluptate uxoria necdum refrenasse detegitur.
units.tr: The election of all priests is so excellent that, although this practice is free from blame in the other members of the Church, it is nevertheless regarded as unlawful in them. For while those who are outside the order of clergy are free to pursue the fellowship of marriage and the begetting of children, yet, to display the purity of perfect continence, not even subdeacons are granted carnal wedlock, so that even those who have wives should be as though they had none, and those who have none should remain unmarried. But if it is right to guard this in the order that stands fourth from the head, how much more must it be observed in the first, or the second, or the third? So that no one may be thought fit for the Levitical ministry, the presbyterial honour, or the episcopal eminence, if he is found not yet to have restrained himself from the pleasure of a wife.

units.la: Subdiaconi easli sunto.
units.tr: Let subdeacons be chaste.

units.la: MVltorum relatione comperimus, hanc apud vos consuetudinem olim tenuisse, Ut Subdiaconi suis licitè misceantur uxoribus. Quod ne denuò quisquam præsumeret, à seruo Dei, sedis nostræ Diacono, ex authoritate nostri prædecessoris, est isto modo prohibitum, Ut eodem tempore, hi qui iam uxoribus fuerant copulati, unum de duobus eligerent, id est, aut à suis uxoribus abstinerent, aut certè ministrare nullo modo præsumerent. Et quantùm dicitur, Speciosus, tunc Subdiaconus, pro loco ab administratione se suspendit officio, & usque in obitus sui tempus, Notarij quidem gessit officium, & à ministerio, quod Subdiaconum oportuerat exhibere, cessauit.
units.tr: We have learned from the report of many that among you it was once the custom for subdeacons to take wives lawfully. So that no one should presume to do this again, it has been forbidden in this manner, on the authority of our predecessor, by the servant of God, the deacon of our see: that at the same time those who were already joined to wives should choose one of two things, namely either to abstain from their wives or at least not presume to minister in any way. And, as is said, Speciosus, then a subdeacon, withdrew from the office of administration for the place, and until the time of his death he performed the office of notary only, and ceased from the ministry which a subdeacon ought to have rendered.

units.la: § De cætero verò, Fraternitas tua sit omnino solicita, ut quos ad hoc officium contigerit promoueri, hoc quàm maximè diligenter inspiciat: Ne, si uxores habent, miscendi se cum eis licentiâ potiantur: sed ad similitudinem Apostolicæ sedis, eos cuncta obseruare, suâ nihilominus distinctione, constituat. Item. Gregorius, Augustino Anglorum Episcopo. Ad interrogationem. 2. respondens.
units.tr: § For the rest, let your Brotherhood be wholly careful that, whoever is to be promoted to this office, be examined with the greatest diligence, so that, if they have wives, they may not obtain licence to mix with them; but, after the likeness of the Apostolic See, let him establish that they observe all things, with his own discretion nonetheless. Likewise, Gregory, to Augustine, Bishop of the English, answering the second question.

units.la: Hieraticos tantùm, Non item exteros Ecclesiæ ministros, coniugium priuat Ecclesiæ stipendiis. Huc omnia de clericalibus connubiis dicta referenda sunt.
units.tr: Marriage deprives of the stipends of the Church only those who are of the priestly order, not foreign ministers of the Church. All that has been said concerning clerical marriages must be referred to this.

units.la: SI qui verò sunt Clerici extra sacros Ordines constituti, qui se continere non possunt, sortiri uxores debent, & stipendia sua exteriùs accipere: quia & de eisdem à patribus nouimus scriptum, quòd diuidebant singulis, prout cuique opus erat. De eorum ergo stipendiis cogitandum, atque prouidendum est, & sub Ecclesiastica regula sunt tenendi, ut bonis moribus viuant, & canendis psalmis inuigilent, & ab omnibus illicitis, & cor, & linguam, & corpus, Deo authore, conseruent. Item. Nicolaus Papa Othoni, Coloniensi Archiepiscopo. Quinque fuerunt hoc nomine Pontifices, Primum, Secundumue oportuit esse, qui hæc rescripserit. Ille Romanus, Anno Christi 860. Hic Celta Burgundus, anno Do. 1060. vel. 1059. Reliquos Nicolaos antecessit Gratianus, qui scripsit hæc 1150. Posteriorem fuisse credo, qui nominatur in Pannomia lib. 3. Tit. De lapsis. Nicolaus iunior, cuius est & aliud decretum sequens.
units.tr: But if there are clerics who are established outside the holy orders and who cannot contain themselves, they ought to take wives and receive their stipends outside the Church, because we know it was also written by the Fathers concerning these men that they distributed to each according as each had need. Therefore thought and provision must be given to their stipends, and they are to be kept under ecclesiastical rule, so that they may live with good morals, keep watch in singing psalms, and preserve heart, tongue and body from all unlawful things, with God as author. Likewise, Pope Nicholas to Otto, Archbishop of Cologne. There have been five Pontiffs of this name; the one who wrote these rescripts must have been the first or the second. The first was the Roman, in the year of Christ 860; the second was the Celtic Burgundian, in the year of the Lord 1060 or 1059. Gratian, who wrote these things in 1150, preceded the other Nicholases. I believe it was the later one, who is named in Pannomia, book 3, title On the lapsed, Nicholas the Younger, whose other decree follows.

units.la: Subdiacono non licet uxorem ducere.
units.tr: A subdeacon may not take a wife.

units.la: DE illo Clerico, Aluerico, nomine, quem per ordines Ecclesiasticos, usque ad Subdiaconatum, castum vixisse dicitis: cur vestrâ authoritate, uxorem duxerit, miramur: eo quòd nulli unquam (exceptis illis, quibus Ecclesiastica regula habere permittit) uxorem habendi licentiam damus. Item. Nicolaus Papa omnibus Episcopis. Mox atque fuit hic in Papam creatus, Concilium habuit apud Lateranum Romae, quo venit et Berengarius haeresin recantans. Ibi vetus hoc statutum fuit a Synodo renovatum.
units.tr: Concerning that cleric Alveric, whom you say lived chastely through the ecclesiastical orders up to the subdiaconate, we marvel that by your authority he took a wife, since we never grant licence to have a wife to anyone, except to those whom the ecclesiastical rule permits. Likewise, Pope Nicholas to all bishops. As soon as he was created Pope here, he held a council at the Lateran in Rome, to which Berengar also came, recanting his heresy. There this old statute was renewed by the Synod.

units.la: Ab impuro Presbytero pura sacra nulla sunt accipienda: cum quo nec alij communicare debent.
units.tr: No holy things are to be received from an impure presbyter; nor should others communicate with him.

units.la: NVllus missam audiat Presbyteri, quem scit concubinam indubitanter habere, aut Subintroductam mulierem. Item Alexander. 2.
units.tr: Let no one hear the Mass of a presbyter whom he knows undoubtedly to have a concubine, or a woman introduced under cover. Likewise, Alexander II.

units.la: PRaetet hoc autem, Praecipiendo mandamus, ut nullus missam audiat Presbyteri, quem scit concubinam habere indubitanter, vel Subintroductam mulierem. Unde etiam sancta Synodus hoc capitulum sub excommunicatione statuit, dicens: Quicunque Sacerdotum, Diaconorum, Subdiaconorum, post constitutum beatae memoriae praedecessoris nostri sancti Leonis Papae, et Nicolai, De castitate clericorum, concubinam palam duxerit, vel ductam non reliquerit, Ex parte omnipotentis Dei, et authoritate principum Apostolorum Petri et Pauli praecipimus, et omnino contradicimus, ut Missas non cantet, nec etiam Euangelium legat, neque Epistolam ad missam, neque in Presbyterio cum his, qui praefatae constitutioni obedientes fuerint, ad officia divina maneat, neque partem ab Ecclesia suscipiat.
units.tr: Moreover, by precept we command that no one hear the Mass of a presbyter whom he knows undoubtedly to have a concubine, or a woman introduced under cover. Hence also the holy Synod has established this chapter under excommunication, saying: Whoever of priests, deacons or subdeacons, after the constitution of our predecessors of blessed memory, Pope Leo and Nicholas, On the chastity of clerics, has openly taken a concubine, or has not put away one he has taken, we command by the authority of Almighty God and the princes of the Apostles Peter and Paul, and wholly forbid, that he is not to sing Masses, nor read the Gospel, nor the Epistle at Mass, nor remain in the presbytery with those who, obedient to the aforesaid constitution, perform the divine offices, nor receive a portion from the Church.

units.la: Honesta, et religiosa Clericorum vita est, In Ecclesia peristylis una morari, undeque viuere.
units.tr: It is an honest and religious life for clerics to dwell together in one colonnade, and to live in one house.

units.la: § Praecipientes etiam statuimus, Ut hi praedictorum ordinum, qui eisdem praedecessoribus nostris obedientes castitatem seruauerint, iuxta Ecclesias (sicut oportet religiosos Clericos) simul manducent, & dormiant: & quicquid eis ab Ecclesiis competit, hoc communiter habeant.
units.tr: § We also decree, by precept, that those of the aforesaid orders who, obedient to our predecessors, have kept chastity, shall eat and sleep together beside the churches (as religious clerics ought), and whatever is due to them from the churches they shall hold in common.

units.la: Ad Oblationes, & Decimas, & Primitias tenentur Laici: Ad illarum dispensationem tenentur Episcopi. Quicunque has malâ fide retinent, sunt excommunicandi.
units.tr: On Oblations, tithes and firstfruits are owed by the laity; the disposition of them belongs to the bishops. Whoever keep these in bad faith are to be excommunicated.

units.la: § Deinde, Vt decimae, & primitiae, seu oblationes viuorum & mortuorum, Ecclesiis Dei fideliter reddatur à Laicis: & vt ipsae in dispositione Episcoporum sint: quas qui retinuerint, à sanctae Ecclesiae communione separentur. Gratianus hic, velut occasionem captans argumentandi, quaestionem relinquens propositam, Quid est (scilicet) quòd vnius vir vxoris exigatur Ecclesiae minister? dissentat, An mali, & non canonici Sacrorum ministri, sacra bene possint & canonice tractare? Posseque probat. Sed hoc non ita, vt dicitur. Attamen, Parergum tractabimus obiter.
units.tr: § Next, that tithes and firstfruits, or the oblations of the living and the dead, be faithfully rendered by the laity to the Churches of God, and that they be at the disposal of the bishops; whoever retain them are to be separated from the communion of the holy Church. Gratian here, as if seizing an occasion for argument, leaves the question proposed, namely: what is it (that is) that a minister of the Church must be the husband of one wife? He disputes whether evil and uncanonical ministers of sacred things can handle sacred things well and canonically. He proves that they can. But this is not so, as is said. Nevertheless, we shall treat this digression in passing.

units.la: Gratianus. VERUM Principia harum authoritatum contraire videntur Hieronymo, Augustino, & caeteris: qui Christi Sacramenta neque in bono, neque in malo homine fugienda demonstrant: sicut subsequens causa Simoniacorum plenius demonstrat. Sed Vrbanus. 2. in Epistola destinata Praeposito Sancti Vincentii hanc contrarietatem determinat, dicens. De hoc Vrbano secundo dicemus, Can. abhinc quinto.
units.tr: Gratian. TRUE, the principles of these authorities seem to contradict Jerome, Augustine and the others, who show that the sacraments of Christ are to be avoided neither in a good man nor in a bad man, as the following case of the Simoniacs demonstrates more fully. But Urban II, in an epistle addressed to the Provost of Saint Vincent, resolves this contrariety, saying: We shall speak of this Urban II in the canon "abhinc quinto".

units.la: Inquinatus minister non inquinat Sacra, quae contrectat.
units.tr: An impure minister does not defile the sacred things he handles.

units.la: AD hoc verò, quod subiungitur in eadem Epistola, id est, Vtrùm sit vtendum ordinationibus, & reliquis Sacramentis à criminosis exhibitis, vt ab adulteris, vel sanctimonialium violatoribus, vel huiusmodi? Ad hoc, inquam, respondemus. Si schismate, vel haeresi ab Ecclesia non separentur, eorundem ordinationes, & reliqua Sacramenta, sancta, & venerandà non negamus, sequendo beatum Augustinum, qui super Ioannem de huiusmodi tam copiose, quàm veraciter disserit. Ait enim: Baptizat seruus, siue bonus, siue malus. Nesciat se ille, qui baptizatur, baptizati, nisi ab eo qui sibi baptizandi dedit potestatem: Et paulò post. Non abhorreat columba ministerium malorum, sed respiciat Domini potestate.
units.tr: As to what follows in the same Epistle, namely, whether ordinations and the other sacraments administered by criminals, such as adulterers, violators of nuns, or men of that kind, should be used: to this, I say, we reply that if they are not cut off from the Church by schism or heresy, we do not deny that their ordinations and the other sacraments are holy and venerable, following the blessed Augustine, who discusses this so fully and so truly in his commentary on John. For he says: "A servant baptizes, whether good or bad. The one who is baptized does not know that he is baptized, except by the one who gave him the power to baptize." And a little later: "The dove does not shrink from the ministry of the wicked, but looks to the power of the Lord."

units.la: Qui malâ suâ conscientiâ non arcetur à mysteriis, debet illinc arceri pudore.
units.tr: One who is not kept from the mysteries by his own evil conscience ought to be kept from them by shame.

units.la: § Attamen prædecessores nostri Nicolaus & Gregorius à Missis Sacerdotum, quos tales revera esse constituerit, Fideles abstinere decreuerunt: ut & peccandi licentiam cæteris auferrent, & huiusmodi ad dignæ pœnitentiæ lamenta reuocarent.
units.tr: § Yet our predecessors Nicholas and Gregory decreed that the faithful should abstain from the Masses of priests whom they had determined to be such in fact, both to take away from the others license to sin, and to call such men back to the lamentations of worthy repentance.

units.la: Scribit enim prædecessor noster Gregorius Rodolpho & Bertolpho ducibus, inter cætera: Officium Simoniacorum, & in fornicatione iacentium, scienter nullo modo recipiatis: & quantum potestis, tales à sanctis ministeriis, vbi oportuerit, prohibeatis.. Hic fuit Gregorius septimus: successor Alexandri 2. circiter annum Do. 1074. persecutor, & hostis acerrimus istiusmodi flagitiosorum Presbyterorum: qui suis incestis concubitibus Alemaniam totam, coniugij nomine, tunc temporis inquinabant: quæ diuulsit, atque dissoluit omnia.
