Rudolphus, & Bertolphus fratres, Sueuiæ duces: postea Rudolphus contendit de regno Theutonico aduersus Henricum quartum, Ecclesiæ Romanæ perduellem infensissimum. Sequitur in vrbani Papæ literis.
units.tr: For our predecessor Gregory writes, among other things, to the dukes Rudolf and Berthold: "You must knowingly receive in no way the office of simoniacs and of those lying in fornication, and, as far as you can, you must keep such men from holy ministries wherever it is necessary." This was Gregory VII, successor of Alexander II, around the year of the Lord 1074, the most bitter persecutor and enemy of such shameful presbyters, who at that time were polluting all of Germany with their incestuous concubinages under the name of marriage, and who threw everything into confusion and dissolution. Rudolf and Berthold were brothers, dukes of Swabia; afterwards Rudolf contended for the German kingdom against Henry IV, the most hostile enemy of the Roman Church. The text continues in the letter of Pope Urban.

units.la: A manifestè malo ministro datum, sine necessitate, sacrum, execrabile est homini sciéter illud accipienti.
units.tr: A sacred thing given by a manifestly wicked minister, without necessity, is detestable to the man who knowingly receives it.

units.la: § Porrò, Ad hæc, quæ tibi syllogisticè in eadem Epistola obiiciuntur: Si corpus & sanguis Christi non sunt, & alia, quæ prædiximus, suæ virtutis effectum non habeant, quid hoc agentibus obsunt? quod si habent, cur spernuntur, si ab indignis præsumuntur? Ad hęc (inquam) ita respondemus, Proprias quidem habent virtutes, & dignitates, vt præfatus Augustinus ait super Ioannem contra Donatistas: Sed agentibus vel suscipientibus hæc eadem Sacramenta, contra præfatorum Pontificum instituta, (nisi forte solâ morte interueniente, vtpote, ne sine Baptismate, vel Communione quilibet humanis rebus excedat) Eis (inquam) agentibus, vel suscipientibus intantum obsunt, ut vere Idololatræ sint: quum talibus & ordinationum, & Sacramentorum confectio, & aliter quàm permissum est, scienter susceptio, vehementer à sanctis Canonibus prohibeantur: Ait enim Samuel Propheta: Quasi peccatum ariolâdi est, Repugnare: & quasi scelus Idololatriæ, nolle acquiescere.
units.tr: § Further, as to the objections put to you in syllogistic form in the same Epistle: "If the body and blood of Christ are not, and the other things we have mentioned do not have the effect of their power, what harm does it do to those who perform them? But if they do have it, why are they despised when they are presumed upon by the unworthy?" To these (I say) we reply as follows. They indeed have their own powers and dignities, as the aforementioned Augustine says in his commentary on John against the Donatists. But for those who perform or receive these same sacraments contrary to the institutions of the aforementioned Pontiffs (unless perhaps death alone intervenes, as when someone is about to depart from human affairs without baptism or communion), these things do such harm to them, I say, when they perform or receive them, that they are truly idolaters, since for such men both the conferring of ordinations and sacraments, and the knowing reception of them otherwise than is permitted, are strongly forbidden by the holy canons. For the prophet Samuel says: "Rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as the wickedness of idolatry."

units.la: Ab Hæretico vel Schismatico Sacramenta conferri nulla unquam possunt: Baptismû Gratianus hic excipit.
units.tr: Sacraments can never be conferred by a heretic or a schismatic. Gratian excepts baptism here.

units.la: § Hæc de malis Catholicis, qui intra Ecclesiam sunt. Cæterum Schismaticorû, & Hæreticorum Sacramenta, quoniam extra Ecclesiam sunt, iuxta sanctorum Patrum traditiones (scilicet Pelagij, Gregorij, Cypriani, Augustini, & Hieronymi) Formam quidem Sacramentorum habent, non autem virtutis effectum habere profitemur: nisi quum ipsi, vel eorum Sacramentis initiati, per manus impositionem, ad Catholicam redierint unitatem.
units.tr: § These things are said of wicked Catholics who are within the Church. But the sacraments of schismatics and heretics, since they are outside the Church, according to the traditions of the holy Fathers (namely Pelagius, Gregory, Cyprian, Augustine, and Jerome), we profess that they indeed have the form of the sacraments, but do not have the effect of their power, unless they themselves, or those initiated by their sacraments, have returned to Catholic unity through the laying on of hands.

units.la: Gratianus. SCIENDVM vero, quòd Canones Apostolorum (quorum authoritate Orientalis, & ex parte, Romana vtitur Ecclesia) etiam insignis Cyprianus martyr, & 8o. Episcopi cum eodem, Baptisma Hæreticorum, lacrum Diaboli appellant: Stephanus, verò & Cornelius Martyres, & Pontifices Romani, & venerabilis Augustinus, in lib. De Baptismo, eundem Cyprianum, & prefatos Episcopos ob hanc causam vehementer redarguunt: Affirmantes, Baptisma, siue ab Hæretico, siue Schismatico, Ecclesiastico more celebratum, ratum esse Baptisma: Et merito: quia alia in Baptismo, & alia in reliquis Sacramentis consideratio est: quippe quum in ordine prior & necessarior sit: Subitò enim morituro, prius Baptismate, quàm Dominici corporis communione, vel aliis Sacramentis consulitur: & dum forte Catholicus non inueniatur, Sanctius est ab Hæretico Baptismi sacramentum sumere, quàm in æternum perire: Et hanc sententiam præscriptorum Pontificum Cornelij, Stephani, & Augustini, secuti sunt Siricius, Innocentius, Leo, Anastasius, & magnus Gregorius, & omnis catholica Ecclesia tenet. Prohibentur ergo de manibus talium Sacerdotum Sacramenta suscipi: non quin sint vera, quantùm ad formam & effectum: sed quia dum huiusmodi Sacerdotes se à populo contemptos viderint, rubore verecundiæ facilius ad pœnitentiam pronocentur. Item. Ex sexta Synodo. Sextus est Synodi Canon: cuius quidem sensum, non autem verba, reddidit antiquus interpres. Ita fine sic habet.
units.tr: Gratian. It must be known that the Canons of the Apostles, on whose authority the Eastern Church and in part the Roman Church relies, together with the famous martyr Cyprian and eighty bishops with him, call the baptism of heretics the bath of the devil. Yet the martyrs Stephen and Cornelius, the Roman pontiffs, and the venerable Augustine, in his book On Baptism, vehemently rebuke Cyprian and the aforementioned bishops for this reason, affirming that baptism celebrated in the church manner, whether by a heretic or a schismatic, is valid baptism. And rightly so, because there is one consideration for baptism and another for the other sacraments: since in order it is prior and more necessary. For one who is about to die suddenly is provided for by baptism before the communion of the Lord's body or the other sacraments; and when perhaps no Catholic can be found, it is holier to receive the sacrament of baptism from a heretic than to perish for ever. This opinion of the aforementioned pontiffs Cornelius, Stephen, and Augustine was followed by Siricius, Innocent, Leo, Anastasius, and the great Gregory, and the whole Catholic Church holds it. Therefore the sacraments are forbidden to be received from the hands of such priests, not because they are not true as to form and effect, but because when such priests see themselves despised by the people, they are more easily moved to repentance by the blush of shame. Likewise, from the Sixth Synod. The thirteenth canon of the Synod: the ancient translator rendered its sense, but not its words. It runs thus.

units.la: Ἐ ἰ δὲ βουλοιτο πης τὴν εἰς κληρον προεχομενον, γαμου νομω σωαπτεσθαι γυναικι, πεὸ τ᾽ ἡ τὸ ἐπισκοπου, ἡ ἀρχοντα, ἡ πρεσβυτερὸν χειροτονιας, ὅ ἐστι πεπληπω. Id sic traducitur.
units.tr: [Ἐὰν δὲ βούλοιτο τῶν εἰς κλῆρον προσερχομένων γάμου νόμῳ συναφθῆναι γυναικί, πρὸ τοῦ τὸν ἐπίσκοπον, ἢ ἄρχοντα, ἢ πρεσβύτερον χειροτονίας, ὅ ἐστι πεπληρῶσθαι.] This is translated thus:

units.la: Qui vxorem ducere volunt, ante Subdiaconi, vel Diaconi, vel Presbyteri ordinem, ducant.
units.tr: Those who wish to take wives should do so before the ordination of subdeacon, or deacon, or presbyter.

units.la: SI quis eorum, qui ad Clerum accedunt, voluerit nuptiali iure mulieri copulari, hoc ante ordinationem Subdiaconatus faciat. Item. Ex Concilio Carthaginensi 3. in cap. Concilij 19. Carthaginem Patres Aphricani convenerunt, Cæsario & Attico Cos. hoc est, Anno Christi 399. Siricio Papa. In Synodorum Charthaginensium Canonibus Græcè compilatis, hic est 16. Inter alia sic ibidem continetur.
units.tr: IF anyone of those who come to the clergy wishes to be joined to a woman by the right of marriage, let him do so before his ordination as subdeacon. Likewise, from the Third Council of Carthage, canon 19. The African Fathers assembled at Carthage in the consulship of Caesarius and Atticus, that is, in the year of Christ 399, under Pope Siricius. In the Carthaginian canons compiled in Greek, this is number 16. Among other things, the following is contained there.

units.la: Ἡ ἡ ρεσπ, ὥστε τὸν ἀναγνωσας εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τ᾽ ἡς ἐρημίας, ἀνακαλέσθαι, ἡ συμβίος ἀχαχέω, ἡ ἐπερώτειαν ὁμολογεῖν. Translator vetus hîc.
units.tr: [Ἡ ἡ ρεσπ, ὥστε τὸν ἀναγνώστην εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐρημίας, ἀνακαλέσασθαι, ἢ συμβίου ἀχωρίστου, ἢ ἐπαγγεῖλαι ὁμολογεῖν.] The old translator here.

units.la: cælibatum, sine perpetuo Continentiæ voto, non probat in suis Ecclesiis.
units.tr: He does not approve celibacy in his churches without a perpetual vow of continence.

units.la: LEctores, quum ad annos pubertatis veniunt, cogun- tur aut uxores ducere, aut continentiam profiteri.
units.tr: Lectors, when they reach the age of puberty, are compelled either to take wives or to profess continence.

units.la: Item. Gregorius, Bonifacio Episcopo Rhegio. Epist. 5. lib. 3.
units.tr: Likewise. Gregory, to Bonifacius, Bishop of Rhegium. Letter 5, book 3.

units.la: Subdiaconos observare Continentiam decet.
units.tr: Subdeacons ought to observe continence.

units.la: SVbdiaconis tuis hoc, quod de Siculis statuimus, de- cernimus observari: nec illam definitionem nostram cuiusquam contumaciâ sinas, aut temeritate corrumpi.
units.tr: Your subdeacons are to observe what we have decreed concerning the Sicilians. Let no one allow this our decision to be corrupted by another's obstinacy or rashness.

units.la: Item. Vrbanus secundus in Synodo apud Meldem. Sedebat hic Gregorij septimi successor anno Christi circiter 1084. per annos 11. quibus Concilia tria convocavit: Placentiam, primum. Alterum, Meldem. Tertium, In Claromontem. Duobus primis Ecclesiasticorum dissolutionem mirè coercuit. Ex quibus tres subsequentes Canones excerpsit post Iuonem, de conti. Cleric. Gratianus. Duo postrema Gallica fuerunt. In Claromonte decreta fuit illa celebris Hierosolymitana expeditio, dicto anno 1084. si qua fides in Platina. Numerant alij, anno 1095. Sed ad rem.
units.tr: Likewise. Urban II, in the synod at Meaux. This successor of Gregory VII held the see about the year of Christ 1084, for eleven years, during which he convened three councils: the first at Piacenza, the second at Meaux, the third at Clermont. In the first two he sharply checked the dissolute conduct of the clergy. From these councils Gratian, after Ivo, extracted the three following canons, on the continence of clerics. The last two were held in France. At Clermont was decreed that famous expedition to Jerusalem, in the year 1084, if one may trust Platina. Others count it as 1095. But to the matter.

units.la: Licet amicas Hieraticorum seruituti mancipare : Hieraticis ipsis a gradu suo depositis.
units.tr: It is permitted to hand over concubines to the service of the clergy, once the clerics themselves have been deposed from their rank.

units.la: EOs, qui post Diaconatum vxoribus vacare voluerint, ab omni sacro ordine remouemus: officioque, atque beneficio Ecclesiae carere decernimus: quòd si ab Episcopo commoniti non se correxerint, Principibus indulgemus licentiā, vt eorum fœminas mācipent seruituti. Si vero Episcopi consenserint eorum prauitatibus, ipsius officij interdictione multentur. Idem. Grandensi Patriarchæ Dominico.
units.tr: We remove from all holy orders those who wish to be devoted to their wives after becoming deacons. We decree that they are to be deprived of their office and of the benefice of the Church. But if, once admonished by the bishop, they do not mend their ways, we grant to the princes the licence to reduce their women to slavery. If, however, the bishops consent to their wickedness, they are to be punished with the prohibition of their office itself. The same, to Dominic, Patriarch of Grado.

units.la: Palàm incontinentium Clericorum poena, est καθαίρεσις.
units.tr: Clearly the penalty for incontinent clerics is deposition (kathairesis) [καθαίρεσις].

units.la: ERubescant impij, & aperte intelligant, iudicio sancti Spiritus eos, qui modò in sacris tribus gradibus (scilicet Presbyteratu, Diaconatu, Subdiaconatu) positi, mulierculas non abiecerint, & castè non vixerint, excludendos ab eorundem graduum dignitate. De manifestis quidem loquimur: Secretorum autem & cognitor Deus, & iudex est. Idem in Meldensi Synodo præsidens ait.
units.tr: Let the impious blush, and let them clearly understand that by the judgment of the Holy Spirit those who are now placed in the three sacred grades (namely the presbyterate, the diaconate and the subdiaconate) and who have not put away their little women, and have not lived chastely, are to be excluded from the dignity of those same grades. We speak of manifest cases; but God alone knows and judges secret ones. The same, presiding at the synod of Meaux, says.

units.la: Probatæ castitatis est, qui vel virgo est, vel unicâ fuit vxore virgine contentus.
units.tr: He is of proven chastity who is either a virgin or has been content with one wife, a virgin.

units.la: NEmo ad sacrum Ordinem permittatur accedere, nisi aut virgo, aut probatæ castitatis, & qui usque ad Subdiaconatum, unicam & virginem vxorem habuerit. Item. In Concilio Carthaginensi quinto, cap. 3. Canonum Græcè collectorum vigesimus quintus est.
units.tr: No one is to be admitted to holy orders unless he is either a virgin or of proven chastity, and has had, up to the subdiaconate, one wife who is a virgin. Likewise. In the fifth Council of Carthage, chapter 3; it is the twenty-fifth of the canons collected in Greek.

units.la: Hieratici mariti pro non maritis habeantur: & vxores habeant, tanquam non vxores.
units.tr: Married clerics are to be regarded as unmarried, and they are to have wives as though they had no wives.

units.la: PLacuit Episcopos, Presbyteros, Diaconos, Subdiaconos* secundum priora constituta, etiam abstinere ab vxoribus: quod nisi fecerint, ab Ecclesiastico remoueantur officio: ceteros verò Clericos ad hoc non togi:sed secundum vniuscuiusque Ecclesiæ consuetudinem obseruari debere. Est, quod circa finem Canonis immoremur diutiuscule: quia Græcè legitur aliud, quàm vetus interpres traduxerit.
units.tr: It has pleased the bishops, presbyters, deacons and subdeacons, in accordance with earlier decrees, to abstain also from their wives; and if they do not do so, they are to be removed from ecclesiastical office. But the other clerics are not to be compelled to this, and should observe it according to the custom of each church. It is worth lingering a little over the end of this canon, because the Greek reads differently from what the old translator rendered.

units.la: Τοὺς δὲ λοιπους κληρικους πρὸς ϲῶφρο μὴ ἀναγκάζεσθαι· εἰ μὴ ἐν πρεσβυτικὴ κείρα.
units.tr: The other clergy are not to be compelled to chastity [Τοὺς δὲ λοιπους κληρικους πρὸς ϲῶφρο μὴ ἀναγκάζεσθαι], unless they are in the presbyterial age [εἰ μὴ ἐν πρεσβυτικὴ κείρα].

units.la: Hic verbum nullum de consuetudine aliarum Ecclesiarum: sed melior & aptior longè sensus inest, puta: Reliquos autem clericos ad hoc non compelli(scilicet, vt uxoribus suis legitimis deinceps abstineant) nisi in grandiore & proueCtiore sint ætate. Sanctam & Euangelicam legem ἐ quæ victos senes à concessa etiam venere abstincre mandat. Præstat & Zonaræ ἰρμνεύων subdere, locum sic explicantis. ______ ἐι μὴ ὁ πρεσβυτικὴ κείρα. εἰ μὴ πάντως ἴσος πρεσβυνκοπτε ὁ ἡλικία. κείρα γάρ, ἡ ἡλικία ἔστι. Id est. Nisi in provectâ ætate, Nisi valde processerint in ætatem: κεῖρα enim ἡλικία est (hoc est ætas). Nisi valde sint senes, Nam qui devenerunt ad extremam senectutem, continentiæ studere oportet. Magis verò, secundum magnum Basilium, quum pro continentia non sit habenda Senum continentia. Dicit autem ille. ______ In senectute continentia, non continentia, sed impotentia debilitas & impotentia. Qui nempe in senectute non continet, hic nimis incontinens est. Hæc de Zonara. Ergo, Iuliæ, Papiæque Leges, in quinquagenariis, & sexagenariis nuptias vetantes, à Christianis obseruande forent. Ad reliqua ______ Item. Leo nonus, contra Epistolam Nicetæ Abbatis. Est in eo Pannomiæ titulo iam dicto.
units.tr: Here there is not a word about the custom of other churches; rather a much better and more apt sense lies within it, namely: the remaining clerics are not to be compelled to this (that is, to abstain from their lawful wives from then on) unless they are of greater and more advanced age. The holy and evangelical law, which bids old men who have been overcome to abstain even from what is permitted, is in harmony with this. It is also worth adding Zonaras' interpretation, explaining the passage thus: unless they are of advanced age, unless they have entirely reached the age of elders; for keira [κεῖρα] is age (hēlikia). That is, unless in advanced age, unless they have truly grown old; for keira means age (that is, time of life). Unless they are truly old, for those who have come to extreme old age ought to pursue continence. Moreover, according to the great Basil, the continence of the aged is not to be counted as continence at all. For he says: in old age, not continence but weakness and impotence. Whoever does not restrain himself in old age is indeed excessively incontinent. So far Zonaras. Therefore the laws of Julia and Papia, which forbid marriages for men of fifty and sixty, ought to have been observed by Christians. As for the rest. Likewise, Leo IX, against the letter of Nicetas the abbot. It is in that title of Pannonia already mentioned.

units.la: Nec ordo minor, Coniugio. Nec vnicæ virginis coniugium, obstat ordini: Monachismus obstat.
units.tr: Nor does a lower order obstruct marriage, nor does marriage to a single virgin obstruct the order; monasticism obstructs it.

units.la: SERIATIM & aperte prosequamur, quod sancta Romana Ecclesia de gradibus Clericorum, ait: Clericos, Ostiarios, Lectores, Exorcistas, Acolitos, si extra votum & habitum Monachi inueniantur, & continentiam profiteri noluerint: vxorem ducere virginem cum benedictione Sacerdotali permittunt, non autem Viduam, aut Repudiatam: quia propter hoc deinceps nec ad Subdiaconatum prouehi poterunt: quia nec Laicus, nisi virginem sortitus vxorem, aut digamus, ad Clericatum potest ascendere.
units.tr: Let us follow in order and openly what the holy Roman Church says about the grades of clerics: if clerics, doorkeepers, readers, exorcists and acolytes are found outside the vow and habit of a monk, and are unwilling to profess continence, they are permitted to take a virgin as wife with the priestly blessing, but not a widow or a divorced woman; because on account of this they will not afterwards be able to be advanced to the subdiaconate, since not even a layman may ascend to the clergy unless he has obtained a virgin as wife, or has been married only twice.

units.la: Mutua perpetuáque debet esse coniugum ad continentiam conuersio.
units.tr: The conversion of spouses to continence ought to be mutual and lasting.

units.la: § Etsi quis ex praefatis ordinibus desiderat ad Subdiaconatum ascendere, nō potest sine consensu uxoris suae: ut fiat de Carnali deinceps Spirituale coniugium, nemine cogente eos. Neque permittitur postea uxor iungi eidem marito suo carnaliter: nec cuiquam nubere in vita, aut post mortem illius.
units.tr: § If anyone of the aforesaid orders desires to ascend to the subdiaconate, he cannot do so without the consent of his wife, so that from carnal marriage there may thereafter come a spiritual marriage, no one compelling them. Nor is the wife afterwards permitted to be joined carnally to the same husband, nor to marry anyone during his life or after his death.

units.la: Item. Ex Concilio Calchedonensi. cap.14.
units.tr: Likewise. From the Council of Chalcedon, canon 14.

units.la: Calchedon ad Bosphorum Thracium, septem solum stadiis a Constantinopoli distans est. Eò convenerunt 630. sancti patres ad Concilium: cui praefuit per suos vicarios Leo Papa I. circiter an. Do. 455.
units.tr: Chalcedon, on the Thracian Bosphorus, is only seven stadia distant from Constantinople. There 630 holy fathers came together for the council, over which Pope Leo I presided through his vicars, about the year of the Lord 455.

units.la: Fideli vetitum cum Infideli iugum ducere.
units.tr: It is forbidden for a believer to take up a yoke with an unbeliever.

units.la: QUoniam in quibusdam prouinciis concessum est Lectoribus, & Psalmistis uxores ducere, constituit sancta Synodus, cuiquam ex his non licere accipere † sectae alterius uxorem. Item. In Nicaeno Concil. cap.3.
units.tr: Since in certain provinces readers and psalmists have been permitted to take wives, the holy Synod has decreed that none of them may take the wife of another sect. Likewise. In the Council of Nicaea, chapter 3.

units.la: Clericorum, & Mulierum (nisi quarundam) cohabitatio prohibetur.
units.tr: The cohabitation of clerics with women (except certain ones) is forbidden.

units.la: INterdixit † per omnia, sancta Synodus, non Episcopo, non Presbytero, non Diacono, non alicui omnino qui in Clero est, licere † Subintroductam habere mulierem: Nisi forte aut matrem, aut soropem, aut amitam, aut eas tantùm personas, quae fugiant omne suspicionem. Item. Hieronymus ad Nepotianum, De vita Clericorum. Et variis aliis in locis, ex quibus consarcinatus est Canon praesens. ex Palaeis est.
units.tr: The holy Synod has entirely forbidden that a bishop, a presbyter, a deacon, or anyone at all in the clergy should have a woman living with him as a housekeeper, except perhaps a mother, a sister, an aunt, or only those persons who avoid all suspicion. Likewise. Jerome, to Nepotianus, On the life of clerics. And from various other passages, out of which this present canon has been patched together; it is taken from the Palea.

units.la: HOspitiolum tuum, aut raro, aut nunquam mulierum pedes terant: quia non potest toto corde cum Deo habitare, qui foeminarum accessibus copulatur. Foemina conscientiam secum pariter habitantis exurit. Nunquam mulierum formis disputes. Fœminæ nomen tuum nesciant. Fœminam, quam bene videris conuersantem, mente dilige, non corporali frequentiâ. Si bonum est mulierem non tangere, malum est ergo tangere.
units.tr: Let your little house be trodden by women's feet rarely, or never; for he who is joined with the approaches of women cannot dwell with God with his whole heart. A woman burns the conscience of the one who lives with her. Never argue about women's looks. Let women not know your name. Love in your mind a woman whom you see behaving well, not with bodily frequency. If it is good not to touch a woman, then it is bad to touch her.

units.la: Item, Gregorius in Dialogorum, lib. 4. cap. 11.
units.tr: Likewise, Gregory, in the Dialogues, book 4, chapter 11.

units.la: Presbyter uxorem suam, quasi sororem, diligat: huius consuetudinem, velut hostem, fugiat.
units.tr: A presbyter should love his wife as a sister: let him flee her company as he would an enemy.

units.la: PResbyter quidam sibi commissam regebat Ecclesiam, cum magno timore Domini, qui ex tempore acceptiordinis Presbyteram suam, ut sororem diligens, sed quasi hostem cauens, ad se propius accedere non sinebat: eámque sibi appropinquare, nullâ occasione permittebat: ab ea sibi communionem funditus familiaritatis abscidit.
units.tr: A certain presbyter ruled the church committed to him with great fear of the Lord. From the time he received the order, he loved his presbyter's wife as a sister, but guarded against her as an enemy; he did not allow her to come closer to him, nor did he permit her to approach him on any occasion; he cut off from her entirely all communion of intimacy.

units.la: Gratianus. PRESBYTERAM vero quam debeamus accipere, Laodicense Concilium ostendit. Laodicæa, Syriæ civitas, in quam statim post apostatæ Iuliani mortem sub annum Do. 367. quietis & pacatis omnibus in Ecclesia, quam turbarat ille sævissimè, tres & triginta Patres è Phrygia convenerunt, ubi quinquaginta novem Canones statuerunt. Hic 11. est.
units.tr: Gratian. What presbyter-woman we ought to receive the Council of Laodicea shows. Laodicea, a city of Syria, in which, immediately after the death of the apostate Julian, about the year of the Lord 367, when all was quiet and peaceful in the Church, which he had most savagely troubled, thirty-three fathers gathered from Phrygia and enacted fifty-nine canons. This is the eleventh.

units.la: Nullæ mulieres in Ecclesia præesse debent.
units.tr: No women ought to preside in the Church.

units.la: MVlieres, quæ apud Græcos, Presbyteræ appellantur (apud nos autem Viduæ, aut Seniores, Vniuiræ, & Matricuriæ appellantur) in Ecclesia tanquam ordinatas constitui non debere decernimus. Bis versi fuerút Latinè Canones Laodicenses. Hæc secunda versio est, quam sequitur Gratianus, neque propositæ quæstioni conueniens, neque litera Græcæ. In qua est.
units.tr: Women who among the Greeks are called presbyteresses (but among us are called widows, or seniors, or univiræ, and matricuriæ) we decree are not to be appointed in the Church as ordained persons. The Laodicean canons have been translated into Latin twice. This second version is the one Gratian follows, which suits neither the question proposed nor the Greek letter. In the Greek it reads: The Greek original is quoted in the next unit.

units.la: Περὶ τῶν, μὴ δεῖν τὰς λεγομένας πρεσβύτιδας, ἢ τοὺς πεσκαδημίας, ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ κατίστασθαι.
units.tr: Concerning those who are called presbytides, or those who preside, it is not fitting that they be set up in the church [Περὶ τῶν, μὴ δεῖν τὰς λεγομένας πρεσβύτιδας, ἢ τοὺς πεσκαδημίας, ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ κατίστασθαι].

units.la: Id est. De hoc, Non oportere vocatas Presbytidas, sive Præsidentes, in Ecclesia præfici.
units.tr: That is: Concerning this, that those called presbytides, or presidents, ought not to be placed in charge in the Church.

units.la: DIS-
units.tr: DIS-

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXXIII.
units.tr: DISTINCTIO XXXIII.

units.la: Pergit adhuc Gratianus in duobus sequentibus Diorismis de Clericorum continentia disputare, nonnulla tamen praeter opus interserens: quod istiusmodi Rhapsodis est peculiare.
units.tr: Gratian still continues to dispute, in the two following Dicta, about the continence of the clergy, though he also inserts some matters outside his subject. This is peculiar to such patchwork compilers.

units.la: Gratianus. ECCE. Quod in Sacris Ordinibus constituti, vxores habere non possunt: vel si Digami aliqui fuerint inuenti, ad Sacros Ordines ascedere non valent. Sed quaeritur, Si quis, praeter vxorem suam, Cocubinam habuerit, vtrum in Sacerdotem promoueri valeat? Tales a Sacris Ordinibus, authoritate Canonum Apostolorum, prohibentur. In quibus sic statutum legitur capire decimo septimo.
units.tr: Gratian. Here. Those who are constituted in holy orders cannot have wives, or, if any are found to have been twice married, they cannot be promoted to holy orders. But the question is raised: if someone, besides his wife, has a concubine, can he be promoted to the priesthood? Such men are excluded from holy orders by the authority of the Canons of the Apostles, in which the following is read as decreed in the seventeenth chapter.

units.la: Bis maritus, vel non maritali concubitu pollutus, ad Ecclesiæ ministerium capi nō debet.
units.tr: A man who has been married twice, or who has been defiled by a non-marital concubinage, must not be received into the ministry of the Church.

units.la: SI quis, post acceptum sacrum Baptisma, secundis fuerit nuptiis copulatus, aut Concubinam habuerit, non poterit fieri Episcopus, nec Sacerdos, nec Diaconus, † aut prorsus ex numero eorum, qui in ministerio Sacro deserviunt. Gratianus. DESERVIENTES Sacro ministerio intelligitur Subdiaconi, qui calicem Diacono offerunt: & Acolyti, qui cum cereis Diaconos praecedunt: unde Ceroferarij dicuntur: qui etiam vinū & aquā praeparando Calici subministrant. Concubina intelligenda est praeter vxorem, Vt iste sit sensus capituli: Siquis post acceptum Sacrū Baptisma, secundis fuerit nuptiis copulatus: aut concubinam habuerit (hīc distinguendū est) antequam vxorē duxerit: siue post mortem vxoris. Unde beatus Gregorius ait. Tertulliani primum nomine circumferebatur liber, De definitionibus orthodoxae fidei, siue De Ecclesiasticis dogmatibus: quem postea tribuerunt Augustino: est in Tomo 3. operum eiusdem. Neutrum esse credidu Gratianus, sed Gregory, cuius titulo citatur, vt hic vides. sp. est 72. complectens impedimenta multa Clericatus.
units.tr: If anyone, after receiving holy baptism, has been joined in second marriage, or has had a concubine, he cannot be made a bishop, nor a priest, nor a deacon, † or in short be of the number of those who serve in the sacred ministry. Gratian. SERVING. By those serving in the sacred ministry are understood the subdeacons, who offer the chalice to the deacon, and the acolytes, who go before the deacons with candles, whence they are called candle-bearers; they also serve in preparing the wine and water for the chalice. A concubine is to be understood as apart from a wife, so that this is the sense of the chapter: if anyone, after receiving holy baptism, has been joined in second marriage, or has had a concubine (here a distinction must be made) before he has taken a wife, or after the wife's death. Hence the blessed Gregory says: the book On the Definitions of the Orthodox Faith, or On Ecclesiastical Dogmas, was first circulated under the name of Tertullian; afterwards they attributed it to Augustine, and it is in the third volume of his works. Gratian believed it was neither, but Gregory, under whose title it is cited, as you see here. It is the 72nd, containing many impediments to the clerical state.

units.la: Qui non fuerit vnius tantum mulieris virginis, & honestae coniugio contentus, non poterit esse Clericus.
units.tr: A man who has not been content with one woman only, a virgin, and with honourable marriage, cannot be a cleric.

units.la: MAritum duarum, post Baptismum, matronarum, Clericum non ordinandum censemus: Nec eum, qui vnā quidem, sed Concubinā, non Matronam habuit: Nec illum qui Viduam, aut Repudiatam, vel Meretricem in matrimonio sumpsit: Neque eum, qui semetipsum, quolibet corporis sui membro, indignatione aliquā, vel iusto, iniustove timore superatus truncauerit: neque illos, qui vsuras accepisse conuincitur: aut in scena lusisse noscuntur: nec eum, qui publicâ pœnitentiâ mortalia crimina desleuit: neque illum, qui in furiam aliquando versus insaniuit, vel afflictione diabolicâ vexatus est: neque eum, qui per ambitionem, ad imitationem Simonis Magi, pecuniam obtulerit.
units.tr: We judge that a man married to two wives after baptism is not to be ordained a cleric; nor one who has had a single wife who was a concubine and not a matron; nor one who has taken to marriage a widow, a divorced woman, or a prostitute; nor one who has mutilated himself in any part of his body, overcome by some indignation, or by a just or unjust fear; nor those who are convicted of having taken usury, or are known to have acted in the theatre; nor one who has atoned by public penance for mortal sins; nor one who at some time has turned to madness and gone insane, or been troubled by diabolical affliction; nor one who has offered money out of ambition, in imitation of Simon Magus.

units.la: Item. Pius Papa. Gratianus Canonem præsentem Pio Papæ tribuit, Si vera est inscriptio suit hic Pius 1. Antonino Pio regnante, circiter annos Do. 154. Nā duos alios Pios annis fere trecentis Gratianus antecessit.
units.tr: Likewise. Pope Pius. Gratian ascribes the present canon to Pope Pius. If the inscription is true, this is Pius I, in the reign of Antoninus Pius, about the year of the Lord 154. For Gratian places him some three hundred years before the other two Pii.

units.la: Arrepticii, vel Epileptici sanctis altaribus non ministrent.
units.tr: Epileptics and those seized by spirits must not minister at the holy altars.

units.la: COmmuniter diffinimus, Vt nullus de iis, qui aut in terra arrepti à dæmonibus eliduntur, aut quolibet modo vexationis incursibus efferuntur, vel Sacris audeant ministrare altaribus, vel in discussè se ingerant Sacramentis diuinis. Exceptis illis, qui corporum incommoditati dediti, sine huiusmodi passionibus in terra probantur elisi: qui tamen & ipsi tandiu erunt ab officiū sui ordine, & loco suspensi, quousque vnius anni spatio, per discretionem Episcopi, inueniantur ab incursu dæmonum liberati. Item Nicolaus Papa. De Nicolai tempore diximus in antecedenti dist. & in 28.
units.tr: We have commonly decreed that none of those who are either seized on the ground by demons and thrown down, or carried off by some attack of affliction in any manner, shall dare to minister at the holy altars or to thrust themselves rashly into the divine sacraments. Excepted are those who, given over to bodily infirmities, are proved to have fallen to the ground without such passions; yet these also shall be suspended from the office of their order and place until, within the space of one year, by the judgement of the bishop, they are found to be freed from the attack of demons. Likewise Pope Nicholas. We have spoken of Nicholas's time in the preceding distinction and in the 28th.

units.la: CLerici, qui in adolescentia à dæmonibus cognoscuntur obsessi, ad superiorem Sacri regiminis gradum ascendere non possunt. Item. Gelasius Papa primus, cap. 21. Epistolæ ad vniuersos Episcopos per Lucaniam, & Brutios, & Siciliam. Gelasius fuit Aphcr, sedebat Romæ, Gotho rege Theodorico occupante Italiam, tempore Zenonis Imperatoris, Anno Do. 496. quo scripta fuit Epistola hic citata, quod ex Consulibus adscriptis in ea colligitur.
units.tr: Clerics who are known to have been possessed by demons in youth cannot ascend to the higher rank of holy ministry. Likewise. Pope Gelasius I, chapter 21, Letter to all the bishops throughout Lucania, Bruttium and Sicily. Gelasius was an African, and he resided at Rome, while Theodoric the Goth occupied Italy, in the time of the emperor Zeno, in the year of the Lord 496, when the letter cited here was written, as is gathered from the consuls named in it.

units.la: VSqueadeo sanè comperimus illicita quæque prorumpere, vt à Dæmoniacis, similibúsque passionibus irretitos, ministeria sacrosancta tractare tribuatur: quibus si in hoc opere positis aliquid propriae necessitatis occurrat, quis de sua, fideliumque salute confidit, vbi ministros ipsos curationis humanae tanta perspexerit calamitate vexari? atque ideo necessario remouendi sunt, ne quibuslibet, pro quibus Christus mortuus est, scandalum generetur infirmis. Postremo, Si corpore sauciatum fortasis, aut debilem, nequaquam sancta contingere, Lex diuina permisit: quanto magis doni coelestis dispensatores esse non conuenit (quod est deterius) mente percussos? Item. Innocentius Papa Primus, Felici Episcopo Nuceriano. Epistola 4. cap.4.
units.tr: We have indeed found such unlawful things breaking out so widely that men entangled by demonic and similar afflictions are allowed to handle the holy ministries. If, while they are in this work, some need of their own should arise, who can trust in his own salvation and that of the faithful when he sees the ministers of human healing themselves so troubled by such calamity? Therefore they must necessarily be removed, lest a stumbling block be created for the weak, for whom Christ died. Finally, if divine law has not permitted one who is wounded or crippled in body to touch holy things at all, how much less is it fitting (which is worse) that those struck in mind should be dispensers of heavenly gifts? Likewise. Pope Innocent I, to Felix, bishop of Nuceria, Letter 4, chapter 4.

units.la: Gratianus ad thema reuertitur. Innocentius hic Ioannis Chrysostomi propugnator maximus, aduersus Eudoxiam Imperatoris Arcadij coniugem inglorioisissimam, Christi an. 410.
units.tr: Gratian returns to his theme. This Innocent, the great champion of John Chrysostom against Eudoxia, the most inglorious wife of the emperor Arcadius, lived in the year of Christ 410.

units.la: Qui Laici coniuges ad clericatum possunt assumi.
units.tr: Which laymen who have wives may be taken up into the clergy.

units.la: LAici, qui habentes vxores baptizati sunt, ac sic se instituerunt, vt in nullo, eorum opinio vacillet, aut Clericis iuncti sunt, aut monasteriis, ex quo Baptizati sunt, adhaeserunt: si non Concubinam, si non Pellicem nouerint, si in bonis operibus vigilauerint: non prohibentur huiusmodi ad Clericatus sortem assumi. Gratianus. CAETERVM, ante susceptum sacrum Ordinem, quosdam legimus concubinam habuisse, quos tamen sacri Canones non reiiciunt, si post sacrum Ordinem ab eius commixtione sese immaculatos custodiunt. Vnde Gregorius, Andreae Tarentino Episcopo, Epist.44.lib.2.siue cap.83.
units.tr: Laymen who were baptized while having wives, and who so conduct themselves that in no respect does their reputation waver, or who have attached themselves to clerics or to monasteries from the time of their baptism, are not forbidden to be admitted to the clerical state, provided they have known no concubine or mistress and have kept watch over themselves in good works. Gratian. Moreover, we read that some men had a concubine before taking up holy orders, and yet the sacred canons do not reject them if after receiving holy orders they keep themselves unstained by such intercourse. Hence Gregory to Andrew, Bishop of Tarentum, Epist. 44, lib. 2, or chap. 83.

units.la: Post ordinem susceptum, Concubinatus reus Episcopus non debet in ordine manere.
units.tr: A bishop accused of concubinage after receiving orders ought not to remain in his office.

units.la: HAbuisse te concubinam manifestâ veritate comperimus, & te illius criminis participationem habere: de qua etiam contraria est quibusdam innata suspicio. Sed quia in ambiguis rebus absolutum nō debet esse iudicium: I hoc tua conscientia committendum eligimus: qua de re, si in sacro Ordine constitutum, eius te recolis permixtione maculatum, Sacerdotij honore deposito, ad ministrandum nullo modo præsumas accedere, sciturus in anima tuę periculo te ministrare: & Deo nostro te sine dubio reddere rationem, si huius sceleris conscius in eo, quo es, Ordine, celans veritatem, permanere volueris.
units.tr: We have learned by clear evidence that you have had a concubine, and that you share in that offence; and there is also a suspicion, arising among some people, to the same effect. But since judgement ought not to be final in doubtful matters, we have chosen to commit this to your own conscience. Therefore, if you recall that you were defiled by that intercourse while you were established in holy orders, lay down the honour of the priesthood and do not presume in any way to approach ministry, knowing that you minister at peril to your soul, and that without doubt you will render an account to our God if, aware of this crime, you choose to remain in the order you hold while concealing the truth.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXXIIII.
units.tr: DISTINCTION XXXIV.

units.la: Unde Nicolaus Papa ad Adaluuinum Archiepiscopum, De Nicolao dimus 32. dist. & 27. Pars prior Canonis Themati non congruit. Venator Episcopus, aut fœminis, etiam sibi sanguine proximis, nimium familiaris, nisi monitus desistat, officio, gradúque suo remouetur.
units.tr: Hence Pope Nicholas to Archbishop Adalwin, as we have said under Nicholas, dist. 32, and 27. The first part of the canon does not fit the theme. A bishop who is a hunter, or who is too familiar with women, even those closely related to him by blood, is removed from his office and rank unless he desists when warned.

units.la: QVorundam relatione fidelium nostris auribus intimatum est, quòd Lanfredus Episcopus (qui & Iuuenis dicitur) venationi sit deditus, quod vitium plurimos etiam de Clericali catalogo, genere duntaxat Germanos & Gallos, irreuerentes implicat. Verùm iste (si ita est, ut audiuimus) merito Iuuenis dicitur: quia Iuuenilibus desideriis occupatus, nullâ grauitate constringitur: nam (ut beatus dicit Hieronymus) Venatorem nunquam legimus sanctum. Nihilominus autem de hoc Episcopo relatum est Apostolatui nostro, quòd cum quadam filia sua immoderatam teneat familiaritatem: & ob id mala fama ei orta sit. Pro qua re à sanctitate tua, cæterisque Coëpiscopis suis admonitus atque correptus est, sed nullatenus emendatus: quæ res in hoc maximè displicet, & magis ac magis deteriorem de se reddit opinionem: in quo. quo beatitudini tuæ, & cæterorum Coëpiscoporum suorum rationibus non obedit, & per inobedientiam in culpam protoplasti relabitur. Oportet ergo fraternitatem tuam Synodale cum Episcopis, & Suffraganeis tuis convocare Concilium: & hunc salutaribus eloquiis Episcopum convenire, atque illi pastorali authoritate præcipere, quatenus ab omnium bestiarum, vel volucrum venatione penitus alienus existat: atque ab immoderata filiæ suæ familiaritate semet omnino coerceat. Quòd si parere contempserit, & tam pro venationis delectatione, quàm pro immoderata filiæ suæ conversatione vitanda, vobis admonentibus obedire distulerit, à vestro collegio excommunicatus abscedat. Quòd si in hoc contumax adhuc apparuerit, à ministerio cessare debebit. Ex Concilio Aurelian. 4.
units.tr: It has been reported to our ears by the trustworthy accounts of certain people that Bishop Lanfred (who is also called "the Young") is given over to hunting, a vice which entangles many men of the clerical order, chiefly the Germans and the French, in disgrace. But this man (if it is as we have heard) is rightly called "Young," because, occupied with youthful desires, he is held back by no seriousness. For (as the blessed Jerome says) we never read that a hunter was holy. Moreover, it has been reported to our Apostolate about this bishop that he keeps an immoderate familiarity with a certain daughter of his, and that for this reason a bad reputation has arisen concerning him. For this matter he was admonished and rebuked by your Holiness and by his other fellow bishops, but he was not in any way amended. This thing displeases most of all, and makes him ever more and more evil in opinion, in that he does not obey the reasons of your Blessedness and of his other fellow bishops, and through disobedience he falls back into the sin of the first-formed man. It is therefore necessary that your brotherhood convene a synod with the bishops and your suffragans, and that they meet this bishop with wholesome words and command him with pastoral authority that he abstain entirely from the hunting of all beasts and birds, and that he wholly restrain himself from immoderate familiarity with his daughter. But if he scorns to obey, and delays obeying your admonitions, both to avoid the pleasure of hunting and to avoid the immoderate company of his daughter, let him depart from your college excommunicated. And if he still appears stubborn in this, he must cease from the ministry. From the Council of Orléans, the fourth.

units.la: Aurelianensia quinque habemus antiqua Concilia: quorum posterius, circiter annum Christi 550. Childeberto Rege, convenit. In nullo nos legimus, quod hic Gratianus (post Iuonem tamen, cap.
units.tr: We have five ancient Councils of Orléans. The later of them, about the year of Christ 550, under King Childebert, met. We do not read anywhere that this (which Gratian, after Ivo, nevertheless, ch.

units.la: 1. De vita Cleric. lib.3.) inde scribit desumptum. Sed hoc in Agathensi Concilio fuit à Gallicis patribus statutum, cap. Concilij 55. cuius capitis verba hic referuntur. Alaricus Rex Gothicus tunc occupabat Galliam Narbonensem, circiter annos Do. 440. Ibi Agatha civitas. Nunc, Ada.
units.tr: 1, On the Life of Clerics, book 3) writes was taken from there. But this was decreed by the Gallic fathers at the Council of Agde, canon 55, whose words are quoted here. Alaric, king of the Goths, then held Narbonese Gaul, about the year of the Lord 440. There is the city of Agde. Now, Ada.

units.la: Hieraticis Hieraces, & omnis omnino venatus, interdicuntur.
units.tr: For clerics, hawks [ἱέραξ], and every kind of hunting at all, are forbidden.

units.la: Episcopum, Presbyterum, aut Diaconum, canes ad venandum, aut accipitres, aut huiusmodi res habere non licet. Quòd si quis talium personarum in hac voluptate sæpius detectus fuerit, si Episcopus est, tribus mensibus à communione suspendatur: si Presbyter, duobus mensibus abstineat. Diaconus verò ab omni officio, & communione suspendatur. Item. Qui sequitur Canon, fuit editus in Synodo quadam Francica, dum filij Principis Martelli Carlomanus & Pipinus breuis, Austrasiæ, Franciæque suæ in illis partibus imperabant. Apostolicâ Papæ Zachariæ iussione tum convenerunt Episcopi Francorum, Sancto Bonifacio præside. Incarnationis Do. anno 742. Sed hæc duo sunt & πάρεργα, & παλαια.
units.tr: It is not lawful for a bishop, a presbyter, or a deacon to keep hounds for hunting, or hawks, or things of that sort. If any such person is caught often in this pleasure, if he is a bishop let him be suspended from communion for three months; if a presbyter, let him abstain for two months. But a deacon is to be suspended from all office and from communion. Likewise. The following canon was issued in a certain Frankish synod, when the sons of the prince Charles Martel, Carloman and Pippin the Short, were ruling in those parts over Austrasia and their Frankish realm. By the command of Pope Zachary the bishops of the Franks then met, with Saint Boniface presiding. In the year of the Lord's incarnation 742. But these two are both side matters [πάρεργα] and old things [παλαια].

units.la: OMnibus servis Domini, Venationes, & Syluaticas vagationes cum canibus, & ut Accipitres aut Falcones habeant, interdicimus. CONCVBINA autem hic intelligitur, quae, cessantibus legalibus instrumentis, vnita est, & comunali affectu asciscitur. Hanc, Coniugem facit affectus, Concubinam vero Lex nominat. De hac dicitur in Concilio Toletano primo. Tum Syricius Ecclesiam procurabat. Canonis verba sic habent.
units.tr: We forbid all servants of the Lord to hunt, to wander in the woods with dogs, and to keep hawks or falcons. Here, however, a concubine is understood to be a woman who is joined to a man, without legal instruments, and is taken into a shared affection. Affection makes her a wife; the law names her a concubine. This is spoken of in the First Council of Toledo. At that time Siricius was governing the Church. The words of the canon read thus.

units.la: Concubina vicem legitimae tenet vxoris.
units.tr: A concubine holds the place of a lawful wife.

units.la: SI quis habens vxorem Fidelis, habeat & Concubinam, Non communicet. Caeterum, Is, qui non habet Vxorem, & pro Vxore Concubinam habet: a communione non repellatur: tamen vt vnius mulieris, aut Vxoris, aut Concubinae sit coniunctione contentus. Item. Isidorus De distantia noui & veteris testamenti. Sic leges in Pannemia libro 6. Tit. De Concubi.
units.tr: If a faithful man who has a wife also has a concubine, let him not be admitted to communion. But he who has no wife, and keeps a concubine in place of a wife, is not to be repelled from communion, provided that he is content with the union of one woman only, either a wife or a concubine. Likewise. Isidore, On the Difference between the New and Old Testament. Thus the laws in the Pannemia, book 6, title On Concubines.

units.la: CHristiano, non dicam plurimas, sed nec duas simul habere licitum est: Nisi vnam tantum, aut Vxorem, aut certe loco Vxoris (si coniunx deest) Concubinam.
units.tr: For a Christian it is lawful to have not, I will not say many, but not even two at the same time: only one, either a wife, or, certainly, in place of a wife (if a spouse is lacking), a concubine.

units.la: Certe hic videntur permittere Concubinatum. Producitur Augustinus in contrarium. Ex dictis Augustini. Legitur ista in Pannemia titulo nunc adductio. Qui verò praesentem Canonem transcripserunt ex Augustino, fideliter hoc non egerunt, immutatis & omissis multis. Ab authoris tamen sensu non recesserunt. Integrum videas Homilia 49. in lib.50. Homiliarum. To.10. Digna certe scitu Palaea. Quid esset nalaia nos ostendebamus in Analectis, explicantes cap.23. de verb. sign. in antiq.
units.tr: Here they certainly seem to permit concubinage. Augustine is brought forward on the other side. From the sayings of Augustine. That passage is read in the Pannemia under the title now cited. But those who copied out the present canon from Augustine did not do so faithfully, since many things were changed and omitted. Yet they did not depart from the author's meaning. You may see the whole in Homily 49 in book 50 of the Homilies, volume 10. Certainly the old texts [παλαια] are worth knowing. We showed what the palaea was in the Analecta, explaining chapter 23 on the meaning of words, in the ancient writers.

units.la: Nulli Christiano fas est, aliy, quam quae propria sit vxor, commisceri mulieri.
units.tr: It is not right for any Christian to have intercourse with a woman other than his own wife.

units.la: AVdite fratres charissimi, membra Christi, & matris Catholicae Ecclesiae filij. Quod dico Competentibus, audiat Fideles: quod dico Fidelibus, audiat Competentes: quod dico Fidelibus & Competentibus & Poenitentibus, audiant & Catechumeni: audiant omnes, & timeat, & nemo contenat: sic sit mihi in consolatione vester auditus, ne vobis sit in testimonium dolor meus. Competentibus dico, Fornicari vobis non licet : sufficiant vobis Vxores: audiat Deus, si vos surdi estis: audiant Angeli, si vos contemnitis. Concubinas habere non licet vobis. & si non habetis vxores, tamen non licet vobis habere concubinas, quas postea dimittatis, & ducatis vxores. Tanto magis damnatio erit vobis, si voluerit is habere Vxores & Concubinas.
units.tr: Hear me, dearest brothers, members of Christ and sons of the Catholic mother Church. What I say to the candidates, let the faithful hear; what I say to the faithful, let the candidates hear; what I say to the faithful and the candidates and the penitents, let the catechumens hear too. Let all hear, and let them fear, and let no one resist. May your hearing be my consolation, so that my grief may not be a witness against you. To the candidates I say: it is not lawful for you to commit fornication; let wives be enough for you. Let God hear, if you are deaf; let the angels hear, if you despise me. It is not lawful for you to keep concubines. And if you do not have wives, still it is not lawful for you to keep concubines, whom you would afterwards dismiss in order to take wives. All the more will the condemnation be yours, if he chooses to have both wives and concubines.

units.la: Gratianus big argumentatur, Concubinatum solum non ossicere promotioni ad Diaconatum: rigore enim Legis mollit dispensatione, si dicens.
units.tr: Gratian argues at length that concubinage alone does not stand in the way of promotion to the diaconate; for by a dispensation he softens the rigour of the law, saying as follows.

units.la: Gratianus. CAETERVM. Si non talis Concubina fuerit, & aetas illius de quo agitur, futurae incontinentiae suspicionem auferre dignoscitur: Apostolica concessione ad ordinem Diaconatus provehi potest. Unde Pelagius Papa scribit Florentino Episcopo. De Pelagiis dixi mus. 28. distinct. can. De Syracusanae.
units.tr: Gratian. MOREOVER. If the concubine is not of such a kind, and the age of the man in question is known to remove any suspicion of future incontinence, he may be advanced to the order of the diaconate by apostolic concession. Hence Pope Pelagius writes to the bishop of Florence. We have spoken of Pelagius under dist. 28, the canon "De Syracusanae."

units.la: Qui post vxoris suae mortem, non abstinuerit amica sive concubina, nec Diaconus quidem fieri potest, absque Papae gratia.
units.tr: One who, after the death of his wife, does not abstain from a female friend or a concubine cannot even be made a deacon without the favour of the Pope.

units.la: FRaternitatis tuae relatione suscepta, eius latorem secundas quidem nuptias expertum non fuisse didicimus: castitatem tamen cum priori non servasse coniugio designasti. Et quamvis multa sint, quae in huiusmodi casibus observari, Canonicae iubeat sublimitatis authoritas: tamen quia defectus nostri temporis, quibus non solum merita, sed corpora ipsa hominum defecerunt, districtionis illius non patitur manere censuram: & aetas illius de quo agitur, futurae incontinentiae suspicionem auferre dignoscitur: ut ad Diaconatus Ordinem possit provehi, concessisse nos noveris. Micenam vero ancillam eius, de qua se, post uxoris transitum, filios habere confessus est, iubemus ut tua dispositione, cuiquam monasterio continentia prosessura tradatur. Gratianus. HOC Ex dispensatione misericordiae. Caeterum, Ex rigore disciplinae intelligitur illud Aurelianensis Concilii: Iuxta fere temporibus, Aurelios convenere Galli Patres, & Hispanici Gerundam (Girona. vulgò) Coss. Anatolio, & Agapito, scilicet, Anno 510. Quare mihi verisimile est Gratianum retulisse ad Aurelianense Concilium, quod fuit in Gerundensi decretum, cap. 8. ut sequitur.
units.tr: Having received the account of your brotherhood, we have learned that its bearer had not experienced a second marriage, but you have indicated that he had not kept chastity with his first marriage. And although there are many things which the authority of the canonical loftiness orders to be observed in cases of this kind, yet because of the defects of our time, in which not only merits but the very bodies of men have failed, the severity of that discipline does not allow its judgment to remain; and since the age of the man in question is known to remove any suspicion of future incontinence, you should know that we have granted that he may be advanced to the order of the diaconate. But as for the maidservant Micena, of whom he confessed that he had sons after the death of his wife, we order that by your disposition she be handed over to some monastery, there to make profession of continence. Gratian. THIS is from the dispensation of mercy. But from the rigour of discipline is understood that canon of the Council of Orléans. In about the same period, Gallic fathers and Spanish ones met at Orléans, and at Gerona (commonly Girona), in the consulship of Anatolius and Agapitus, that is, in the year 510. Hence it seems likely to me that Gratian referred to the Council of Orléans what was decreed at the Council of Gerona, canon 8, as follows.

units.la: Non admittatur ad Clerum, qui praeter uxorem cognoverit aliam.
units.tr: No one who has known a woman other than his wife should be admitted to the clergy.

units.la: SI quis de Laicis, post uxorem suam, aliam cuiuscunque conditionis cognoverit mulierem, in Clerum nullatenus admittatur. QVOD ergo de Pellice & Meretrice apud Gregorium & Innocentium scribitur, Propter spem futurae incontinentiae constitutum esse creditur: quia difficile continentiam servat, qui se illicito concubitu maculare non metuit. Vel, Prohibetur ordinari, qui pellicem, vel meretricem cognoverit maritali affectu, vel quia corrupta florem virginitatis amisit, vel quia meretricari non definit, licet in uxorem ducatur: Utrumque enim cuilibet impedimentum praestat, quo minus ad Sacros Ordines pertingere valeat. Unde. Hilarius Papa scribit, dicens. In Synodo Romana, quam habuit Fl. Basilico, & Hermineriche Coss. hoc est, Anno Christi 467. est in cap. 1. Synodi. To. 1. Concil.
units.tr: If anyone from the laity, after his wife, has known another woman of any condition, he is by no means to be admitted into the clergy. As for what is written about the concubine and the harlot in Gregory and Innocent, it is believed to have been laid down because of the expectation of future incontinence: he who does not fear to defile himself with illicit intercourse hardly keeps continence. Or: he is forbidden to be ordained who has known a concubine or a harlot with marital affection, either because she has lost the flower of virginity through corruption, or because he has not ceased to whore, even though he takes her as a wife. Each of these presents an impediment to anyone, so that he cannot attain to the holy orders. Hence Pope Hilary writes, saying: In the Roman Synod which he held in the consulship of Flavius Basilicus and Herminericus, that is, in the year of Christ 467. It is in chapter 1 of the Synod, Tom. 1 of the Councils.

units.la: Qui virginem non duxit uxorem, ad Sacros Ordines non accedat.
units.tr: He who has not taken a virgin as his wife should not approach the holy orders.

units.la: CAuendum † ergo in primis est, Ne ad Sacros Ordines (sicut gestis prioribus ante scriptum est) quisquam, qui uxorem non duxit virginem, aspiret. Item. Gregorius urbis Romanae praesul Squilatino Episcopo lib. secundo Epistol. 25.
units.tr: Care must therefore be taken above all that no one who has not married a virgin as his wife aspires to the holy orders, as was written earlier in the former acts. Likewise Gregory, bishop of the city of Rome, to Bishop Squilatinus, book 2 of the Letters, letter 25.

units.la: Digamus, vel Poenitens, Corpore vitiatus, Literas ignorans, Curiae vel conditioni obnoxius, non fiat Clericus.
units.tr: A bigamist, a penitent, one bodily damaged, one ignorant of letters, one bound to the court or to some condition, let him not become a cleric.

units.la: PRaecipimus, Ne unquam illicitas ordinationes facias: Nec digamum, Aut qui virginem non est sortitus uxorem, Aut ignorantem literas, Vel qualibet parte corporis vitiatum, Vel poenitentiae, Vel curiae, aut cuilibet conditioni obnoxium, ad Sacros Ordines permittas accedere: sed si quos huiusmodi repereris, non audeas promovere. Item. In Neocaesariensi Concilio. cap. 8. Est Neocaesarea in Cappadocia. Licinio, Constantini collega, faciente adhuc per Orientem, Synodus haec habita fuit annis aliquot ante Nicaenam. Supra diximus. dist. 28.
units.tr: We direct that you never make illicit ordinations. Do not permit to approach the holy orders a bigamist, or one who has not obtained a virgin as wife, or one ignorant of letters, or one injured in any part of the body, or one subject to penance, or to the court, or bound to any condition. But if you find any such persons, do not dare to promote them. Likewise in the Council of Neocaesarea, chapter 8. Neocaesarea is in Cappadocia. Licinius, colleague of Constantine, still ruling in the East, this synod was held some years before Nicaea. We said above, dist. 28.

units.la: Non fiat Sacerdos, cuius uxorem constat euidenter adulterium admisisse.
units.tr: No one whose wife is clearly known to have committed adultery should become a priest.

units.la: S I cuius uxorem adulterium commisisse, quum esset Laicus, euidenter fuerit probatum, †hic ad ministerium Ecclesiasticum admitti non potest. Quòd si † in Clericatu eo iam constituto, adulterauit, † dato repudio dimittere eam debet. Si uero † retinere eius consortium uelit, non potest † suscepto ministerio perfrui. Item. Ex Concilio Martini Papae cap.28. Vide superius dist. 27.
units.tr: If the wife of anyone has been clearly proved to have committed adultery while he was a layman, he cannot be admitted here to ecclesiastical ministry. But if, after he has already been established in the clergy, she commits adultery, he ought to dismiss her by giving a bill of divorce. But if he wishes to retain her company, he cannot enjoy the ministry he has received. Likewise from the Council of Pope Martin, chapter 28. See above, dist. 27.

units.la: S I Laici uxor in adulterio fuerit deprehensa, hic talis ad ministerium Ecclesiasticum nullo modo adducatur. Si autem post ordinationem, alicuius Clerici uxor adulterata fuerit, dimittat eam. Si autem cum ipsa voluerit permanere, à ministerio existat alienus. Gratianus.
units.tr: If a layman's wife has been caught in adultery, such a man is in no way to be brought to ecclesiastical ministry. But if, after ordination, the wife of any cleric has committed adultery, let him put her away. If he wishes to remain with her, let him be excluded from the ministry. Gratian.

units.la: PRAEMISSIS authoritatibus, Digami, Et qui virgines non sunt fortiti uxores, à Sacris Ordinibus prohibentur. Sed quaeritur, Si quis ante baptismum viduam duxerit uxorem, an postea sit prohibendus à Sacris Ordinibus? De his ita scribit Innocentius Papa primus, Victricio Rothomagensi Episcopo. Epist. 2. cap. 5. & 6. annum superius annotauimus. dist. 31. can. Tenere.
units.tr: With these authorities set out, bigamists and those who have not taken virgins as wives are forbidden the holy orders. But it is asked: if someone before baptism took a widow as his wife, is he afterwards to be forbidden the holy orders? On this Pope Innocent I writes thus to Victricius, Bishop of Rouen, Epist. 2, chapters 5 and 6. We noted the year above, dist. 31, can. Tenere.

units.la: Vidua maritus nunquam debet Ordinari.
units.tr: A man who has married a widow must never be ordained.

units.la: S I quis uiduam (licet Laicus) duxerit uxorem, seu ante Baptismum, seu post Baptismum, non admittatur ad clerum: quia eodem vitio videtur exclusus. In Baptismate enim crimina dimittuntur, non accepta uxoris consortium relaxatur. Quòd si non putatur uxor esse computanda, quae ante Baptismum ducta est: ergo nec filij, qui ante Baptismum geniti sunt, pro filiis habeantur.
units.tr: If anyone has taken a widow as his wife (even though he is a layman), whether before baptism or after baptism, let him not be admitted to the clergy, since he seems to be excluded by the same defect. For in baptism crimes are forgiven, but the partnership of a wife taken is not released. But if the wife taken before baptism is not thought to be counted as a wife, then neither should the children born before baptism be regarded as children.

units.la: Gratianus. PROHIBENTUR etiam Digami, à quolibet Ordine Clericatus: iuxta illud Ambrosij ad Vercellenses. Epist. 82. lib. 10. Epist. To. 3.
units.tr: Gratian. Bigamists are also forbidden every order of the clergy, according to that saying of Ambrose to the Vercellenses, Epist. 82, book 10, Epist. Tom. 3.

units.la: Qui secunda coniugia sortitur, Clericus non fiat.
units.tr: He who has contracted second marriages should not become a cleric.

units.la: C Ognoscamus non solùm de Episcopo, & Presbytero, Apostolum statuisse: sed etiam Patres in Concilij Niceni tractatu addidisse. Clericum quemquam non debere esse, qui secunda coniugia sit sortitus. SIMILITER etiam Viduarum mariti, vel Ancillarum, vel Meretricū, Clerici fieri non possunt. Vnde in Canonibus Apostolorum legitur. Can 18.
units.tr: We should recognize that the Apostle laid this down not only concerning bishop and presbyter, but also that the Fathers, in the treatise of the Council of Nicaea, added that no one who has contracted second marriages should be a cleric. Likewise, husbands of widows, or of maidservants, or of harlots, cannot become clerics. Hence it is read in the Canons of the Apostles, canon 18.

units.la: Saltatricem, vel Viduam, vel Eiectam, vel Ancillam, vel Impudicam ducens vxorem, non debet ordinari.
units.tr: One who takes as wife a dancer, a widow, a divorced woman, a maidservant, or an unchaste woman, ought not to be ordained.

units.la: SI quis Viduam, vel Eiectam acceperit, aut Meretricem, aut Ancillam, vel aliquam de his quae publicis mancipantur spectaculis: non poterit esse Episcopus, aut Presbyter, aut Diaconus, aut ex numero eorum, qui ministerio Sacro deseruiunt. QVAE autem sit Vidua, quae Eiecta, vel Meretrix, Hieronymus ad Fabiolam. De veste Sacerdotali ostendit, dicens. To.3.
units.tr: If anyone has taken a widow, or a divorced woman, or a harlot, or a maidservant, or any of those who are given over to public spectacles, he cannot be a bishop, or a presbyter, or a deacon, or of the number of those who serve the sacred ministry. What a widow is, and what a divorced woman or harlot is, Jerome shows in his letter to Fabiola, On priestly dress, saying, Tom. 3.

units.la: VIdua est, cuius maritus mortuus est. Eiecta est, quae a marito viuente eiicitur. Meretrix, quae multorum libidini patet. SED postea, temporum defectui condescendens Papa Martinus, in minoribus Ordinibus eos constitui permisit, non tamen regulam praefigendo, Dicens.cap.44.
units.tr: A widow is one whose husband has died. A divorced woman is one who is cast out by her husband while he is living. A harlot is one who lies open to the lust of many. But afterwards Pope Martin, condescending to the defect of the times, permitted such men to be established in the minor orders, without however laying down a fixed rule, saying, chapter 44.

units.la: Regradatur Hypodiaconus nuptias secundas iniens, Ergo non vbique Matrimonii abstinebant Hypodiaconi.
units.tr: A subdeacon who enters a second marriage is demoted: therefore subdeacons did not everywhere abstain from marriage.

units.la: SI Subdiaconus secundam vxorem duxerit, inter Lectores, vel Ostiarios habeatur: ita vt Apostolum non legat. NECESSITATE tamen exigente, Digamus vsque ad Subdiaconatum poterit promoveri.
units.tr: If a subdeacon takes a second wife, he is to be counted among the readers or doorkeepers, so that he does not read the Apostle. Yet if necessity requires it, a bigamist may be promoted up to the subdiaconate.

units.la: Vnde Martinus Papa ait. cap.43. Ex hac pseudepigraphe, quae Canones istos adscribit Martino Papae, nascitur erroris plena quaestio. Nunquid Papa cum Digamis dispensare poterit? De Martino superius annotata vide in can.1.dist.27.can.Si qua vidua 28. dist.
units.tr: Hence Pope Martin says, chapter 43. From this pseudepigraph, which ascribes these canons to Pope Martin, arises a question full of error: can the Pope dispense with bigamists? For what has been noted above about Martin, see on can. 1, dist. 27, and can. Si qua vidua, dist. 28.

units.la: LEctor, si viduam alterius vxorem acceperit, in Lectoratu permaneat: Aut si necessitas fuerit, Subdiaconus fiat: nihil autem supra. Similiter si Digamus fuerit. QVIBVS autem propria coniugia prohibentur, interdicitur etiam nuptialibus conuiuiis interesse. Vnde. In Agathensi Concilio, cap.39.legitur.
units.tr: A reader who takes as wife the widow of another should remain in the reader's office; or, if necessity arises, he may become a subdeacon, but nothing higher. Likewise if he is a bigamist. Moreover, those who are forbidden their own marriages are also forbidden to attend wedding feasts. Hence it is read in the Council of Agde, chapter 39.

units.la: Lasciuiis
units.tr: Wantonness

units.la: Lasciniis nuptialibus, locisve theatralibus suos nec oculos, nec aures prophanare debent Sacri Domini Dei nostri Iesu Sacerdotes.
units.tr: Priests of our Lord God Jesus Christ ought not to profane their eyes or ears with wanton wedding songs or theatrical places.

units.la: PResbyteri, Diaconi, Subdiaconi, vel deinceps, quibus ducendi uxores licentia modo non est, etiam aliarum nuptiarum euitent conuiuia: nec his coetibus misceantur, vbi amatoria cantantur, & turpia, aut obscoeni motus corporum choreis & saltationibus efferuntur: ne auditus & obtutus Sacris mysteriis deputati, turpium spectaculorum atque verborum contagione polluantur. Digna scitu quaestio definitur hic. Quòd, Non omnis illa mulier est vidua, cuius vir obierit. Gratianus. VIDVA vero est intelligenda, Si post solenne foedus nuptiarum, morte interueniente, à viro suo diuisa fuerit. Caeterum, si antequam conueniant, fatali necessitate ab alterutro diuisi fuerint: licet ex sponsalibus Vxor sit appellata, non tamen post mortem sponsi, etiamsi in propria sit ducta, & etiam cum eo velata, Vidua appellatur: nec ex eius copula à Sacris Ordinibus aliquis prohibetur. Vnde Pelagius Papa scribit:
units.tr: Presbyters, deacons, subdeacons, and those after them, to whom the licence to take wives is no longer given, should also avoid the feasts of other weddings. Nor are they to mix in those gatherings where love songs and shameful ones are sung, or where obscene movements of the body are performed in dances and leaping, lest the hearing and sight, assigned to the sacred mysteries, be polluted by the contagion of shameful spectacles and words. A question worth knowing is settled here: not every woman whose husband has died is a widow. Gratian. But a widow is to be understood as one who, after the solemn covenant of marriage, has been separated from her husband by death intervening. But if, before they came together, they were separated by fatal necessity from one or the other, then although she is called a wife from the betrothal, yet after the death of the betrothed she is not called a widow, even if she was taken into his own house and veiled with him; and no one is prohibited from holy orders on account of that union. Hence Pope Pelagius writes:

units.la: Concubitus, non consensus facit Digamiam.
units.tr: Intercourse, not consent, makes bigamy.

units.la: VAlentino Clerico, cui mulier cum alio ante velata, non tamen illi nupta, sed virgo permanens, post mortem eius, cum quo velata fuerat sponsa, coniugali est copulâ sociata: quia iterum velamen accepit, nullum in promouendo generatur obstaculum: quia nihil est (quantum ad hunc articulum pertinet) quod ei de Canonicis obuiet institutis. Hactenus Gratianus de Sacerdotum coniugio. Exponens illud Apostoli. Oportet Episcopum esse vnius vxoris virum. Sequitur, & Sobrium. de quo in dist. sequenti.
units.tr: To Valentinus, a cleric, whose betrothed had earlier been veiled with another man, but had not been married to him, and remained a virgin: after the death of the man with whom she had been veiled, she was joined in conjugal union with him. Because she received the veil again, no obstacle arises to his promotion, since there is nothing (as far as this point is concerned) that stands in the way of the canonical institutions. Thus far Gratian, on the marriage of priests, expounding that saying of the Apostle: A bishop must be the husband of one wife. There follows: and sober, which is treated in the following distinction.

units.la: DISTINCTIO XXXV.
units.tr: DISTINCTIO XXXV.

units.la: Tertium, quod visitur in Speculo.
units.tr: The third thing seen in the Mirror.

units.la: ΔΕῖ ΤΌΝ ΠΡΕΣΒΎΤΕΡΟΝ ΕΊΝΑΙ ΝΗΦΆΛΙΟΝ.
units.tr: THE ELDER MUST BE SOBER [ΔΕῖ ΤΌΝ ΠΡΕΣΒΎΤΕΡΟΝ ΕΊΝΑΙ ΝΗΦΆΛΙΟΝ].

units.la: Sobrij sint, & Vigilantes Ecclesiastici. Chrysostomus περὶ ἱερωσύνης, Haec duo iunxit idem notantia. Νηφάλιον εἰ αι δὲ τοῦ ἱερέα, καὶ διορατικόν. Νηφάλιος quippe vtrumque significat, & Abstemium, & Vigilantem. Sermo de omnibus est. Gratianus A QVIBVS Ordinibus Digami prohibeantur: & vtrum reputentur Digami, qui ante Baptismum habuerunt vnam, & post Baptismū habuerunt alteram: & an constitutis in Sacris Ordinibus liceat vxores sortiri, multorum authoritatibus breuiter monstratum est. Sequitur autem in descriptione illa Apostolica: Vt sit sobrius, qui Ordinandus est, non vinolentus: quod ex authoritate veteris testamenti introductum est: Ministri enim templi prohibentur vinum, & siceram bibere, Ne ebrietate grauetur corda eorum, vt sensus eorum vigeat semper, & tenuis sit: vel, Qui i venter mero aestuans facile despumat in libidinem. Vnde Noe in ebrietate nudauit foemora. Loth autem, quem Sodoma non vicit, vina vicerunt. Quòd autem Vinolentus esse prohibetur: non semel, sed frequenter vino repletus debet intelligi. Hinc etiam in Canonibus Apostolorum legitur, Cano. 41. & 43.
units.tr: "Let the ecclesiastics be sober and watchful." Chrysostom, in his book On the Priesthood: "He has joined these two words, which signify the same thing: [the priest must be sober and discerning] [νηφάλιον εἶναι δὲ τὸν ἱερέα, καὶ διορατικόν]. For nephalios means both abstinent and watchful. The discourse concerns everyone." Gratian, on which orders digamists are forbidden, whether those are counted as digamists who had one wife before baptism and another after baptism, and whether those in holy orders may take wives, has been briefly shown by the authority of many. Next, in that Apostolic description: "He must be sober, who is to be ordained, not given to wine," which was introduced on the authority of the Old Testament. For the ministers of the temple are forbidden to drink wine and strong drink, "lest their hearts be weighed down with drunkenness, so that their senses may always be alert and clear"; or, "the belly that boils with wine readily foams over into lust." Hence Noah in drunkenness uncovered his thighs; but Lot, whom Sodom did not conquer, was conquered by wine. Moreover, that a man is forbidden to be given to wine should be understood not as once, but as being filled with wine frequently. Hence it is also read in the Canons of the Apostles, Canons 41 and 43.

units.la: Ebriosus, aut Alcator Episcopus, aut Presbyter, aut Diaconus, gradu suo mouetur, ni desistat. Reliqui excommunicantur.
units.tr: A bishop, presbyter or deacon who is a drunkard or a gambler is deposed from his rank unless he gives it up. The rest are excommunicated.

units.la: E Piscopus, aut Presbyter, aut Diaconus, aleae vel ebrietati deseruiens, aut desinat, † aut certè damnetur. Subdiaconus, aut Lector, aut Cantor similia faciès: aut desinat, aut communione priuetur. Similiter & Laicus. Item. Hieronymus, lib. 1. contra Iouinianum.
units.tr: If a bishop, presbyter or deacon serves dice or drunkenness, let him either give it up or else be condemned. A subdeacon, reader or cantor who does similar things must either give it up or be deprived of communion. Likewise also a layman. Likewise Jerome, book 1 against Jovinian.

units.la: Esus carnium, Vinique potus post diluuium concessus, post Christum derelictus.
units.tr: Eating meat and drinking wine, permitted after the flood, forsaken after Christ.

units.la: A B exordio conditionis humanę, nec carnibus vescebamur, nec dabamus repudium, nec praeputia nobis eripiebantur in signum. Hoc cursu vsque ad diluuium perucnimus. Post diluuium autem cum datione legis, quam implere nullus potuit, carnes ingestæ sunt ad vescendum: & repudia concessa duritiæ: & cultellus circuncisionis appositus: quasi, Dei manus plus in nobis creauerit, quàm necesse est. Postquàm autem Christus venit in fine temporum, & ω, reuoluit ad ʌ: & ꝯ, extremitatem retraxit ad principium: nec repudium nobis dare permittitur, nec circuncidimur, nec comedimus carnes, dicente Apostolo: Bonum est vinum non bibere, & carnes non comedere: Vinum enim cum carnibus post diluuium dedicatum est. Idem. Aduersus eundem Iouinianum lib. 1. ex cap. 10. Proverb.
units.tr: From the beginning of the human condition we neither ate flesh, nor gave a bill of divorce, nor were foreskins taken from us as a sign. We ran this course down to the flood. But after the flood, together with the giving of the law, which no one could fulfil, flesh was thrust upon us for food, divorce was permitted because of hardness of heart, and the knife of circumcision was applied, as if the hand of God had created more in us than was necessary. But after Christ came at the end of the times, and omega has turned back to alpha, and the extremity has drawn back to the beginning, it is no longer permitted to us to give a bill of divorce, nor are we circumcised, nor do we eat flesh, the Apostle saying: "It is good not to drink wine, nor to eat flesh"; for wine was consecrated together with flesh after the flood. The same, against the same Jovinian, book 1, from chapter 10. Proverbs.

units.la: Alienum est à Sapiente, potationibus & ebrietatibus vacare.
units.tr: It is foreign to a wise man to devote himself to drinking parties and drunkenness.

units.la: Luxuriosa res est Vinum, & contumeliosa Ebrietas: omnis qui cum his miscetur, non erit Sapiens.
units.tr: Wine is a riotous thing and drunkenness an insolent one; whoever is mixed up with these will not be wise.

units.la: Hic erat adponendum, quod statim sequitur in Hieronymo, congruuntque proposito.
units.tr: This should be placed here, what immediately follows in Jerome, and it agrees with our purpose.

units.la: Ne tales accipiamus cibos, quos, aut difficulter digerere, aut comesos, magno partos & perditos labore doleamus. Idem. To. 6. Michaeae Prophetiam explicans ita vaticinantis cap. 2. Duces populi mei proiicientur de domibus deliciarum suarum. Propter malas adinuentiones suas eiecti sunt.
units.tr: Let us not take such foods as we grieve to digest with difficulty, or, once eaten, to have gained and lost with great toil. The same. In volume 6, explaining the prophecy of Micah, who prophesies thus in chapter 2: "The leaders of my people will be cast out of the houses of their delights. They were cast out on account of their wicked inventions."

units.la: Ignominiosum est Sacerdoti affluere deliciis, epulis, atque lasciuiis.
units.tr: It is shameful for a priest to abound in luxuries, feasts and wantonness.

units.la: Ecclesiae principes, qui deliciis affluunt, & inter epulas atque lasciuias, pudicitiâ seruare se credunt, Propheticus sermo describit: Quòd eiiciendi sunt de spatiosis domibus, lautisque conuiuiis, & multo labore epulis conquisitis. Et si vis scire, quò eiiciendi sunt propter malas cogitationes; & opera sua. Euangelium lege: In tenebras, scilicet, exteriores, vbi erit fletus & stridor dentium. An non cófusio & ignominia est, Iesum crucifixum, magistrum, pauperem & esurientem, sacris prædicare corporibus? Et ieiuniorum doctrinam, rubentes buccas, tumentiáque ora proferre? Si in Apostolorum loco sumus, non solum sermonem eorum imitemur, sed etiam conuersationem & abstinentiam. Deduit huc ex Hieronymo totus ille transcribi locus, Aposcopos eui nostri graphicè describens. Vltima dutaxat adiiciam verba. Christi Sacerdotes, qui pudore & verecundiâ non tenentur, Agant pœnitentiam saltem comminatione pœnarum. Idem, Paulo ante finem Epistolæ ad Oceanum.
units.tr: The prophetic word describes the leaders of the Church, who abound in luxuries and believe that they keep themselves chaste amid feasts and wantonness: that they must be cast out of their spacious houses and elegant banquets, and of the feasts procured with much labour. And if you wish to know where they must be cast out on account of their evil thoughts and their works, read the Gospel: into the outer darkness, namely, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Is it not confusion and shame to preach Jesus crucified, the teacher, poor and hungry, with sacred bodies? And to put forward the doctrine of fasts with reddened cheeks and swollen mouths? If we stand in the place of the Apostles, we should imitate not only their word but also their manner of life and abstinence. Here the whole passage from Jerome, which vividly describes the bishops of our time, ought to be copied out. I will add only the final words. The priests of Christ, who are not restrained by shame and modesty, should at least do penance through the threat of punishments. The same, shortly before the end of the letter to Oceanus.

units.la: Vbi ebrietas, ibi libido, atque furor, ac mors tandem dominatur.
